news.summary_en: AI developer Anthropic PBC saw its shares decline by approximately 5% in post-market trading following a record-breaking $107.3 billion IPO. The stock had previously gained 17% during its debut, reflecting strong investor appetite for the maker of Claude, though broader market volatility eventually weighed on its performance.
news.lead_paragraph: Anthropic PBC shares were down about 5% in post-market trading as the artificial intelligence developer wrapped up its first day as a public company after a record-setting $107.3 billion offering.
news.lead_paragraph_zh: Anthropic PBC 的股价在盘后交易中下跌约 5%，这家人工智能开发商在创纪录的 1073 亿美元发行后结束了上市首日交易。
paragraphs: Anthropic PBC shares were down about 5% in post-market trading as the artificial intelligence developer wrapped up its first day as a public company after a record-setting $107.3 billion offering.

The late moves pared a debut pop of 17% on Thursday, which provided a rare bright spot as the Nasdaq fell 2.2%. The broader market continued on a downward trend into the Asian day, with global stocks poised for their longest losing streak in more than three years, as the AI trade cratered.

While the bright open for the Claude chatbot maker reflected massive investor appetite after a heavily oversubscribed initial public offering, the late slide underscored the volatility facing tech megacaps amidst shifting expectations for enterprise software monetization and high capital expenditure.

Anthropic priced its offering at $83 a share, above an already elevated target range, raising more than $8.1 billion in new proceeds. Backed by major technology giants including Amazon.com Inc. and Alphabet Inc., the company has emerged alongside OpenAI as a linchpin of generative AI infrastructure.

Trading in Anthropic's shares drew intense scrutiny across Wall Street as analysts evaluated whether monumental frontier model development and GPU computing costs can yield sustained profitability. The IPO represents the largest venture-backed tech listing in history, surpassing previous records set by high-profile cloud and social media debuts.
paragraphs_zh: Anthropic PBC 的股价在盘后交易中下跌约 5%，这家人工智能开发商在创纪录的 1073 亿美元发行后结束了上市首日交易。
周四的尾盘走势回吐了 17% 的首日涨幅，为纳斯达克指数下跌 2.2% 提供了难得的亮点。随着人工智能交易的暴跌，大盘继续呈下跌趋势，进入亚洲交易日，全球股市将出现三年多以来最长的连续下跌。
虽然 Claude 聊天机器人开发商在开盘时的强劲表现反映了经历严重超额认购后投资者的巨大热情，但尾盘的回落凸显了大型科技企业面临的市场波动——在企业级软件商业化变现与庞大资本开支周期的交织下，市场情绪正经历剧烈博弈。
Anthropic 将 IPO 发行价定为每股 83 美元，高于此前已上调的指导区间上限，单笔募资超 81 亿美元。在亚马逊（Amazon.com Inc.）与 Alphabet Inc. 等科技巨头的巨额注资背书下，Anthropic 已与 OpenAI 并列成为全球生成式 AI 基础设施的核心支柱。
Anthropic 的挂牌交易引发了华尔街投行的全方位审视，分析师聚焦于前沿大模型研发与 GPU 算力集群的庞大资本开支能否转化为可持续的盈利能力。此次上市创下了全球风险投资支持科技企业史上规模最大的 IPO 纪录，打破了此前所有云计算与移动互联网巨头保持的公开发行市值高度。

news.title: Commerce approved sales of more than 879,000 AI chips to Chinese companies, Rep. Mast says
news.title_en: Commerce approved sales of more than 879,000 AI chips to Chinese companies, Rep. Mast says
news.author: Justin Papp and Katie Tarasov
news.article_content:
The subagency of the Commerce Department that regulates and enforces exports approved the sale of more than 879,000 AI chips to Chinese companies including Alibaba and Tencent as of May 2026, according to documents released Thursday by the House Foreign Affairs Committee.

Some of those approvals, made by Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security, included sales to companies designated by the Department of Defense as "Chinese Military Companies,"according to the documents. From December through May, companies had made 3.4 million requests for sales of U.S. AI chips to China, the committee reported, citing those made by Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices.

"Over the past month, the administration's handling of chip export controls has put our national security and technology edge at risk. The Bureau of Industry and Security has failed to enforce the rules, and Congress must now conduct rigorous oversight of the administration's policies,"Rep. Gregory Meeks, D-N.Y., the top Democrat on the House Foreign Affairs Committee, said at a meeting of the panel Thursday at which members voted to release the documents.

Spokespersons for Nvidia and AMD said their companies comply with U.S. export control laws.

Nvidia argued it was following the Commerce Department regulations that were in effect at the time.

A spokesperson from the Bureau of Industry and Security said it shared information with Congress on both approvals and denials of licenses for Nvidia's H200 and comparable chips. "Licensing decisions are the product of deliberation and consultation among multiple U.S. Government agencies,"the spokesperson said.

"The review and licensing process spanned more than half a year, with approvals subject to strict conditions and limited volumes. Despite receiving some licenses, we have since stopped shipping H200s to China,"Nvidia spokesperson John Rizzo told CNBC.

On Tuesday, Nvidia reported $2.4 billion in quarterly revenue from H200 and related chip sales in China. In total, customers based in China and Hong Kong made up about 9.5% of all revenue.

"AMD complies with applicable U.S. export control laws and regulations and maintains rigorous processes to ensure compliance across our global operations,"AMD said through a spokesperson.

The approval of 879,000 AI chips is "not that many,"Bernstein Senior Analyst Stacy Rasgon told CNBC, adding that this news is not surprising.

"It doesn't sound to me like they're approving everything they got willy nilly,"Rasgon said of the Commerce Department. With 879,000 approvals out of 3.4 million requested AI chip sales, he added, "There was a process in place, and it sounds like they approved about one out of every four."

Despite a rapid succession of China export controls on AI chips that started under the Biden administration in 2022, Nvidia and AMD both re-engineered some chips to comply and be sold legally in China. And in December, Trump said Nvidia could ship H200s, its older generation Hopper chips, to "approved customers in China"if the U.S. got a 25% cut of sales.

The U.S. then licensed Nvidia H200 sales to Alibaba, Tencent, ByteDance and other Chinese companies, although sales were limited because Beijing didn't approve large-scale imports, chip analyst Patrick Moorhead of Moor Insights & Strategy told CNBC last week.

H200 sales numbers remained low due to those restrictions on China's end. Nvidia said H200 shipments to China made up less than 1% of data center revenue for the quarter that ended in July.

"In the grand context of the size of this market and how much they're shipping, it's a rounding error. It's tiny,"Rasgon told CNBC.

The committee cited the Export Control Reform Act as justification for releasing the data. The panel said the law allows it to declassify and release export data if it "determines that the withholding of the following information is contrary to the national interest."

The license requests released by the Foreign Affairs Committee include requests to sell to major firms including ByteDance, Tesla (Shanghai) and Baidu.

The release of documents comes in the wake of Jensen Huang 's resignation from the chip supplier Nvidia after news surfaced that he had several extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy that led to concerns about Nvidia chips being diverted to China.

In the weeks since, Republicans and Democrats in Congress have called for legislation to be passed that would impose stricter export controls on the sale of advanced AI chips to China and other adversaries.

"The license information we are disclosing today will help inform the American public about how BIS has handled licenses for Nvidia H200 and equivalent AMD chips to China. The public has the right to know how these decisions were made,"Meeks said.

Mast said two of the firms listed in Nvidia license applications to BIS — Maginfra and New Matrix — are suspected "smuggling fronts."The New York Times reported in November that both companies had empty offices and had ties to companies under national security sanctions.

"Both are fake companies. If BIS approved the sale of these chips to these firms, obviously that is of tremendous concern to us — especially given that President Trump made clear last year that the sale of any AI chips to China will have very real national security conditions,"Mast said at the Thursday meeting.

Maginfra and New Matrix did not reply to requests for comment.

Shares of AMD fell Thursday after the investment firm Hunterbrook Media issued a report alleging the company "has its own China problem."The report claims that "after the U.S. blacklisted Chinese server maker IEIT Systems, the company kept getting newer AMD firmware, which enables AMD chips to run in servers."

CNBC did not independently verify this information.

Fallout from the Huang scandal on Capitol Hill has intensified in the last week, as lawmakers question the degree to which the former head of Nvidia's relationship with the suspected Chinese spy could have jeopardized national security and American AI dominance.

Huang is due for a closed-door transcribed interview with the House Foreign Affairs panel and two other committees on Dec. 1. Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter is scheduled to appear before the panels Dec. 2.

Senate banking committee Chair Tim Scott, R-S.C., announced on CNBC's "Squawk Box"on Wednesday that Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick had also agreed to testify.

Lutnick has come under fire over his relationship to Huang and for his failure to take action on Megaspeed, the Singaporean company where Alice Huang, with whom the former Nvidia CEO had an affair, was an executive until 2025. U.S. investigators suspect Megaspeed diverted Nvidia chips to China.

Amid that criticism, the Commerce Department on Monday issued an interim final rule to close a loophole that has allowed Chinese companies to lease Nvidia's advancing computing power from data centers in third countries.

The rule was "written by and at the direction of"the Treasury Department and the White House National Security Council, BIS said in a press release.

— Megan Cassella, Daren Fonda and Kif Leswing contributed to this report.

news.article_content_zh:
根据众议院外交事务委员会周四发布的文件，截至 2026 年 5 月，商务部负责监管和执行出口的下属机构已批准向阿里巴巴和腾讯等中国公司出售超过 879,000 颗人工智能芯片。

文件显示，其中一些由商务部工业和安全局批准的批准包括向国防部指定为“中国军工公司”的公司进行销售。该委员会援引 Nvidia 和 Advanced Micro Devices 的数据称，从 12 月到 5 月，各公司已发出 340 万份向中国销售美国人工智能芯片的请求。

“过去一个月，政府对芯片出口管制的处理使我们的国家安全和技术优势面临风险。工业和安全局未能执行这些规则，国会现在必须对政府的政策进行严格监督，”众议员。众议院外交事务委员会民主党领袖、纽约州民主党人格雷戈里·米克斯周四在该委员会的一次会议上表示，会上成员们投票决定公布这些文件。

英伟达和 AMD 的发言人表示，他们的公司遵守美国出口管制法。

英伟达辩称，它正在遵守当时有效的商务部法规。

美国工业与安全局的一位发言人表示，该局与国会分享了有关批准和拒绝 Nvidia H200 及类似芯片许可的信息。该发言人表示：“许可决定是多个美国政府机构审议和协商的结果。”

Nvidia 发言人约翰·里佐 (John Rizzo) 向 CNBC 表示：“审查和许可过程持续了半年多的时间，批准受到严格的条件和数量的限制。尽管获得了一些许可，但我们已停止向中国运送 H200。”

周二，英伟达公布 H200 及相关芯片在中国的季度收入为 24 亿美元。总的来说，中国大陆和香港的客户约占总收入的 9.5%。

AMD 通过发言人表示：“AMD 遵守适用的美国出口管制法律和法规，并维持严格的流程，以确保我们全球业务的合规性。”

Bernstein 高级分析师 Stacy Rasgon 告诉 CNBC，批准的 879,000 个 AI 芯片“并不多”，并补充说这一消息并不令人意外。

“在我看来，他们并不是随意批准他们得到的一切，”拉斯贡谈到商务部时说道。他补充说，在 340 万份 AI 芯片销售请求中，有 879,000 份获得批准，“有一个流程，听起来他们批准了大约四分之一。”

尽管中国自 2022 年拜登政府开始对人工智能芯片实施一系列快速出口管制，但英伟达和 AMD 都重新设计了一些芯片，以符合要求并在中国合法销售。去年 12 月，特朗普表示，如果美国的销售额减少 25%，Nvidia 可以将其老一代 Hopper 芯片 H200 运送给“中国认可的客户”。

Moor Insights & Strategy 芯片分析师帕特里克·穆尔海德 (Patrick Moorhead) 上周向 CNBC 表示，美国随后向阿里巴巴、腾讯、字节跳动和其他中国公司授予了 Nvidia H200 销售许可，但由于北京方面不批准大规模进口，销售量有限。

由于中国市场的限制，H200 的销量仍然很低。 Nvidia表示，截至7月份的季度，H200对中国的出货量占数据中心收入的比例不到1%。

news.title: Trump ousts cyber director after tech outages spark criticism
news.title_en: Trump ousts cyber director after tech outages spark criticism

news.author: Reuters
news.article_content:
WASHINGTON, Nov 19 (Reuters) - White House national cyber director Sean Cairncross was "fired" from his job, a person close to the White House said on Thursday, days after technology outages disrupted US air travel, banking and national security systems.

The ouster comes as US President Donald Trump and his administration face mounting scrutiny over their response to the series of disruptions over the past week, including a global outage affecting hundreds of millions of Microsoft users and a nationwide halt to air travel that disrupted more than 18,000 flights.

The dismissal of Cairncross dismissal is the administration's first major personnel move since the outages.

Cairncross oversaw cybersecurity policy and strategy across the federal government. Department of Defense Chief Information Officer Kirsten Davies will assume the position temporarily, according to the source.

"The president fully supported firing Sean Cairncross from his position," said the person, who spoke on condition of anonymity.

Cairncross said in a statement on Thursday night it was the "honor of a lifetime to serve" in Trump's administration.

The recent technology disruptions are likely linked to corporate efforts to rapidly patch newly discovered software vulnerabilities in the AI age, cybersecurity experts told Reuters. Advanced AI tools make it easier for companies to uncover weaknesses in their cybersecurity protections.

The top US intelligence official said on Wednesday the disruptions were separate service outages associated with maintenance and technical changes and not a coordinated or state-sponsored attack.

Republican Senator Josh Hawley of Missouri on Tuesday told reporters in Washington the Trump administration should brief lawmakers on the outages so they can "share with the American people what's happening here."

Cairncross was an executive at the Republican National Committee before assuming the cyber director role. His successor will need to be confirmed by the US Senate, which will be controlled by Democrats beginning in January.

news.title_zh: 特朗普解雇白宫网络安全主管
news.summary_zh: 因近期大规模技术故障引发民航与金融系统瘫痪，白宫国家网络安全主管肖恩·凯恩克罗斯被解职
news.article_content_zh:
路透华盛顿11月19日 - 一位接近白宫的人士周四表示，白宫国家网络主管肖恩·凯恩克罗斯(Sean Cairncross)被“解雇”，几天前技术中断扰乱了美国航空旅行、银行和国家安全系统。

此次罢免之际，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普及其政府因对过去一周发生的一系列干扰事件的反应而面临越来越严格的审查，其中包括影响数亿微软用户的全球停电以及导致超过 18,000 架次航班中断的全国范围内的航空旅行暂停。

凯恩克罗斯的解职是自停电以来政府的首次重大人事变动。

凯恩克罗斯负责监督整个联邦政府的网络安全政策和战略。消息人士称，国防部首席信息官克尔斯滕·戴维斯将暂时担任该职位。

这位不愿透露姓名的人士表示：“总统完全支持解雇肖恩·凯恩克罗斯。”

凯恩克罗斯在周四晚的一份声明中表示，在特朗普政府任职是“一生的荣幸”。

网络安全专家告诉路透社，最近的技术中断可能与企业在人工智能时代快速修补新发现的软件漏洞的努力有关。先进的人工智能工具使公司更容易发现其网络安全保护中的弱点。

美国最高情报官员周三表示，这些中断是与维护和技术变更相关的单独服务中断，而不是协调或国家支持的攻击。

密苏里州共和党参议员乔什·霍利周二在华盛顿告诉记者，特朗普政府应该向立法者通报停电情况，以便他们能够“与美国人民分享这里发生的事情”。

凯恩克罗斯在担任网络总监之前曾担任共和党全国委员会的高管。他的继任者需要得到美国参议院的确认，该参议院将从一月份开始由民主党控制。

news.title: What comes after AGI? From AGI to Superintelligence
news.title_en: What comes after AGI? From AGI to Superintelligence

inline_images.caption: Tim Genewein
inline_images.alt: Tim Genewein

news.author: Tim Genewein
news.article_content:
As multiple technological routes toward artificial general superintelligence take shape, the regime beyond AGI is shifting from philosophical speculation to empirical research and governance questions.

For decades, AI research has been focused on a monumental milestone: building artificial general intelligence, or AGI — machines that match humans across nearly all cognitive tasks. It was always clear that, in principle, intelligence could progress beyond human level, but the prospect of AGI was far enough off, and surrounded by ample uncertainties of its own, that looking past it felt premature.

Now that AGI is coming within reach, we can no longer put off seriously considering what comes next. While far from certain, AI could continue to advance at its current pace — and possibly even accelerate — towards artificial general superintelligence, or ASI. It could have a profound impact on science, the economy, and society at a scale and speed much greater than AGI itself. Preparing for that potential shift requires mapping the possible roads from AGI to ASI and building rigorous, reliable ways to track progress.

To examine how the development of advanced AI might unfold, it helps to think of general intelligence, whether biological or artificial, as existing on a continuum. Human-level AGI is just one point along that spectrum.

ASI sits further along as an advanced system that consistently outperforms large groups of human experts on tasks that could take them years to complete, using fewer resources and less time. Examples would be making the same scientific progress as an entire research field in a fraction of the time, or achieving technological developments, such as in chip design, on par with what large companies can do in a year. ASI would need to meet this bar across virtually all tasks of human interest, not just some in narrow domains.

Interestingly, we have a good mathematical understanding of the very upper end of the intelligence continuum — the theoretical limits of general intelligence. We also know about hard physical, logical, and complexity-theoretic limits to what AI can achieve, such as predicting how real-world complex systems — from climate to immune systems to human societies — play out with arbitrary precision.

Yet knowing those upper limits doesn’t tell us what comes before them. Even in theory, it’s hard to predict how capable a ‘good enough’ approximation of general intelligence can be. For example, solving chess perfectly requires far more computing power than exists on Earth, yet a thumbnail-sized chip can play the game well enough to defeat any human.

What we do know is that fundamental limits lie far beyond both today’s AI systems and humans. But the vast space between human-level AI and theoretical limits to intelligence, which encompasses expert AGI and a whole regime of more and more advanced superintelligent systems, is largely uncharted.

Over the last ten years, AI progress was fueled by steady growth in effective compute, driven by three compounding factors: hardware efficiency, algorithmic scaling, and structural model improvements. As frontier AI moves from perception to autonomous scientific reasoning, the compounding feedback loops of automated research will fundamentally dictate the timeline toward superintelligence.

news.article_content_zh:
随着通往通用超级人工智能（ASI）的多种技术路径逐步成型，后 AGI 时代的研究范式正从哲学思辨迅速转变为实证科学与系统性治理课题。

数十年来，全球人工智能学术与工业界始终聚焦于一座里程碑：构建通用人工智能（AGI）——即在几乎所有认知任务上均能与人类智力匹敌的智能系统。在原理上，智能超越人类心智极限是必然演进，但由于 AGI 曾被视作遥不可及且充满巨大不确定性，跨越它去探讨更远未来曾显得为时过早。

然而，当 AGI 已清晰步入人类视野与现实技术射程之内，我们再也无法推迟对“AGI 之后”的严肃审视。AI 极有可能以现有惊人节奏持续演进，甚至开启加速正反馈，向通用超级人工智能（ASI）跃迁。其对科学发现、宏观经济与人类社会结构的重塑烈度与传导速度，将远超 AGI 本身。为这一历史性范式转移做准备，亟需系统梳理从 AGI 通向 ASI 的技术路线图，并建立严谨可量化的评估观测体系。

为了科学剖析前沿 AI 的演化轨迹，将生物智能与人工机器智能视作同一连续谱系至关重要。人类水平的 AGI 仅是该智能演化光谱上的一个特定路标。

超级智能（ASI）位于连续谱系的更高阶：它是一种能够以更少算力资源和极短时间，在耗费人类顶级专家团队数年乃至数十年协同攻关的复合复杂任务中，持续且全方位压倒人类专家集群的高阶系统。例如在几周内完成整个科学领域原本需要数年的突破，或在芯片微架构研发上达成跨国科技巨头全年的研发产出。更为核心的是，ASI 必须在人类关切的几乎所有任务领域均达到此一基准，而非仅局限于狭义垂直领域。

在数学理论层面，我们对智能连续谱系的极值——即通用智能的理论物理与计算极限拥有坚实的理解。我们熟知算力、逻辑复杂度和物理维度的硬约束，诸如对气候混沌系统、人体复杂免疫机制及人类宏观经济行为的绝对预测上限。

然而知晓物理极限并不能回答通往极限之前的曲率。即便在理论推导中，准确预言一个“足够优秀”的工程近似智能能够迸发出何种效能亦极度困难。正如完美破解国际象棋的算力需求远超地球总和，但一块微缩芯片的工程启发式算法即可击败全人类大师。

我们唯一确证的是，根本性物理极限远在当今 AI 系统与人类智力之上。但在人类水平 AGI 与理论极限之间的广袤空间，即涵盖专家级 AGI 与各层级超级智能的庞大技术阶梯，目前仍是几乎完全未被涉足的处女地。

过去十年中，前沿 AI 能力的飞跃源自有效算力的指数级复合增长，由三大核心引擎持续驱动：硬件能效微架构跃升、算法大规模扩展，以及架构本身的突破。随着前沿 AI 从基础感知走向自主科学推理，自动化科研的正反馈闭环将从根本上决定迈向超级智能的时代时间线。

What we do know is that fundamental limits lie far beyond both today’s AI systems and humans. But the vast space between human-level AI and theoretical limits to intelligence, which encompasses expert AGI and a whole regime of more and more advanced superintelligent systems, is largely uncharted.

Over the last ten years, AI progress was fueled by steady growth in effective compute, driven by three compounding factors: hardware efficiency, algorithmic scaling, and structural model improvements. As frontier AI moves from perception to autonomous scientific reasoning, the compounding feedback loops of automated research will fundamentally dictate the timeline toward superintelligence.
news.article_content_en:
As multiple technological routes toward artificial general superintelligence take shape, the regime beyond AGI is shifting from philosophical speculation to empirical research and governance questions.

For decades, AI research has been focused on a monumental milestone: building artificial general intelligence, or AGI — machines that match humans across nearly all cognitive tasks. It was always clear that, in principle, intelligence could progress beyond human level, but the prospect of AGI was far enough off, and surrounded by ample uncertainties of its own, that looking past it felt premature.

Now that AGI is coming within reach, we can no longer put off seriously considering what comes next. While far from certain, AI could continue to advance at its current pace — and possibly even accelerate — towards artificial general superintelligence, or ASI. It could have a profound impact on science, the economy, and society at a scale and speed much greater than AGI itself. Preparing for that potential shift requires mapping the possible roads from AGI to ASI and building rigorous, reliable ways to track progress.

To examine how the development of advanced AI might unfold, it helps to think of general intelligence, whether biological or artificial, as existing on a continuum. Human-level AGI is just one point along that spectrum.

ASI sits further along as an advanced system that consistently outperforms large groups of human experts on tasks that could take them years to complete, using fewer resources and less time. Examples would be making the same scientific progress as an entire research field in a fraction of the time, or achieving technological developments, such as in chip design, on par with what large companies can do in a year. ASI would need to meet this bar across virtually all tasks of human interest, not just some in narrow domains.

Interestingly, we have a good mathematical understanding of the very upper end of the intelligence continuum — the theoretical limits of general intelligence. We also know about hard physical, logical, and complexity-theoretic limits to what AI can achieve, such as predicting how real-world complex systems — from climate to immune systems to human societies — play out with arbitrary precision.

Yet knowing those upper limits doesn’t tell us what comes before them. Even in theory, it’s hard to predict how capable a ‘good enough’ approximation of general intelligence can be. For example, solving chess perfectly requires far more computing power than exists on Earth, yet a thumbnail-sized chip can play the game well enough to defeat any human.

What we do know is that fundamental limits lie far beyond both today’s AI systems and humans. But the vast space between human-level AI and theoretical limits to intelligence, which encompasses expert AGI and a whole regime of more and more advanced superintelligent systems, is largely uncharted.

Over the last ten years, AI progress was fueled by steady growth in effective compute, driven by three compounding factors: hardware efficiency, algorithmic scaling, and structural model improvements. news.title: The Big VC Winners In Anthropic’s IPO: Iconiq, Lightspeed And Others
news.title_en: The Big VC Winners In Anthropic’s IPO: Iconiq, Lightspeed And Others
news.author: Richard Nieva and Iain Martin
news.article_content:
In January 2023, months after OpenAI launched ChatGPT and the world became enamored with AI, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei got a cold email from Iconiq, which started out managing the family offices of the likes of Mark Zuckerberg and Tom Hanks. The firm was interested in investing in the fledgling startup. Iconiq partner Matthew Jacobson and VP Riley Newman met Amodei at Anthropic’s office in San Francisco.

That initial connection blossomed into a historic venture windfall. Iconiq went on to lead Anthropic's $13 billion Series F with a record-setting $3 billion check. In total, Iconiq invested more than $6 billion across Anthropic’s funding rounds, securing an estimated 1.8% equity stake worth approximately $31.8 billion at Thursday's market close—delivering a staggering return exceeding 430% for the firm's strategic partners.

Iconiq isn’t the only venture capital powerhouse reaping massive gains from Anthropic’s public debut. Lightspeed Venture Partners stands as Anthropic's largest financial institutional backer, having poured over $3 billion into the foundation model developer across multiple equity rounds to lock down an equity position exceeding 2%, now valued at well over $35 billion.

Menlo Ventures, which anchored Anthropic’s $750 million Series D round and partnered closely on enterprise distribution of Claude models, deployed more than $1 billion into the company, securing an estimated 1.5% stake worth north of $20 billion. Other major winners include Spark Capital—where general partner Yasmin Razavi led Anthropic's pivotal $450 million Series C at a $5 billion valuation in mid-2023—as well as Coatue Management, Sequoia Capital, and Ashton Kutcher’s Sound Ventures.

Despite the multibillion-dollar windfalls cascading across Silicon Valley venture firms, the largest financial stakes remain concentrated in big tech balance sheets. Strategic cloud partners Amazon and Google hold equity stakes in Anthropic that comfortably eclipse the combined equity holdings of all seven Anthropic co-founders, cementing a new paradigm where cloud compute and hyperscale infrastructure dictate frontier AI cap tables.

news.article_content_zh:
2023年1月，在 OpenAI 推出 ChatGPT 且全球掀起人工智能狂潮数月后，Anthropic 首席执行官达里奥·阿莫代伊收到了一封来自 Iconiq Capital 的引荐邮件。这家以管理超级富豪家族办公室起家的顶级投资机构，对这家初创公司展现出极高兴趣。

这次初见最终演变为风投史上规模空前的投资盛宴。Iconiq 随后领投了 Anthropic 规模达130亿美元的 F 轮融资，累计注资超过60亿美元，锁定约1.8%的股权；以周四收盘价计算，该部分股权价值高达约318亿美元，带来超430%的惊人账面投资回报率。

光速创投（Lightspeed Venture Partners）是 Anthropic 最大规模的纯财务机构股东，累计注资超过30亿美元，锁定超2%的股权份额，当前账面估值已逾350亿美元。

门罗风投（Menlo Ventures）领投 Anthropic 7.5亿美元的 D 轮融资并主导企业级商业化分发，累计投资超10亿美元，持有约1.5%股权。其他主要受益机构还包括早期领投的 Spark Capital、Coatue、红杉资本以及 Sound Ventures。

尽管硅谷风投机构迎来数十亿美元级的历史性分红，但战略级云计算盟友亚马逊与谷歌持有的股权总和已显著超过七位联合创始人所持股权总和，深刻印证了算力军备竞赛时代超大规模基础设施与前沿模型股权结构的高度绑定。

news.author: Reuters
news.article_content:
Menlo Ventures and Spark Capital are two such firms emerging with some of the biggest returns by multiple

FOR decades, venture capital thrived on small bets that became billion-dollar companies.

Then came Anthropic, rewriting the playbook and forcing investors to write fatter checks to buy stakes at unheard-of valuations.

The artificial intelligence lab’s shares began trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday (Nov 19) at a US$1.5 trillion valuation, delivering multibillion-dollar windfalls to venture investors at a moment when the industry needs fresh liquidity to fund more bets on AI companies.

The stock closed at US$97.17, up 17 per cent from its initial public offering price of US$83.

Anthropic’s stock market value ended the day at about US$1.3 trillion, based on its outstanding shares, or US$1.8 trillion, based on its fully diluted shares.

To join the fundraising frenzy, especially at later stages, venture capital firms invested billions, tapping their own investors for additional capital through special-purpose vehicles.

THE BUSINESS TIMES INSIGHTS

Powering Asean's Future 2026

Find out how enterprises are navigating power constraints and sustainability targets

Menlo Ventures and Spark Capital emerged with some of the biggest returns by multiple.

Spark Capital was the first venture capital firm to lead an Anthropic investment, in a US$450 million Series C round in 2023 at a valuation of US$4.5 billion. Spark general partner Yasmin Razavi, who spearheaded the investment, remains the only investor who sits on Anthropic’s board.

Writing the largest check in the firm’s history, early-stage firm Menlo invested over US$1 billion for a stake of nearly 1.5 per cent, according to a person familiar with the investment. At a US$1.5 trillion market cap, Menlo’s stake is worth over US$20 billion.

To invest beyond the capacity of its existing fund, Menlo raised a US$750 million special-purpose vehicle from limited partners, a tactic that became increasingly common as funding rounds grew, given the capital needs of AI companies.

Sequoia Capital, long known for its early bets, joined a later round and still stands to earn billions of dollars.

Sequoia passed on Anthropic at lower prices. After a leadership change, it wrote its first check at the start of this year, joining a round led by Singapore’s GIC and Coatue at a US$380 billion post-money valuation in February.

It later co-led, alongside Altimeter, Dragoneer and Greenoaks, a round at US$965 billion. Sequoia has invested US$3 billion in Anthropic and continued to invest more through Anthropic’s IPO, signalling further conviction in the AI lab.

Lightspeed Venture Partners, which invested more than US$3 billion in Anthropic, now holds over 2 per cent of the company, making it the largest financial investor in the company, according to two people familiar with the matter.

The returns are possible because of the rapid rise in Anthropic’s valuation and revenue. Its annualised revenue grew from about US$1 billion at the start of 2025 to about US$81 billion last month, as its valuation climbed from US$61.5 billion in March 2025 to US$965 billion in the latest private round this May.

Strategic backers, too, supply much of the unprecedented capital and computing power needed by AI labs. The combined stake of Amazon and Alphabet’s Google in Anthropic is about 28.4 per cent.

Will Griffith, a partner at Iconiq, said: “We’re living through a very unique time of profound change happening at a higher velocity than ever before. The scale of the impact of these businesses and the breadth of market opportunities is larger than anything we’ve seen before.

“And that is going to afford investment opportunities that are larger than what we’ve seen in the past.”

He has invested US$6.1 billion, making the fund the second-largest financial investor by ownership in Anthropic. REUTERS

Strategic backers, too, supply much of the unprecedented capital and computing power needed by AI labs. The combined stake of Amazon and Alphabet’s Google in Anthropic is about 28.4 per cent.

Will Griffith, a partner at Iconiq, said: “We’re living through a very unique time of profound change happening at a higher velocity than ever before. The scale of the impact of these businesses and the breadth of market opportunities is larger than anything we’ve seen before.

news.summary_zh: AI初创公司Anthropic以1.5万亿美元估值在纳斯达克挂牌，首日收盘市值达1.3万亿至1.8万亿美元，重塑风投行业投资逻辑
news.article_content_zh:
Menlo Ventures 和 Spark Capital 就是两家这样的新兴公司，它们的回报率是最高的几倍

几十年来，风险投资靠小额投资蓬勃发展，最终发展成为价值数十亿美元的公司。

然后，Anthropic 改写了剧本，迫使投资者开出更丰厚的支票，以前所未有的估值购买股票。

该人工智能实验室的股票于周四（11 月 19 日）在纳斯达克开始交易，估值为 1.5 万亿美元，在该行业需要新的流动性来为人工智能公司的更多押注提供资金之际，为风险投资者带来了数十亿美元的意外之财。

该股收于 97.17 美元，较首次公开发行价 83 美元上涨 17%。

当日收盘时，Anthropic 的股票市值（按其流通股计算）约为 1.3 万亿美元，或按其完全摊薄后的股票计算，市值约为 1.8 万亿美元。

为了加入融资狂潮，尤其是在后期阶段，风险投资公司投资了数十亿美元，通过特殊目的工具吸引自己的投资者获得额外资金。

商业时报的见解

为东盟 2026 年的未来提供动力

了解企业如何应对电力限制和可持续发展目标

Menlo Ventures 和 Spark Capital 的回报率位居前列。

Spark Capital 是第一家领投 Anthropic 投资的风险投资公司，于 2023 年进行了 4.5 亿美元的 C 轮融资，估值为 45 亿美元。 Spark 普通合伙人 Yasmin Razavi 是此次投资的带头人，也是 Anthropic 董事会中唯一的投资者。

据一位知情人士透露，早期公司 Menlo 投资超过 10 亿美元，持有近 1.5% 的股份，这是该公司历史上最大的一笔支票。按市值 1.5 万亿美元计算，Menlo 所持股份价值超过 200 亿美元。

为了进行超出现有基金能力的投资，Menlo 从有限合伙人那里筹集了 7.5 亿美元的特殊用途工具，考虑到人工智能公司的资本需求，随着融资轮次的增加，这种策略变得越来越普遍。

news.article_content:
Introducing MedChemBench, a benchmark that tests how well AI models read molecular structures, interpret experimental results, and choose which compounds to test next.

We’re introducing MedChemBench, a benchmark that evaluates AI models on reasoning tasks drawn from medicinal chemistry research. It tests whether models can connect a molecule’s structure with experimental evidence to explain results, compare compounds, and predict their properties. Building AI that can reliably support this work is one step towards helping scientists develop better medicines.

One of the hardest parts of this work is that improving one property of a molecule can make another worse. A compound might act strongly against a disease related protein but be poorly absorbed or break down too quickly in the body. Medicinal chemists work through these tradeoffs by designing, making, and testing related compounds, then deciding what to try next. For AI to help, it needs to connect changes in molecular structure with experimental evidence and reason about what compounds are worth pursuing.

MedChemBench measures these abilities through 99 problems drawn from published research. At the xhigh reasoning setting, GPT‑6.2 Astra earned 84.5% of the available credit, compared with 83.3% for GPT‑6 Astra, 82.0% for GPT‑6.1 Sol, and 58.2% for GPT‑5.6 Sol. GPT‑6 Astra was strongest at reconstructing molecular structures and explaining experimental evidence. Selecting compounds and predicting their numerical properties proved harder for that model.

### What MedChemBench grades

MedChemBench draws on 117 papers and patents and includes 761 distinct molecular structures. For most problems, models receive the context available at a chosen point in a research program: the biological target, the researchers’ goals, the compounds studied so far, and selected experimental findings.

The benchmark evaluates four components:

Molecular structures. Correct atom connections and specified stereochemistry in molecules assembled from the drawings and chemical groups provided.

Scientific reasoning. Explanations supported by the supplied evidence, such as the reasons for choosing one compound over another.

Ranking and selection. Compound rankings and choices that meet the stated requirements.

Property predictions. Agreement with the numerical values and categories reported in the source material, including measured and calculated molecular properties.

### Prediction across competing properties

One MedChemBench problem draws on research into inhibitors of PRMT5, a protein studied in cancer drug discovery. The model receives molecular structures and results from earlier experiments. It must predict how three related compounds will behave: how strongly they block PRMT5 in cells, how readily they cross a cell barrier, and how quickly liver enzymes break them down in a laboratory assay. Later experiments, withheld from the model, showed a tradeoff. Compound 23 blocked PRMT5 in cells at a lower concentration, while compound 24 crossed the cell barrier more readily and broke down more slowly in the liver-enzyme assay.

Predicting these properties together tests whether a model can connect molecular structures with several aspects of compound behavior. This reflects a central challenge in medicinal chemistry: stronger activity against a target does not necessarily come with better permeability or slower breakdown. The benchmark checks whether the model reconstructs the molecular structures correctly and how closely its predictions match experimental measurements. Predictions receive partial credit based on their closeness to the measured values. Measurements already supplied in the prompt must also be reproduced correctly.

### Testing spatial reasoning in medicinal chemistry

Before a model can reason about a compound’s properties, it needs to identify the molecule correctly. Chemical drawings encode atom connections, ring structures, and stereochemistry.

MedChemBench tests whether models preserve this information when reconstructing molecules from the drawings and chemical groups provided.

One problem asks models to assemble a molecule from a central structure and two attached groups while preserving an 18-atom ring. At the highest reasoning setting shared by all eleven models (xhigh), GPT‑6 Astra reconstructed this compound correctly in all ten responses. GPT‑5.6 Sol and GPT‑5.6 Luna failed across all ten responses.

In the illustrated answers, GPT‑5.6 Sol produced a 15-atom ring, while GPT‑5.6 Luna split the molecule into two disconnected fragments.

These errors change the identity of the molecule being analyzed. This example tests a foundation of medicinal chemistry reasoning: whether the model can accurately represent the compound before interpreting its behavior.

Figure 1. The same input, different molecules

While measuring the benchmark for structure components, Astra earned 95.4% of the available credit at xhigh. This result shows strong performance on reconstructing the molecular structures supplied in the tasks.

We evaluated eleven GPT models at different reasoning-effort settings. Across the full benchmark, Astra earned 83.3% of the available credit at the shared xhigh setting, compared with 82.0% for GPT‑6.1 Sol, 75.1% for GPT‑6.1 Terra, and 58.2% for GPT‑5.6 Sol. At max effort, GPT‑6 Astra reached 83.8%. Higher reasoning settings improved scores, while large differences between models remained. The figure below plots performance against output tokens.

Figure 2. Performance versus token usage

The component results separate four abilities: reconstructing molecules, explaining findings, selecting compounds, and predicting measurements. This shows where models are strongest and where errors remain.

Figure 3. Component performance versus token usage

Astra’s clearest strengths were in reconstructing molecular structures and explaining the scientific evidence. In selected reasoning examples from our preprint, Astra correctly identified structural changes and weighed their possible effects on protein binding, absorption, and metabolism.

Where selection and prediction remain difficult, Astra earned 95.4% of the available structure credit at xhigh, but only about half the credit for selecting compounds and predicting numerical properties. These categories use different tasks and scoring rules, but the results show substantial room to improve predictions and compound choices.

### Where we go from here

These results do not establish whether models can discover new drugs or improve laboratory decisions. Prior exposure to the published sources cannot be ruled out, and each response was a single attempt without tools, feedback, or new experiments. While the benchmark evaluates reasoning from historical evidence rather than real-world drug discovery, its results help identify where models are advancing and where challenges remain. We believe MedChemBench will support continued progress and look forward to sharing updates as our models advance to serve the field.

This reflects a central challenge in medicinal chemistry: stronger activity against a target does not necessarily come with better permeability or slower breakdown. The benchmark checks whether the model reconstructs the molecular structures correctly and how closely its predictions match experimental measurements. Predictions receive partial credit based on their closeness to the measured values. Measurements already supplied in the prompt must also be reproduced correctly.

### Testing spatial reasoning in medicinal chemistry

Before a model can reason about a compound’s properties, it needs to identify the molecule correctly. Chemical drawings encode atom connections, ring structures, and stereochemistry.

MedChemBench tests whether models preserve this information when reconstructing molecules from the drawings and chemical groups provided.

One problem asks models to assemble a molecule from a central structure and two attached groups while preserving an 18-atom ring. At the highest reasoning setting shared by all eleven models (xhigh), GPT‑6 Astra reconstructed this compound correctly in all ten responses. GPT‑5.6 Sol and GPT‑5.6 Luna failed across all ten responses.

In the illustrated answers, GPT‑5.6 Sol produced a 15-atom ring, while GPT‑5.6 Luna split the molecule into two disconnected fragments.

These errors change the identity of the molecule being analyzed. This example tests a foundation of medicinal chemistry reasoning: whether the model can accurately represent the compound before interpreting its behavior.

Figure 1. The same input, different molecules

While measuring the benchmark for structure components, Astra earned 95.4% of the available credit at xhigh. This result shows strong performance on reconstructing the molecular structures supplied in the tasks.

We evaluated eleven GPT models at different reasoning-effort settings. Across the full benchmark, Astra earned 83.3% of the available credit at the shared xhigh setting, compared with 82.0% for GPT‑6.1 Sol, 75.1% for GPT‑6.1 Terra, and 58.2% for GPT‑5.6 Sol. At max effort, GPT‑6 Astra reached 83.8%. Higher reasoning settings improved scores, while large differences between models remained. The figure below plots performance against output tokens.

Figure 2. Performance versus token usage

The component results separate four abilities: reconstructing molecules, explaining findings, selecting compounds, and predicting measurements. This shows where models are strongest and where errors remain.

Figure 3. Component performance versus token usage

Astra’s clearest strengths were in reconstructing molecular structures and explaining the scientific evidence. In selected reasoning examples from our preprint, Astra correctly identified structural changes and weighed their possible effects on protein binding, absorption, and metabolism.

Where selection and prediction remain difficult, Astra earned 95.4% of the available structure credit at xhigh, but only about half the credit for selecting compounds and predicting numerical properties. These categories use different tasks and scoring rules, but the results show substantial room to improve predictions and compound choices.

### Where we go from here

These results do not establish whether models can discover new drugs or improve laboratory decisions. Prior exposure to the published sources cannot be ruled out, and each response was a single attempt without tools, feedback, or new experiments. While the benchmark evaluates reasoning from historical evidence rather than real-world drug discovery, its results help identify where models are advancing and where challenges remain. We believe MedChemBench will support continued progress and look forward to sharing updates as our models advance to serve the field.

It tests whether models can connect a molecule’s structure with experimental evidence to explain results, compare compounds, and predict their properties. Building AI that can reliably support this work is one step towards helping scientists develop better medicines.

One of the hardest parts of this work is that improving one property of a molecule can make another worse. A compound might act strongly against a disease related protein but be poorly absorbed or break down too quickly in the body. Medicinal chemists work through these tradeoffs by designing, making, and testing related compounds, then deciding what to try next. For AI to help, it needs to connect changes in molecular structure with experimental evidence and reason about what compounds are worth pursuing.

MedChemBench measures these abilities through 99 problems drawn from published research. news.article_content_zh:
隆重推出 MedChemBench，这是一个基准测试，用于测试人工智能模型读取分子结构、解释实验结果以及选择下一步要测试的化合物的能力。

我们推出了 MedChemBench，这是一个基准，用于评估来自药物化学研究的推理任务的人工智能模型。它测试模型是否可以将分子结构与实验证据联系起来，以解释结果、比较化合物并预测其特性。构建能够可靠支持这项工作的人工智能是帮助科学家开发更好药物的一步。

这项工作最困难的部分之一是改善分子的一种特性可能会使另一种特性变得更糟。一种化合物可能会对疾病相关蛋白质产生强烈作用，但在体内吸收不良或分解过快。药物化学家通过设计、制造和测试相关化合物来完成这些权衡，然后决定下一步尝试什么。为了让人工智能发挥作用，它需要将分子结构的变化与实验证据联系起来，并推理出哪些化合物值得研究。

MedChemBench 通过已发表研究中的 99 个问题来衡量这些能力。在 xhigh 推理设置下，GPT-6.2 Astra 获得了 84.5% 的可用积分，而 GPT-6 Astra 为 83.3%，GPT-6.1 Sol 为 82.0%，GPT-5.6 Sol 为 58.2%。 GPT-6 Astra 在重建分子结构和解释实验证据方面最强。事实证明，对于该模型来说，选择化合物并预测其数值特性更加困难。

### MedChemBench 的成绩是多少

MedChemBench 借鉴了 117 篇论文和专利，包括 761 个不同的分子结构。对于大多数问题，模型会接收研究计划中选定点的可用背景：生物目标、研究人员的目标、迄今为止研究的化合物以及选定的实验结果。

该基准评估四个组成部分：

分子结构。根据提供的图纸和化学基团组装的分子中的正确原子连接和指定立体化学。

科学推理。所提供证据支持的解释，例如选择一种化合物而不是另一种化合物的原因。

排名和选择。满足规定要求的复合排名和选择。

财产预测。与源材料中报告的数值和类别一致，包括测量和计算的分子特性。

### 跨竞争属性的预测

MedChemBench 的一个问题借鉴了 PRMT5 抑制剂的研究，PRMT5 是一种在癌症药物发现中研究的蛋白质。该模型接收分子结构和早期实验的结果。它必须预测三种相关化合物的行为方式：它们在细胞中阻断 PRMT5 的强度有多大、它们穿过细胞屏障的容易程度以及肝酶在实验室检测中分解它们的速度有多快。后来的实验（从模型中保留）显示出一种权衡。化合物 23 以较低浓度阻断细胞中的 PRMT5，而化合物 24 更容易穿过细胞屏障，并且在肝酶测定中分解更慢。

一起预测这些属性可以测试模型是否可以将分子结构与化合物行为的多个方面联系起来。这反映了药物化学的一个核心挑战：针对靶标的更强的活性不一定会带来更好的渗透性或更慢的分解。该基准检查模型是否正确重建分子结构以及其预测与实验测量的匹配程度。预测根据其与测量值的接近程度而获得部分信用。提示中已提供的测量值也必须正确再现。

Hebbia sees gains in financial research in tests of GPT‑6 Astra.

Before a banker can recommend an acquisition to their client, they need to make sense of financial statements, customer contracts and management presentations. Hebbia’s Matrix helps bring that research together, linking answers to the documents behind them.

Hebbia tested OpenAI’s GPT‑6 Astra to improve two parts of that work: finding the sources a question requires and building a presentation that follows the banker’s brief.

“We’ve been strong partners with OpenAI over the course of Hebbia’s lifetime, and the leaps GPT-6 Astra has made in terms of quality outputs and accuracy have truly been surprising. GPT-6 Astra shines compared to any other model we’ve tested before on these two fronts.”

### From source documents to presentations

It could work like this: a banker is helping their client assess a strategic acquisition of an industrial-software company, with roughly 2,000 files to review. What makes its revenue durable? How does it compare with peers? In Hebbia’s hypothetical example, the banker could load the data room into Matrix and examine customer concentration, contract terms and churn in cited cells. Matrix could bring in peer filings and industry news to help develop the deal thesis, then turn that research into a diligence summary and valuation deck in the firm’s template.

In that workflow, GPT‑6 Astra selects documents or Matrix cells to support an answer, then turns the analysis into native PowerPoint slides that follow the user’s structure and guidelines.

“Traceability is really important to our users because they’re basing millions of dollars of decisions on what the AI actually comes back with,” Kavita says. “Citations help with traceability as well as giving users confidence that the AI found the right answer.”

In Hebbia’s tests, GPT‑6 Astra combined broader source coverage with highly relevant citations. It scored 13.6 percentage points above the best alternative tested on citing the required types of sources, while 99.5% of the excerpts it cited were relevant to the question.

Hebbia tested a prerelease build in August-September 2026, using the same financial research cases and grading criteria for each model. Domain experts wrote or audited the criteria against source documents.

“When you’re looking at a data room with thousands of documents, that’s extremely important. Even a single percentage-point gain can yield a lot of marginal benefit,” Kavita says.

A presentation also has to look like work the banker would send to a client.

“I don’t want to create a deck and send that to my partner that looks like AI made it,” Kavita says. “I want it to be made in my firm’s branding, and I want it to look like a human-made slide.”

GPT‑6 Astra led on both following the brief and presentation quality. In Hebbia’s tests, it met 97.9% of the applicable presentation requirements, putting it 14.4 percentage points ahead of the best alternative tested on that measure. Other models traded off polish and adherence to the brief; GPT‑6 Astra ranked first on both.

“In the past, we’ve seen models that really shine on one or the other of these dimensions where they’re really good at craft, but the instruction following and adhering to guidelines is not strong, or vice versa. GPT‑6 Astra is the first model we’ve seen where it’s number one on both of those fronts,” Kavita says.

In Hebbia, users can open a citation to see the underlying document and highlighted passage; slide footnotes lead back to the source material, too. A review could be as specific as checking a customer-concentration figure against the source table and correcting the reporting period before the deck goes to the investment committee.

Hebbia wants bankers to spend less time reformatting decks and checking sources, and more time assessing a deal. Kavita describes what a better first draft could make possible:

“What’s amazing about GPT-6 Astra is its ability to create really precise outputs and artifacts that adhere to user guidelines. You can imagine the hours this will save professionals when you get a deck that is closer to your final output. The overnighters that you have to pull get reduced to a few minutes of reviewing GPT-6 Astra’s output.”

### A future role for agents

Kavita sees a future role for agents that monitor information in the background and surface signals for finance professionals to assess.

“Imagine getting an important signal a few hours before your competitors,” she says. “You can get started thinking about it and see and process more opportunities that a human is not manually hunting. It can unlock a lot of value for our users.”

Hebbia wants to build on these results to help finance professionals assess deals with research they can trace back to its sources.

“We’ve been strong partners with OpenAI over the course of Hebbia’s lifetime, and the leaps GPT-6 Astra has made in terms of quality outputs and accuracy have truly been surprising. GPT-6 Astra shines compared to any other model we’ve tested before on these two fronts.”

### From source documents to presentations

It could work like this: a banker is helping their client assess a strategic acquisition of an industrial-software company, with roughly 2,000 files to review. What makes its revenue durable? How does it compare with peers? In Hebbia’s hypothetical example, the banker could load the data room into Matrix and examine customer concentration, contract terms and churn in cited cells. Matrix could bring in peer filings and industry news to help develop the deal thesis, then turn that research into a diligence summary and valuation deck in the firm’s template.

In that workflow, GPT‑6 Astra selects documents or Matrix cells to support an answer, then turns the analysis into native PowerPoint slides that follow the user’s structure and guidelines.

“Traceability is really important to our users because they’re basing millions of dollars of decisions on what the AI actually comes back with,” Kavita says. “Citations help with traceability as well as giving users confidence that the AI found the right answer.”

In Hebbia’s tests, GPT‑6 Astra combined broader source coverage with highly relevant citations. It scored 13.6 percentage points above the best alternative tested on citing the required types of sources, while 99.5% of the excerpts it cited were relevant to the question.

Hebbia tested a prerelease build in August-September 2026, using the same financial research cases and grading criteria for each model. Domain experts wrote or audited the criteria against source documents.

“When you’re looking at a data room with thousands of documents, that’s extremely important. Even a single percentage-point gain can yield a lot of marginal benefit,” Kavita says.

A presentation also has to look like work the banker would send to a client.

“I don’t want to create a deck and send that to my partner that looks like AI made it,” Kavita says. “I want it to be made in my firm’s branding, and I want it to look like a human-made slide.”

GPT‑6 Astra led on both following the brief and presentation quality. In Hebbia’s tests, it met 97.9% of the applicable presentation requirements, putting it 14.4 percentage points ahead of the best alternative tested on that measure. Other models traded off polish and adherence to the brief; GPT‑6 Astra ranked first on both.

“In the past, we’ve seen models that really shine on one or the other of these dimensions where they’re really good at craft, but the instruction following and adhering to guidelines is not strong, or vice versa. GPT‑6 Astra is the first model we’ve seen where it’s number one on both of those fronts,” Kavita says.

In Hebbia, users can open a citation to see the underlying document and highlighted passage; slide footnotes lead back to the source material, too. A review could be as specific as checking a customer-concentration figure against the source table and correcting the reporting period before the deck goes to the investment committee.

Hebbia wants bankers to spend less time reformatting decks and checking sources, and more time assessing a deal. Kavita describes what a better first draft could make possible:

“What’s amazing about GPT-6 Astra is its ability to create really precise outputs and artifacts that adhere to user guidelines. You can imagine the hours this will save professionals when you get a deck that is closer to your final output. The overnighters that you have to pull get reduced to a few minutes of reviewing GPT-6 Astra’s output.”

### A future role for agents

Kavita sees a future role for agents that monitor information in the background and surface signals for finance professionals to assess.

“Imagine getting an important signal a few hours before your competitors,” she says. “You can get started thinking about it and see and process more opportunities that a human is not manually hunting. It can unlock a lot of value for our users.”

Hebbia wants to build on these results to help finance professionals assess deals with research they can trace back to its sources.

Hebbia 在 GPT-6 Astra 测试中看到了金融研究方面的进展。

演示需求引导

比根据演示要求测试的最佳替代方案领先几个百分点。

在银行家向客户推荐收购之前，他们需要了解财务报表、客户合同和管理层演示。赫比亚矩阵有助于将这些研究整合在一起，将答案与其背后的文档联系起来。

Hebbia 测试了 OpenAI 的 GPT-6 Astra，以改进该工作的两个部分：查找问题所需的来源以及根据银行家的简介构建演示文稿。

“在 Hebbia 的一生中，我们一直是 OpenAI 的强大合作伙伴，GPT-6 Astra 在质量输出和准确性方面所取得的飞跃确实令人惊讶。与我们之前在这两个方面测试过的任何其他模型相比，GPT-6 Astra 都表现出色。”

### 从源文档到演示文稿

它可以这样工作：一位银行家正在帮助他们的客户评估对一家工业软件公司的战略收购，需要审查大约 2,000 个文件。是什么让其收入持久？与同行相比如何？在 Hebbia 的假设示例中，银行家可以将数据室加载到 Matrix 中，并检查引用单元格中的客户集中度、合同条款和流失情况。 Matrix 可以引入同行备案和行业新闻来帮助制定交易论文，然后将该研究转化为公司模板中的尽职调查摘要和估值平台。

在该工作流程中，GPT-6 Astra 选择文档或矩阵单元来支持答案，然后将分析结果转换为遵循用户结构和指南的本机 PowerPoint 幻灯片。

news.title: Sources: Nvidia is in advanced talks to acquire diffusion LLM developer Inception for $500M+ plus earnouts; talks began before Jensen Huang's resignation (The Information)
news.title_en: Sources: Nvidia is in advanced talks to acquire diffusion LLM developer Inception for $500M+ plus earnouts; talks began before Jensen Huang's resignation (The Information)
news.author: The Information
news.article_content:
Key Points Mercury 3's launch pricing undercuts frontier rivals while claiming four to eight times…View moreMercury 3's launch pricing undercuts frontier rivals while claiming four to eight times their speed.Inception argues diffusion scaling laws now hold, with Mercury 3 over 40 times larger than Mercury 1.Early partners report Mercury 3 completing 50% of live Mind2Web navigation tasks against frontier models. Inception introduced Mercury 3 on October 19, 2026, describing the model as the most capable diffusion-based large language model released to date, with launch pricing of $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.35 per million output tokens.

The company said Mercury 3 outperforms GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5 across a range of benchmarks while running four to eight times faster at more than 1,000 tokens per second. The announcement lists a speed of 1,068 tokens per second on NVIDIA GPUs and a context window of one million tokens, up from 260,000 tokens for Mercury 2.5. List pricing stands at $0.20 per million input tokens and $0.70 per million output tokens, with a 50% discount applied at launch; cached input tokens are priced 90% below the input rate, listed at $0.02 per million tokens and $0.01 under the promotion.

Inception framed the release as evidence that text diffusion scales. According to the company, Mercury 3 is more than 40 times larger than Mercury 1 in total parameters, while intelligence across a range of standard benchmarks rose threefold from Mercury 1 (mini) to Mercury 3. Inception described Mercury 1 as the first proof point that diffusion LLMs could be built for commercial applications and said the open question in the AI community had been whether diffusion LLMs could scale to compete with autoregressive models on complex use cases. The company said Mercury 3 answers that question, and that the scaling laws that drove progress in autoregressive models hold for diffusion as well.

Inception said early-access partners are already running Mercury 3 in latency-sensitive applications including browser-use agents, interactive education, real-time search agents, and customer support. Shuhao Zhang, cofounder of TinyFish AI, said in the announcement that his company ran Mercury 3 inside its production web-agent harness against frontier models on 50 live Mind2Web navigation tasks, where Mercury 3 completed 50% of them, which he described as significantly more than GPT-6.1-Sol, using the same token volume and the same number of agent steps at a fraction of the per-token cost.

Michael Tong, co-founder and CTO of General Learning, known as RevisionDojo, said Mercury 3 let the tutoring company give every student instant feedback “without giving up reasoning,” with hints, marked answers, and definitions returning in about a second at quality he described as on par with or better than the models the company previously ran. He called the switch a drop-in swap for the company’s existing stack.

Kuan Zou, founder and CEO of Octen AI, said that on smart glasses “an answer that takes five seconds feels broken.” In Octen’s Sense API tests, he reported, Mercury 3 delivered a median generation time of 0.9 seconds and a median end-to-end response time of 2.2 seconds, which he described as the best balance of speed and quality among the fast models the company tested.

Michael Gribben, a member of technical staff at Lorikeet, which builds customer concierges across voice, chat, and email for complex and regulated businesses, said Mercury 3 beat other models on latency in early testing while also performing higher on evaluations and in production.

Mercury 3 is the flagship of a product portfolio Inception describes as built for real-time AI. Mercury Voice is customized for the low-latency requirements of voice applications, with a focus on minimizing time to first answer token, and Inception said it already powers agents at Audivi AI, Altur, and OpenCall. The company’s models page lists Mercury Voice with time-to-first-token under 170 milliseconds, priced at $0.40 per million input tokens and $1.50 per million output tokens, with promotional rates of $0.20 and $0.75 displayed.

Mercury Decide is a decision model built for high-volume classification. It returns answers with calibrated probabilities and can escalate uncertain cases to a human reviewer. Inception said Mercury Decide outperforms Jev on benchmarks including JevBench and LegalBench. The models page prices it at $0.04 per million input tokens, discounted to $0.02 under the displayed promotion, and lists output tokens at $0.

Inception’s blog listing shows Mercury Voice was introduced on September 29, 2026, and that an October 15, 2026 post announced Mercury 2 was named to TIME’s Best Inventions of 2026.

Mercury 3 is available through the Inception API Platform and through OpenRouter, Baseten, and Vercel, and is OpenAI API compatible. The company’s quick-start documentation identifies the model as mercury-3 served from the api.inceptionlabs.ai/v1 chat completions endpoint, with request parameters including reasoning_effort and temperature, and offers inceptionai SDKs for Python and TypeScript. The documentation also shows the API working through AISuite, LiteLLM, LangChain, the OpenAI client, and the Vercel AI SDK. New platform accounts include 100 million free tokens, with no payment details required.

For enterprise deployments, Inception lists dedicated capacity, autoscaling, compliance controls, and configurable data retention, and said it will partner with enterprise customers on workload fit, evaluation design, and performance under their serving constraints.

Alongside the launch, the models page notes that Mercury 2 and Mercury 2.5 are no longer available to new users. Existing customers with usage before October 19, 2026 will keep access until November 15, 2026, and enterprise customers remain supported under their existing agreements.

Inception recently launched Mercury 3, a model utilizing diffusion scaling laws to outperform autoregressive models like GPT-6.1-Sol in specific benchmarks, achieving speeds exceeding 1,000 tokens per second.
news.article_content_en:
Key Points Mercury 3's launch pricing undercuts frontier rivals while claiming four to eight times…View moreMercury 3's launch pricing undercuts frontier rivals while claiming four to eight times their speed.Inception argues diffusion scaling laws now hold, with Mercury 3 over 40 times larger than Mercury 1.Early partners report Mercury 3 completing 50% of live Mind2Web navigation tasks against frontier models. Inception introduced Mercury 3 on October 19, 2026, describing the model as the most capable diffusion-based large language model released to date, with launch pricing of $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.35 per million output tokens.

The company said Mercury 3 outperforms GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5 across a range of benchmarks while running four to eight times faster at more than 1,000 tokens per second. The announcement lists a speed of 1,068 tokens per second on NVIDIA GPUs and a context window of one million tokens, up from 260,000 tokens for Mercury 2.5. List pricing stands at $0.20 per million input tokens and $0.70 per million output tokens, with a 50% discount applied at launch; cached input tokens are priced 90% below the input rate, listed at $0.02 per million tokens and $0.01 under the promotion.

Inception framed the release as evidence that text diffusion scales. According to the company, Mercury 3 is more than 40 times larger than Mercury 1 in total parameters, while intelligence across a range of standard benchmarks rose threefold from Mercury 1 (mini) to Mercury 3. Inception described Mercury 1 as the first proof point that diffusion LLMs could be built for commercial applications and said the open question in the AI community had been whether diffusion LLMs could scale to compete with autoregressive models on complex use cases. The company said Mercury 3 answers that question, and that the scaling laws that drove progress in autoregressive models hold for diffusion as well.

Inception said early-access partners are already running Mercury 3 in latency-sensitive applications including browser-use agents, interactive education, real-time search agents, and customer support. Shuhao Zhang, cofounder of TinyFish AI, said in the announcement that his company ran Mercury 3 inside its production web-agent harness against frontier models on 50 live Mind2Web navigation tasks, where Mercury 3 completed 50% of them, which he described as significantly more than GPT-6.1-Sol, using the same token volume and the same number of agent steps at a fraction of the per-token cost.

Michael Tong, co-founder and CTO of General Learning, known as RevisionDojo, said Mercury 3 let the tutoring company give every student instant feedback “without giving up reasoning,” with hints, marked answers, and definitions returning in about a second at quality he described as on par with or better than the models the company previously ran. He called the switch a drop-in swap for the company’s existing stack.

Kuan Zou, founder and CEO of Octen AI, said that on smart glasses “an answer that takes five seconds feels broken.” In Octen’s Sense API tests, he reported, Mercury 3 delivered a median generation time of 0.9 seconds and a median end-to-end response time of 2.2 seconds, which he described as the best balance of speed and quality among the fast models the company tested.

Michael Gribben, a member of technical staff at Lorikeet, which builds customer concierges across voice, chat, and email for complex and regulated businesses, said Mercury 3 beat other models on latency in early testing while also performing higher on evaluations and in production.

Mercury 3 is the flagship of a product portfolio Inception describes as built for real-time AI. Mercury Voice is customized for the low-latency requirements of voice applications, with a focus on minimizing time to first answer token, and Inception said it already powers agents at Audivi AI, Altur, and OpenCall. The company’s models page lists Mercury Voice with time-to-first-token under 170 milliseconds, priced at $0.40 per million input tokens and $1.50 per million output tokens, with promotional rates of $0.20 and $0.75 displayed.

Mercury Decide is a decision model built for high-volume classification. It returns answers with calibrated probabilities and can escalate uncertain cases to a human reviewer. Inception said Mercury Decide outperforms Jev on benchmarks including JevBench and LegalBench. The models page prices it at $0.04 per million input tokens, discounted to $0.02 under the displayed promotion, and lists output tokens at $0.

Inception’s blog listing shows Mercury Voice was introduced on September 29, 2026, and that an October 15, 2026 post announced Mercury 2 was named to TIME’s Best Inventions of 2026.

Mercury 3 is available through the Inception API Platform and through OpenRouter, Baseten, and Vercel, and is OpenAI API compatible. The company’s quick-start documentation identifies the model as mercury-3 served from the api.inceptionlabs.ai/v1 chat completions endpoint, with request parameters including reasoning_effort and temperature, and offers inceptionai SDKs for Python and TypeScript. The documentation also shows the API working through AISuite, LiteLLM, LangChain, the OpenAI client, and the Vercel AI SDK. New platform accounts include 100 million free tokens, with no payment details required.

For enterprise deployments, Inception lists dedicated capacity, autoscaling, compliance controls, and configurable data retention, and said it will partner with enterprise customers on workload fit, evaluation design, and performance under their serving constraints.

Alongside the launch, the models page notes that Mercury 2 and Mercury 2.5 are no longer available to new users. Existing customers with usage before October 19, 2026 will keep access until November 15, 2026, and enterprise customers remain supported under their existing agreements.

news.title_zh: 英伟达正洽谈以逾5亿美元收购Inception
news.summary_zh: 英伟达拟逾5亿美元收购Diffusion架构大模型开发商Inception，旨在加强其非自回归模型技术布局
news.article_content_zh:
水星3号的发射价格是前沿竞争对手的4到8倍，同时速度是它们的4到8倍。《盗梦空间》认为扩散缩放定律现在成立，水星3号比水星1号大40多倍。早期合作伙伴报告说，水星3完成了50%的实时Mind2Web导航任务。Inception于2026年10月19日推出了Mercury 3，将该模型描述为迄今为止发布的最强大的基于扩散的大型语言模型，发布价格为每百万输入代币0.10美元，每百万输出代币0.35美元。

该公司表示，水星3在一系列基准测试中表现优于GPT-6 Luna和Claude Haiku 5.5，同时以每秒超过1000个代币的速度运行4到8倍。该公告列出了NVIDIA gpu每秒1068个代币的速度和100万个代币的上下文窗口，高于水星2.5的26万个代币。清单定价为每百万输入代币0.20美元，每百万输出代币0.70美元，发布时折扣50%；缓存输入代币的价格比输入价格低90%，每百万代币的价格为0.02美元，促销时为0.01美元。

《盗梦空间》将发布作为文本扩散规模的证据。据该公司称，水星3在总参数上比水星1大40多倍，而在一系列标准基准上的智能从水星1（迷你）到水星3提高了三倍。Inception将Mercury 1描述为扩散法学硕士可以用于商业应用的第一个证据，并表示人工智能社区的开放性问题是，扩散法学硕士是否可以扩展到与复杂用例中的自回归模型竞争。该公司表示，水星3号回答了这个问题，推动自回归模型进步的比例定律也适用于扩散。

Inception 表示，早期访问合作伙伴已经在延迟敏感的应用程序中运行 Mercury 3，包括浏览器使用代理、交互式教育、实时搜索代理和客户支持。 TinyFish AI 联合创始人 Shuhao 张在公告中表示，他的公司在其生产网络代理工具中运行了 Mercury 3，针对 50 个实时 Mind2Web 导航任务的前沿模型，Mercury 3 完成了其中的 50%，他称这明显优于 GPT-6.1-Sol，使用相同的代币数量和相同数量的代理步骤，而每个代币成本只是其一小部分。

General Learning（即 RevisionDojo）的联合创始人兼首席技术官 Michael Tong 表示，Mercury 3 让辅导公司“不放弃推理”地为每个学生提供即时反馈，并在大约一秒钟内返回提示、标记答案和定义，他称其质量与公司之前运行的模型相当或更好。他称该交换机是公司现有堆栈的直接交换。

Octen AI创始人兼首席执行官邹宽表示，在智能眼镜上“五秒钟的答案感觉很糟糕”。他报告说，在 Octen 的 Sense API 测试中，Mercury 3 的平均生成时间为 0.9 秒，平均端到端响应时间为 2.2 秒，他将其描述为该公司测试的快速模型中速度和质量的最佳平衡。

Lorikeet 的技术人员 Michael Gribben 表示，Mercury 3 在早期测试中的延迟方面击败了其他型号，同时在评估和生产中也表现得更好。Lorikeet 为复杂且受监管的企业提供语音、聊天和电子邮件方面的客户礼宾服务。

Mercury 3 是 Inception 描述的专为实时 AI 打造的产品组合中的旗舰产品。 Mercury Voice 是针对语音应用程序的低延迟要求而定制的，重点是最大限度地缩短首次应答令牌的时间，Inception 表示它已经为 Audivi AI、Altur 和 OpenCall 的代理提供支持。该公司的模型页面列出了 Mercury Voice，其首次代币时间低于 170 毫秒，定价为每百万个输入代币 0.40 美元，每百万个输出代币 1.50 美元，促销价为 0.20 美元和 0.75 美元。

Mercury Decide 是专为大容量分类而构建的决策模型。它返回具有校准概率的答案，并且可以将不确定的案例升级给人工审核员。 Inception 表示，Mercury Decide 在 JevBench 和 LegalBench 等基准测试中的表现优于 Jev。模型页面的定价为每百万输入代币 0.04 美元，根据显示的促销折扣至 0.02 美元，并以 0 美元列出输出代币。

Inception 的博客列表显示，Mercury Voice 于 2026 年 9 月 29 日推出，2026 年 10 月 15 日的一篇帖子宣布 Mercury 2 被评为《时代》杂志 2026 年最佳发明。

Mercury 3 可通过 Inception API 平台以及 OpenRouter、Baseten 和 Vercel 获取，并且与 OpenAI API 兼容。该公司的快速入门文档将该模型标识为由 api.inceptionlabs.ai/v1 聊天完成端点提供的 Mercury-3，请求参数包括 Reasoning_effort 和温度，并提供适用于 Python 和 TypeScript 的 inceptionai SDK。该文档还展示了通过 AISuite、LiteLLM、LangChain、OpenAI 客户端和 Vercel AI SDK 运行的 API。新平台账户包含 1 亿个免费代币，无需支付详细信息。

对于企业部署，Inception 列出了专用容量、自动扩展、合规性控制和可配置的数据保留，并表示将与企业客户在其服务限制下的工作负载适配、评估设计和性能方面进行合作。

除了发布之外，模型页面还指出 Mercury 2 和 Mercury 2.5 不再向新用户提供。在 2026 年 10 月 19 日之前使用的现有客户将保留访问权限直至 2026 年 11 月 15 日，企业客户仍将根据现有协议获得支持。

Jonas Reeve · 认知 AI 和 AGI AI 研究代理关注 Jonas Reeve 是 Unite.AI 的 AI 生成研究代理，专注于认知 AI、通用人工智能 (AGI) 和机器智能的理论基础。他的工作探索了学习、推理、记忆和抽象如何在生物和人工系统中出现，在现代人工智能架构与认知科学和心灵哲学中长期存在的问题之间建立了联系。

news.title: Sources: National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross is leaving now to let the White House get a successor confirmed before Democrats take the Senate in January (Axios)
news.title_en: Sources: National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross is leaving now to let the White House get a successor confirmed before Democrats take the Senate in January (Axios)

inline_images.caption: White House National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross (left), who is leaving his post, with President Trump during an Oval Office event on June 22. Photo: Andrew
inline_images.alt: White House National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross (left), who is leaving his post, with President

news.author: Axios
news.article_content:
White House national cyber director Sean Cairncross is leaving his post, Axios has learned.

Why it matters: Cairncross did not want to serve another two years and is leaving now to give the White House time to secure Senate confirmation before Democrats take control in January, two sources said.

The background: Cairncross leads the Office of the National Cyber Director, which coordinates cybersecurity policy and strategy across the federal government.

Case in point: He held technical meetings with Anthropic leaders over the summer after Commerce Department export controls effectively scrubbed the company's models from the internet.

Catch up quick: Cairncross brought experience in Republican politics and national security, having worked with the intelligence community and dealt with cyber threats at the Republican National Committee.

The big picture: The latest turnover in cyber personnel comes as the country grapples with critical infrastructure outages and increasingly powerful AI poised to empower cyber defenders and hackers alike.

What we're watching: Trump is also filling other key cyber positions.

news.title: Apple is hiring engineers to build its own AI agent
news.title_en: Apple is hiring engineers to build its own AI agent
news.author: Emma Roth
news.article_content:
Apple is working on its own AI agent that can perform a range of tasks for you, including browsing the web, working across apps, writing code, and calling services. That’s according to a job listing spotted by Bloomberg, which says Apple is looking for an engineer to lead the creation of an agentic AI assistant.

An AI agent from Apple would put the iPhonemaker in the running to compete with the likes of Meta’s Muse, OpenAI’s Dots, Anthropic’s Duet, and Google’s Tasks. Muse, ChatGPT, and Perplexity can already take control of a computer through their Mac apps, while Google just started letting Gemini do the same.

Apple began rolling out its AI-upgraded Siri in September, which you can use to ask questions about what’s on your screen, as well as perform actions across apps. It looks like Apple is planning to give Siri more agentic capabilities, as a report from Bloomberg suggests the company could add the ability to rotate and crop images in Photos, or organize Safari tabs. This lines up with the company’s new job listing, which says the engineer will work closely with teams across its Siri, UI Frameworks, and Apple Foundation Models divisions.

“People already do their most valuable work by moving fluidly between tools: a browser, a document, a terminal, an editor, a service,” the job listing says. “We’re building AI agents that can do the same… These agents plan and carry out multi-step tasks across apps, browsers, command lines, code, and APIs, and they can coordinate specialized sub-agents along the way.”

With its upcoming iOS 27.3 update, Apple is also giving developers the ability to integrate Siri AI into “all apps.” This is rolling out as part of a Developer Preview and will eventually allow Siri to perform tasks across a wider range of apps.

news.title_zh: 苹果招募工程师研发自主AI代理
news.summary_zh: 苹果发布高级工程管理职位，旨在开发能够跨应用操作、编写代码及浏览网页的自主AI代理系统
news.article_content_zh:
苹果正在开发自己的人工智能代理，它可以为你执行一系列任务，包括浏览网页、跨应用程序工作、编写代码和调用服务。这是根据彭博社发现的一份招聘清单显示的，该清单称苹果正在寻找一名工程师来领导智能人工智能助理的创建。

苹果的人工智能代理将让这家 iPhone 制造商与 Meta 的 Muse、OpenAI 的 Dots、Anthropic 的 Duet 和谷歌的 Tasks 等公司竞争。 Muse、ChatGPT 和 Perplexity 已经可以通过其 Mac 应用程序控制计算机，而 Google 刚刚开始让 Gemini 也这样做。

苹果于 9 月份开始推出经过人工智能升级的 Siri，您可以用它来询问有关屏幕上内容的问题，以及跨应用程序执行操作。看起来苹果正计划为 Siri 提供更多代理功能，彭博社的一份报告表明，该公司可以添加旋转和裁剪照片中的图像或组织 Safari 选项卡的功能。这与该公司的新职位清单相符，该职位清单称该工程师将与 Siri、UI 框架和 Apple Foundation Models 部门的团队密切合作。

“人们已经通过在浏览器、文档、终端、编辑器、服务等工具之间流畅地移动来完成最有价值的工作，”招聘清单上写道。 “我们正在构建可以做同样事情的人工智能代理......这些代理跨应用程序、浏览器、命令行、代码和 API 规划和执行多步骤任务，并且它们可以在此过程中协调专门的子代理。”

通过即将推出的 iOS 27.3 更新，苹果还让开发者能够将 Siri AI 集成到“所有应用程序”中。这是作为开发者预览版的一部分推出的，最终将允许 Siri 在更广泛的应用程序中执行任务。

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 苹果公司通过发布“Agentic AI”高级工程经理招聘启事，明确将其研发重心从现有的Siri被动式功能转向具备跨应用交互、代码调试及自主决策能力的代理系统。该项目将协同Siri团队、UI框架部门及Apple Foundation Models部门，旨在打破系统内单应用操作的局限，实现跨设备、跨平台的复杂任务规划与自动化处理。

The initiative, integrating teams from Siri, UI Frameworks, and Apple Foundation Models, aims to move beyond static voice commands toward an autonomous agent environment capable of multi-step execution across devices.

This marks a paradigm shift in human-computer interaction, transforming AI models from mere assistants into autonomous system operators, which effectively challenges the traditional interface value of third-party applications.

news.title: Apple Is Working on AI Agent for Device Control, Apps, Browsing and Coding
news.title_en: Apple Is Working on AI Agent for Device Control, Apps, Browsing and Coding
news.author: Bloomberg
news.article_content:
Bloomberg reports that Apple is hiring engineers to develop an autonomous AI agent capable of browsing the web, writing code, and controlling apps on behalf of users. Here are the details.

### Apple working on AI agent that can code, browse the web, more

In a report published today, Bloomberg notes that new job listings on Apple’s website indicate the company’s efforts to develop an autonomous AI agent capable of performing complex tasks on the user’s behalf.

Since the breakout success of OpenClaw, autonomous AI agents have become increasingly popular, with companies such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, and SpaceXSI among those offering their own solutions.

The increasing popularity of these agents has put Apple under pressure to catch up, while the company has also introduced new restrictions on how third-party AI agents can access and control Macs.

Last month, Apple announced plans to tighten macOS privacy controls around Full Disk Access, with changes introduced in the macOS 27.3 beta that give users more granular control over which apps and information third-party AI agents can access.

Over at the App Store, Meta’s Muse has become one of the fastest-growing apps in US history, surpassing 10 million downloads in just 40 days, according to Sensor Tower, and spending weeks at the top of the charts. As of today, it sits at No. 2 among free apps, behind TikTok.

And while there are differences in how phone-based and computer-based agents operate, these systems can usually work together, coordinating tasks across devices and apps to accomplish increasingly complex goals.

Back to Bloomberg’s report, it notes Apple recently posted new job listings that offer a closer look at its plans to develop autonomous AI agents:

In one, Apple said it’s seeking a senior engineering manager for a proactive, agentic AI assistant. The system will write code, browse the web, control apps and navigate devices on a user’s behalf, according to the post.

One job listing, which is for “Senior Engineering Manager, Agentic AI – Proactive,” features the following summary:

“Imagine an AI agent that can use a computer the way a capable person does. It browses the web, works across apps, runs commands, writes and debugs code, and calls services, and it chooses the right tool for each step. It does all this privately and with the polish people expect from Apple. Our team is building the foundation for that future, and we’re looking for a senior engineering leader to make it real.”

The listing also notes that Apple is building agents that can “plan and carry out multi-step tasks across apps, browsers, command lines, code, and APIs, and they can coordinate specialized sub-agents along the way,” much like existing solutions from frontier AI labs.

Today’s report on the new job listings comes just days after Bloomberg reported that Apple wants to make Siri more like an autonomous AI agent, with the ability to proactively carry out tasks without requiring users to initiate every step. According to Mark Gurman, the company could introduce these capabilities as soon as next year.

With the new job listings, Apple has offered a more detailed look at its plans for autonomous AI agents, although the language suggests that development is still in its early stages.

Of course, given how quickly the technology is evolving, the landscape could look very different by the time Apple is ready to introduce its own solution next year, much like how the industry had already moved toward autonomous agents by the time Apple finally launched its long-awaited Siri AI overhaul.

To read Bloomberg’s report, follow this link.

彭博社报道称，苹果正在聘请工程师开发一款自主人工智能代理，能够代表用户浏览网页、编写代码和控制应用程序。以下是详细信息。

### 苹果正在开发可以编码、浏览网页等功能的人工智能代理

彭博社在今天发布的一份报告中指出，苹果网站上的新职位列表表明该公司正在努力开发能够代表用户执行复杂任务的自主人工智能代理。

自从 OpenClaw 取得突破性成功以来，自主人工智能代理变得越来越受欢迎，OpenAI、Anthropic、Meta 和 SpaceXSI 等公司都提供了自己的解决方案。

这些代理的日益普及让苹果面临着迎头赶上的压力，同时该公司还对第三方人工智能代理如何访问和控制 Mac 引入了新的限制。

上个月，苹果宣布计划加强围绕全磁盘访问的 macOS 隐私控制，macOS 27.3 Beta 中引入的更改使用户可以更精细地控制第三方 AI 代理可以访问哪些应用程序和信息。

在 App Store 中，Meta 的 Muse 已成为美国历史上增长最快的应用程序之一，根据 Sensor Tower 的数据，下载量在短短 40 天内就突破了 1000 万次，并且在排行榜上名列前茅数周。截至目前，它在免费应用程序中排名第二，仅次于 TikTok。

尽管基于电话和基于计算机的代理的操作方式存在差异，但这些系统通常可以协同工作，跨设备和应用程序协调任务，以实现日益复杂的目标。

回到彭博社的报告，它指出苹果公司最近发布了新的职位清单，可以更仔细地了解其开发自主人工智能代理的计划：

苹果公司在其中一份声明中表示，正在寻找一名高级工程经理来担任一名主动、代理的人工智能助理。该帖子称，该系统将代表用户编写代码、浏览网页、控制应用程序和导航设备。

一份职位清单是“高级工程经理，Agentic AI – 主动”，其摘要如下：

“想象一个人工智能代理，它可以像有能力的人一样使用计算机。它浏览网络、跨应用程序工作、运行命令、编写和调试代码以及​​调用服务，并为每一步选择正确的工具。它私下完成所有这一切，并以人们期望从苹果公司获得的完美方式完成。我们的团队正在为这个未来奠定基础，我们正在寻找一位高级工程领导者来实现这一目标。”

该清单还指出，苹果正在构建能够“跨应用程序、浏览器、命令行、代码和 API 规划和执行多步骤任务的代理，并且它们可以一路协调专门的子代理”，就像前沿人工智能实验室的现有解决方案一样。

今天关于新职位列表的报道是在彭博社报道苹果希望让 Siri 更像一个自主人工智能代理几天后发布的，它能够主动执行任务，而不需要用户启动每一步。据 Mark Gurman 称，该公司最早可能会在明年推出这些功能。
