These lasers can grab hold of each atom — like a pair of tweezers pinching a house fly — and carefully isolate it from the rest of the world.

As they do, each atom becomes a qubit. Dr. Lukin and his colleagues can perform calculations by manipulating these qubits, reading and writing information through subtle changes to their physical behavior. Much as a classical machine writes data into a bit by changing its charge, a quantum computer writes data into a qubit by shifting its quantum state.

The neutral atom technique is particularly effective because it gives researchers fine-grained control over each qubit. Because these atoms are neutral — because they are separated from the rest of the world — researchers can readily move them and manipulate them. Then, exploiting a phenomenon called the Rydberg blockade, individual atoms can be excited to high-energy states that let them trade information over long distances, without interacting with other atoms close by. This allows researchers to build the equivalent of circuits, capable of running complex calculations.

But arranging clouds of atoms into viable machines involves years of work. Dr. Lukin started working on the problem in the early 2000s, and the technology is only now reaching the point where it can start to realize its promise.

Dr. Lukin is also one of the founders and the chief scientist of the Cambridge start-up Quera, which aims to commercialize the technology. Increasingly, others are following his lead. In October, he attended the Nobel Symposium on Quantum Computing in Cape Town, where Jian-Wei Pan, widely known as China’s “father of quantum,” told him that no fewer than 20 Chinese companies were building machines using neutral atoms in the city of Shanghai alone.

“We have finally demonstrated all the elements that we need to get there,” Dr. Lukin said. “For the first time, the ideas that people had three or four decades ago are now within our line of sight.”

In Santa Barbara, Google’s quantum computer looks more like a Byzantine chandelier than a maze of lasers. This silver-and-gold lattice holds computer chips made from exotic metals that Dr. Neven and his team drop into massive refrigerators, cooling them to temperatures nearly 460 degrees below zero.

For years, these superconducting qubits looked like the surest path to a viable quantum computer. Like Amazon, IBM and others, Google strung together hundreds of qubits, showing that these quantum contraptions could perform increasingly complex calculations.

Google’s research indicates that a quantum computer is capable of the feats that scientists have promised for decades. But first, like all researchers in the field, they must solve the error correction problem.

Why is error correction so much harder in quantum computing than in traditional computing? Quantum systems are plagued by the famous “Heisenberg uncertainty principle,” which explains that with superposition — the state that quantum computers use to achieve their advantage over traditional machines — measuring one of the many properties of a particle will cause others to become unmeasurable. This means that merely looking at the information in an individual qubit causes it, in the terminology of quantum mechanics, to “collapse”: It slips back in the world of classical physics and transforms into an ordinary bit.

To deal with this problem, researchers design quantum computers that span far more qubits than they need for each calculation. That way, they can then read some qubits while leaving others undisturbed.

This is effective because quantum systems exhibit another strange property called “entanglement.” Through entanglement, one quantum system can influence the behavior of another, even when very far away — a phenomenon that Albert Einstein described as “spooky action at a distance.” Thanks to entanglement, researchers can glean information from a qubit by reading other qubits inside the same machine.

Part physical and part mathematical, this elaborate process is how researchers aim to crack error correction.

“It is intricate and complicated,” said Chris Langer, a fellow at Quantinuum, a company that is using a third quantum technique called “trapped ion” computing. “The basic idea is that you don’t measure the individual bits themselves. You measure information about the collection state.”

As far back as December 2024, Google said its machine had surpassed the “error correction threshold,” meaning that as its researchers increased the number of qubits, they could exponentially reduce the number of errors. Quantinuum recently showed similar progress with trapped ions — charged particles that researchers trap and isolate in much the same way they isolate neutral atoms. But other researchers argue that error correction could be most efficient with the neutral-atoms method, because it offers more freedom to rearrange the qubits, tinker with their behavior and make the process more efficient.

When you build a quantum computer from neutral atoms, you have more room to manipulate them, to move them from place to place, to reconfigure them into new logical circuits, said Adam Kaufman, a professor of physics at the University of Colorado, Boulder. That means you have more freedom to do error correction.

“You have a way of turning their interactions on and off,” Dr. Kaufman, who leads Google’s new team in Colorado, added. “This gives you the flexibility to realize a quantum circuit that you can rewire as you evolve your quantum computer over time.”

Dr. Neven still isn’t sure which method will reach the finish line first. Even if neutral atoms win the day, he believes, superconducting qubits will be more effective in the long run. Regardless, he has faith that Google is on track to solve the error correction problem in the coming years.

The result would be a machine that is nothing like today’s supercomputers. One long-feared consequence will be the breaking of today’s encryption technologies, which rely on huge factoring problems that quantum computers will, in theory, be able to solve; earlier this year, Google vowed to overhaul its encryption techniques before 2030.

“In 2022 or 2023, I would have a told you that the encryption scare was far out,” Dr. Neven said. “The timelines have come down.”

But such a machine will also provide a way of examining the world through the lens of quantum mechanics — helping to better understand biology and disease, the world around us and the ways we navigate that world. All are dependent on the strange behavior of the quantum realm.

If you want to build a computer that simulates the natural world and helps unlock its deepest mysteries, it must operate at a level that today’s computers do not, Dr. Feynman, the physicist, explained during a 1981 lecture. “Nature isn’t classical, dammit,” he said. “If you want to make a simulation of nature, you’d better make it quantum mechanical.”

But this year, a brand-new lab in Colorado — developing a totally different path to a quantum machine — has changed the narrative and accelerated the competition.
The most surprising part of all is the new lab’s funder: Google itself.

Forty-five years after scientists first floated the idea of a quantum computer, the race to build one has turned into a sprint, with many experts now believing that the first viable machine could arrive before the end of the decade or soon after. This new excitement has unlocked enormous investment, with tech giants like Amazon, IBM and Microsoft racing alongside Google. But not all companies are approaching this big idea in the same way, and it is increasingly unclear which method will prevail — which is why Google has decided to hedge its bets.

items.title_zh: 谷歌量子计算战略从单一路径转向多线对冲
items.summary_zh: 谷歌通过在科罗拉多州新建实验室，并行开发不同技术路线，以应对量子纠错技术难题与日益激烈的全球算力竞赛
items.article_content_zh:
近十年来，位于加利福尼亚州圣巴巴拉的谷歌实验室一直引领着全球竞赛，打造一台利用量子力学力量的计算机：量子力学是一种看不见的物理特性，可以让光、亚原子粒子和其他奇异物质以违背常识的方式运行。

但今年，科罗拉多州的一个全新实验室正在开发一条完全不同的量子机器路径，改变了叙事并加速了竞争。

最令人惊讶的是新实验室的资助者：谷歌本身。

在科学家首次提出量子计算机的想法四十五年后，建造量子计算机的竞赛已经变成了冲刺，许多专家现在相信第一台可行的机器可能会在本世纪末或不久之后问世。这种新的兴奋释放了巨额投资，亚马逊、IBM 和微软等科技巨头与谷歌并肩作战。今年 5 月，在中国承诺向量子研究投入超过 152 亿美元后，特朗普政府向众多美国初创企业和芯片制造商注入了 20 亿美元。

但并非所有公司都以同样的方式实现这一伟大想法，而且越来越不清楚哪种方法会占上风——这就是谷歌决定对冲其赌注的原因。

要理解这种扭曲，有必要回到 2014 年，当时德裔美国物理学家哈特穆特·内文 (Hartmut Neven) 在圣巴巴拉建立了谷歌实验室，并从几英里外的加州大学校园物理系聘请了 20 多名科学家。

与其他几家科技巨头一样，谷歌科学家选择使用一种称为超导量子位的技术来构建他们的量子计算机，该技术依赖于将金属冷却到极低的温度。在接下来的五年里，谷歌似乎领先于竞争对手。 2019年，该公司宣布其机器已经实现了“量子霸权”，即完成了传统计算无法解决的任务。不到四分钟，谷歌的机器就完成了现有超级计算机需要一万年才能完成的计算。

即使该领域取得了进展，创建可用量子计算机的一个主要障碍仍然存在：“纠错”问题。纠错是任何计算机的重要组成部分，可确保计算不会因热、电推理或其他物理力而产生偏差。我们每天使用的硅微芯片依赖于强大的电气设备和复杂的算法，可以在此类错误导致程序崩溃或数据损坏之前消除这些错误。

但传统计算和通信中使用的相同纠错方法不适用于量子计算。近年来，尽管内文博士的实验室在这个问题上取得了进展，但他开始看到竞争对手的研究使用了一种完全不同的量子计算——“中性原子”方法，其中涉及用光束捕获单个原子——这似乎使纠错变得更容易。

面对这项研究，内文博士和谷歌迈出了大胆的一步。今年四月，在对圣巴巴拉实验室进行了十年的投资之后，该公司在科罗拉多州博尔德开设了第二个竞争实验室，以探索中性原子技术。

“超导将帮助我们实现这一目标，但我想避免最后一刻，因为其他技术可能会与我们擦肩而过，即使这只是暂时的，”内文博士说。 “中性原子就有这样的机会。”

内文博士是该领域的杰出人物之一，他们现在认为强大的量子计算机即将到来。当它们确实出现时，它们不会取代我们每天依赖的计算机。但它们具有某些类型计算的设施可以改变我们生活的世界——帮助研究人员发现新药物、创造新材料并加速人工智能的进步等。

哈佛大学物理学教授米哈伊尔·卢金 (Mikhail Lukin) 表示，量子计算机“可以让你看到从未去过的宇宙角落”。

哈佛物理实验室位于马萨诸塞州剑桥大学校园北院，是一栋拥有 100 年历史的建筑。在它的地下室里，一扇门通向一个小房间，里面装满了电脑屏幕、示波器、键盘、浪涌保护器和老鼠巢般的电缆。

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 谷歌近期在科罗拉多州增设实验室，旨在并行推进超导量子位与另一新兴量子计算路径，以应对量子纠错这一核心技术瓶颈。此举不仅是对既有超导路线的策略性对冲，亦反映出在面对亚马逊、IBM及微软等竞争对手及全球资金角逐时，谷歌正加速从学术探索转向工程交付的阶段。

This strategic hedging reflects the escalating race against industry rivals like Amazon, IBM, and Microsoft as the competition shifts from theoretical milestones to practical engineering deployment.

items.title: NYU's Tristan Buckmaster and Anthropic's Levent Alpöge publish an AI-aided proof of Navier-Stokes blowup, saying it closes a loophole in OpenAI's solution (Peter Hall/Scientific American)
items.title_en: NYU's Tristan Buckmaster and Anthropic's Levent Alpöge publish an AI-aided proof of Navier-Stokes blowup, saying it closes a loophole in OpenAI's solution (Peter Hall/Scientific American)

items.author: Scientific American
items.article_content:
Two months after getting scooped by OpenAI, N.Y.U. professor Tristan Buckmaster and Anthropic employee Levent Alpöge are back with a new AI-aided proof of Navier-Stokes blowup

It looks like Anthropic employee Levent Alpöge was not satisfied with one blockbuster math proof today. Right after Alpöge’s announcement of a claimed proof of the Riemann hypothesis—math’s most famed open problem—has come the news that he and New York University professor Tristan Buckmaster believe they have closed a controversial loophole in OpenAI’s September solution of another million-dollar problem.

The Navier-Stokes equations, dating back to the early- to mid-19th century, model how fluids swirl and eddy. In September OpenAI proved that the equations “blow up,” meaning they occasionally claim that a fluid’s speed becomes infinite—something real fluids cannot do.

But while the September solution technically satisfied the conditions for the Clay Mathematics Institute’s $1-million prize, many experts were left unsatisfied with how it did so. OpenAI’s proof imagined an unrealistic, finely tuned force that “stirs” the liquid in just the right way to produce infinite velocity—an approach many consider a loophole in the wording of the problem.

The proof was also the subject of controversy because Buckmaster claimed it was a deliberate attempt on the part of OpenAI to scoop his and Alpöge’s progress on the problem. Now the pair claims to have taken back the lead on the problem, closing the loophole OpenAI left open and providing the solution to Navier-Stokes that experts have long sought.

On Mastodon at 8:37 A.M. EST this morning, Buckmaster posted a dense, artificial-intelligence-aided proof and noted that the write-up was unpolished because, “after last time,” he and Alpöge “couldn’t risk waiting” because of concerns over getting scooped. items.summary_zh: 纽约大学教授Buckmaster与Anthropic研究员Alpöge发布AI辅助证明，旨在修复OpenAI此前被指存在逻辑漏洞的流体力学解法
items.article_content_zh:
被 OpenAI 抢先两个月后，纽约大学 (N.Y.U.) Tristan Buckmaster 教授和 Anthropic 员工 Levent Alpöge 带着新的人工智能辅助的纳维-斯托克斯爆炸证明回来了

看来 Anthropic 员工 Levent Alpöge 对今天的一项重大数学证明并不满意。就在 Alpöge 宣布黎曼猜想（数学最著名的开放问题）的证明得到证明后，有消息称，他和纽约大学教授 Tristan Buckmaster 相信他们已经堵住了 OpenAI 9 月份解决另一个百万美元问题的一个有争议的漏洞。

纳维-斯托克斯方程可以追溯到 19 世纪早期到中期，它模拟了流体如何旋转和涡流。九月份，OpenAI 证明了这些方程“爆炸”，这意味着他们偶尔会声称流体的速度变得无限大——这是真实流体无法做到的。

尽管 9 月份的解决方案在技术上满足了克莱数学研究所 100 万美元奖金的条件，但许多专家对其实现方式并不满意。 OpenAI 的证明设想了一种不切实际的、经过微调的力，以正确的方式“搅拌”液体以产生无限的速度——许多人认为这种方法是问题措辞中的漏洞。

该证明也引起了争议，因为巴克马斯特声称这是 OpenAI 故意企图抢占他和 Alpöge 在该问题上的进展。巴克马斯特公开表示怀疑，该公司甚至在疯狂的竞赛中窃取了他的用户数据，以抢先一步。 （OpenAI 否认了犯规行为的指控，早期的报告表明该公司的证明可能采取了与 Buckmaster 和 Alpöge 的工作不同的途径来解决问题。）

现在，两人声称已经在这个问题上夺回了领先地位，堵住了 OpenAI 留下的漏洞，并为 Navier-Stokes 提供了专家们长期以来寻求的解决方案。

上午 8:37 在 Mastodon 上美国东部时间今天早上，巴克马斯特发布了一份密集的人工智能辅助证明，并指出该文章未经修饰，因为“在上次之后”，他和阿尔波格“不能冒险等待”，因为担心被抢先报道。仓促间，两人也没有公布成绩证明。他们在报告中声称很快就会发布。

伟大的科学新闻需要人类的专业知识、时间、努力和创造力。而且这需要花钱。这就是为什么我和《科学美国人》的记者希望您加入我们的社区。

items.title: Microsoft plans to retire its To Do app on June 30, 2027, offering migration to Planner for work and school accounts, but no replacement for personal accounts (Todd Bishop/GeekWire)
items.title_en: Microsoft plans to retire its To Do app on June 30, 2027, offering migration to Planner for work and school accounts, but no replacement for personal accounts (Todd Bishop/GeekWire)
items.author: GeekWire
items.article_content:
Microsoft acquired the popular Wunderlist app in 2015, shut it down in 2020 and told its loyal users that Microsoft To Do would be their new home. Now they’re being asked to pack up again.

Microsoft plans to retire the To Do apps on June 30, 2027, moving personal task management for work and school accounts into Planner, its team project-management app. Microsoft disclosed the change Wednesday in a long Planner blog post amid the company’s Ignite announcements, and Windows Latest flagged the change later that day.

The reaction was swift and mostly unhappy. Tom Warren of The Verge summed it up on X: “Microsoft is killing its great tasks app in favor of its worse tasks app.”

That’s not entirely fair to Planner, which is built for a different job. But it captures the gripe: To Do was simple, free and worked across Windows, Mac, iOS, Android and the web, and nothing Microsoft is offering replaces all of that.

The catch for personal users: Microsoft’s support page says the To Do apps are also retiring for personal Microsoft accounts, including paid Microsoft 365 Personal and Family subscribers, and that Planner isn’t available for those accounts. Microsoft hasn’t announced a replacement for them.

For work and school accounts, Microsoft says Planner “will be the destination for managing personal work tasks,” but “existing To Do tasks and lists will not migrate to Planner.” It says it will offer a way to export To Do data before the app shuts down.

Tony Redmond of Office365itpros, who tracks Microsoft 365 closely, cataloged the gaps: no file attachments on private Planner tasks, no equivalent for To Do’s list groups, no transfer of shared-list membership, assignments or permissions, and no native Planner apps for Windows or Mac.

He also noted the irony that Outlook’s old Exchange-based tasks will outlive To Do.

Why Microsoft is doing it: The company said putting individual and shared work on the same foundation lets it deliver more consistent features, and lets people connect their own tasks to Copilot and other AI agents. A new Planner agent, available with a Copilot add-on license, can take on tasks and generate status reports.

The Register’s Richard Speed put it less charitably, saying Microsoft had slipped the news into “this week’s Ignite AI puffery.”

Users weigh in: Brad Silverberg, the former Microsoft executive who led Windows 95 development and later became a Seattle venture investor, posted on X that he has used To Do daily, and Wunderlist before it.

“Very disappointed now,” he wrote, adding that he’s looking at TickTick and Todoist.

Similar posts piled up on LinkedIn from Microsoft 365 consultants and everyday users, some of them describing Planner as clunky by comparison.

Patrick Husting, a Seattle-area entrepreneur and software developer whose Ghostwriter add-in brought AI to Microsoft Office before Microsoft announced Microsoft 365 Copilot, offered on LinkedIn to maintain To Do for Microsoft for free.

Rivals smell an opportunity: Competitors wasted no time. TickTick posted a migration guide for To Do refugees. Todoist CEO Amir Salihefendic wrote on LinkedIn that the shutdown was “pretty unexpected” and pointed out that his app has outlasted competitors for 20 years.

The most pointed pitch came from Superlist, which called itself “the natural successor” and said it already has a tool for importing To Do lists. Wunderlist founder Christian Reber started the company in 2020.

Reber and his co-founders sold Wunderlist’s parent company, 6Wunderkinder, to Microsoft in 2015 for a reported $100 million to $200 million. In 2019, as Microsoft prepared to shut the app down, he publicly asked Satya Nadella to sell it back. Microsoft kept it, then retired it in favor of To Do.

Now some of those former Wunderlist users may end up back with the people who built it.

微软于 2015 年收购了广受欢迎的奇妙清单应用程序，并于 2020 年将其关闭，并告诉其忠实用户微软待办将成为他们的新家。现在他们又被要求收拾行李。

微软计划于 2027 年 6 月 30 日停用待办事项应用程序，将工作和学校帐户的个人任务管理转移到其团队项目管理应用程序 Planner 中。周三，微软在公司发布 Ignite 公告的同时，在一篇长篇 Planner 博客文章中披露了这一变化，Windows Last 也在当天晚些时候标记了这一变化。

人们的反应很快，而且大多是不高兴的。 The Verge 的 Tom Warren 对 X 进行了总结：“微软正在淘汰其优秀的任务应用程序，转而选择更糟糕的任务应用程序。”

这对于 Planner 来说并不完全公平，因为它是为不同的工作而构建的。但它抓住了人们的抱怨：To Do 简单、免费，并且可以在 Windows、Mac、iOS、Android 和网络上运行，而微软提供的任何产品都无法取代这一切。

个人用户面临的问题：微软的支持页面称，个人微软帐户的待办事项应用程序也将停用，包括付费的 Microsoft 365 个人和家庭订阅者，并且 Planner 不适用于这些帐户。微软尚未宣布它们的替代品。

对于工作和学校帐户，微软表示 Planner“将成为管理个人工作任务的目的地”，但“现有的待办事项和列表不会迁移到 Planner。”它表示它将提供一种在应用程序关闭之前导出待办事项数据的方法。

Office365itpros 的托尼·雷蒙德 (Tony Redmond) 密切跟踪 Microsoft 365，他对这些差距进行了分类：私人 Planner 任务上没有文件附件，待办事项列表组没有等效项，没有共享列表成员身份、分配或权限的传输，并且没有适用于 Windows 或 Mac 的本机 Planner 应用程序。

他还指出具有讽刺意味的是，Outlook 旧的基于 Exchange 的任务将比待办事项更长寿。

微软这样做的原因：该公司表示，将个人和共享工作放在同一基础上可以提供更一致的功能，并让人们将自己的任务连接到 Copilot 和其他人工智能代理。带有 Copilot 附加许可证的新 Planner 代理可以承担任务并生成状态报告。

The Register 的理查德·斯皮德 (Richard Speed) 的说法就不那么仁慈了，他说微软已经将这一消息塞进了“本周的 Ignite AI 吹嘘”中。

用户发表意见：领导 Windows 95 开发、后来成为西雅图风险投资人的微软前高管布拉德·西尔弗伯格 (Brad Silverberg) 在 X 上发帖称，他曾使用过“待办事项”和之前的奇妙清单。

“现在非常失望，”他写道，并补充说他正在考虑 TickTick 和 Todoist。

Microsoft 365 顾问和日常用户在 LinkedIn 上发布了类似的帖子，其中一些人认为相比之下，Planner 很笨重。

Patrick Husting 是一位西雅图地区的企业家和软件开发人员，他的 Ghostwriter 插件在 Microsoft 发布 Microsoft 365 Copilot 之前将 AI 引入了 Microsoft Office，并在 LinkedIn 上免费提供 Microsoft 待办事项维护服务。
fact_bullets_zh: 【核心事件】微软公司（Microsoft）在Microsoft Ignite年度技术大会：宣布停用To Do应用，并将其工作负载整合至Planner
【起因与机理】旨在将个人与团队任务统一底层架构，以适配Copilot及AI智能体调度
【核心事实细节】微软将于2027年6月30日终止To Do应用服务。
【各方立场与态度】此次整合旨在将个人任务纳入Copilot智能体调度框架。
fact_bullets_en: [Core Event] Microsoft (Microsoft Ignite Conference): Plan to deprecate To Do and consolidate workloads into Planner
[Root Cause & Mechanism] To unify task management architecture for Copilot and AI agent integration
[Key Metrics] Reber and his co-founders sold Wunderlist’s parent company, 6Wunderkinder, to Microsoft in 2015 for a reported $100 million to $200 million.
[Key Position & Outlook] Consolidation aims to integrate task management into Copilot AI agent ecosystem.

items.title: Industry insiders say new US export rules affect a broader range of chips, including SoCs used in consumer electronics, extending beyond advanced AI chips (Cheng Ting-Fang/Nikkei Asia)
items.title_en: Industry insiders say new US export rules affect a broader range of chips, including SoCs used in consumer electronics, extending beyond advanced AI chips (Cheng Ting-Fang/Nikkei Asia)

items.author: Nikkei Asia
items.article_content:
TAIPEI -- Tighter U.S. export controls introduced Thursday are having a far broader impact on the global semiconductor supply chain than initially expected, extending beyond advanced AI chips to those used in everyday mobile and consumer applications and affecting developers beyond China, multiple industry executives told Nikkei Asia.

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co., the world's largest contract chipmaker, has put shipments to several Chinese and non-Chinese chip developers on hold as it reviews compliance with the stricter regulations, sources briefed on the matter said.

The new rules, announced Monday by the U.S. Commerce Department, further restrict foundries' ability to serve Chinese chip developers, including Xiaomi, as well as customers in Vietnam, Malaysia, Singapore and other countries. They threaten emerging semiconductor ambitions across Asia and disrupt the global chip supply chain on a much wider scale than previously, Nikkei Asia has learned.

Contract chipmakers must now assume that all chips manufactured using process technologies more advanced than the 14- or 16-nanometer nodes first mass-produced by TSMC and Samsung Electronics about a decade ago are subject to export restrictions, unless their developers are on a U.S. government whitelist. The rules could therefore affect a broad range of chips, including those used in autonomous driving, connectivity and smartphones, rather than just high-performance processors for data center servers.

briefed on the matter said the new rules effectively required Chinese chip developers to apply for export licenses, even for chips designed for consumer electronics and automotive applications. Some key TSMC clients, including Xiaomi, which is developing its own mobile processors, and many Chinese automotive chip developers, are affected, two sources told Nikkei Asia.

"The new rule is very strict this time, and the affecting scope is far beyond only chips for data centers but covers smartphone processors, autonomous driving and other types of chips for consumer electronics as well as others if they are using nodes that are 14-nanometer or 16-nanometer or more advanced tech," a source said.

"The move would delay shipments to many chip developers worldwide before they can clear compliance and hit many emerging startups in many Asian nations."

Previous U.S. restrictions primarily targeted data center and high-performance computing chips that met certain thresholds and used advanced packaging technologies required for AI computing.

However, the latest restrictions could also deal a blow to emerging chip design hubs across Asia that are seeking to build their own chip development ecosystems. These include Vietnam and Malaysia, both of which have ambitions to develop domestic chip design capabilities.

As part of the latest restrictions, the U.S. has also said global contract chipmakers and chip packaging service providers need to do more to verify the final destinations of the chips.

The export controls aim to close loopholes that have allowed Chinese chip developers and other entities to continue accessing the world's leading semiconductor supply chains and advanced American technologies. The same controls also require data centers in Malaysia, Singapore, and Thailand to apply for U.S. licenses.

TSMC said it was aware of the new regulations and would comply as applicable. Xiaomi did not immediately respond to Nikkei Asia's request for comment.

The Financial Times first reported TSMC and Samsung Electronics had suspended some chip shipments to Chinese customers.

items.article_content_zh:
台北——多位行业高管告诉《日经亚洲》，美国周四实施的更严格的出口管制对全球半导体供应链的影响比最初预期的要广泛得多，不仅限于先进的人工智能芯片，还扩展到日常移动和消费应用中使用的芯片，并影响到中国以外的开发商。

全球最大的代工芯片制造商台积电已暂停向多家中国和非中国芯片开发商发货，以审查是否遵守更严格的规定。

美国商务部周一宣布的新规定进一步限制了代工厂为包括小米在内的中国芯片开发商以及越南、马来西亚、新加坡和其他国家的客户提供服务的能力。日经亚洲获悉，它们威胁到整个亚洲新兴的半导体雄心，并比以前更广泛地扰乱全球芯片供应链。

合同芯片制造商现在必须假设，所有使用比台积电和三星电子大约十年前首次大规模生产的 14 或 16 纳米节点更先进的工艺技术制造的芯片都受到出口限制，除非其开发商列入美国政府白名单。因此，这些规则可能会影响广泛的芯片，包括用于自动驾驶、连接和智能手机的芯片，而不仅仅是数据中心服务器的高性能处理器。

了解此事的消息人士称，新规定实际上要求中国芯片开发商申请出口许可证，即使是为消费电子和汽车应用设计的芯片。两位消息人士告诉《日经亚洲》，台积电的一些主要客户，包括正在开发自己的移动处理器的小米，以及许多中国汽车芯片开发商，都受到了影响。

消息人士称：“这次新规定非常严格，影响范围远远超出了数据中心芯片的范围，还包括智能手机处理器、自动驾驶和其他类型的消费电子芯片，以及其他使用14纳米、16纳米或更先进技术节点的芯片。”

“此举将推迟向全球许多芯片开发商发货，然后他们才能通过合规性并打击许多亚洲国家的许多新兴初创公司。”

美国此前的限制主要针对数据中心和满足一定门槛并使用人工智能计算所需的先进封装技术的高性能计算芯片。

然而，最新的限制也可能对亚洲各地正在寻求建立自己的芯片开发生态系统的新兴芯片设计中心造成打击。其中包括越南和马来西亚，这两个国家都有发展国内芯片设计能力的雄心。

作为最新限制的一部分，美国还表示，全球合约芯片制造商和芯片封装服务提供商需要采取更多措施来验证芯片的最终目的地。

出口管制旨在弥补漏洞，这些漏洞使中国芯片开发商和其他实体能够继续获得世界领先的半导体供应链和先进的美国技术。同样的控制还要求马来西亚、新加坡和泰国的数据中心申请美国许可证。

台积电表示已了解新规定，并将酌情遵守。小米没有立即回应日经亚洲的置评请求。

英国《金融时报》首先报道称，台积电和三星电子已暂停向中国客户发货部分芯片。

【起因与机理】旨在通过更广泛的制程节点锁定，阻断全球先进代工产能向目标国家转移
【关键数据与实测】管制门槛由高性能AI芯片下调至14/16纳米全类芯片。
【行业影响与走向】产业链影响从AI中心延伸至智能手机及自动驾驶等消费领域。

[Key Metrics] Export control threshold lowered from AI-specific chips to all 14/16nm nodes.
[Industry Impact & Outlook] Supply chain impact spreads from AI data centers to smartphone and automotive sectors.

items.title: Ubisoft launches Motherbrain, a subsidiary focused on developing "smart NPCs with memory and AI game masters that manage large-scale systemic worlds" (Sophie McEvoy/GamesIndustry.biz)
items.title_en: Ubisoft launches Motherbrain, a subsidiary focused on developing "smart NPCs with memory and AI game masters that manage large-scale systemic worlds" (Sophie McEvoy/GamesIndustry.biz)
items.author: GamesIndustry.biz
items.article_content:
Ubisoft has launched Motherbrain, a dedicated subsidiary focused on developing proprietary generative AI technology for gameplay.

Announced in the firm's H1 financial results published yesterday, Motherbrain consists of the team behind Ubisoft's generative AI project Teammates, which began playtesting last year.

Ubisoft said the subsidiary is currently focused on developing "smart NPCs with memory and AI game masters that manage large-scale systemic worlds."

"[Motherbrain] aims to serve creators globally, both within Ubisoft’s Creative House ecosystem and beyond, and form partnerships with selected technology actors."

Ubisoft CEO Yves Guillemot added that Motherbrain aimed to "empower creators and open up new possibilities for richer, more immersive and engaging player experiences."

The launch of Motherbrain comes as Ubisoft laid off 166 staff at its Montreal and Quebec studios. Production and support roles were eliminated "to ensure our resources are aligned with current production priorities and business needs."

As GamesIndustry.biz understands, the cuts accounted for less than 4% of the studios' total headcount and included members of Vantage Studios.

"As our portfolio evolves, our production needs are changing, requiring us to adjust the size of some teams to ensure our resources are aligned with current production priorities and business needs," said Ubisoft.

items.article_content_zh:
育碧推出了 Motherbrain，这是一家专注于开发专有的游戏生成人工智能技术的子公司。

该公司在昨天发布的上半年财务业绩中宣布，Motherbrain 由育碧生成式人工智能项目 Teammates 背后的团队组成，该项目于去年开始进行游戏测试。

育碧表示，该子公司目前专注于开发“具有记忆能力的智能 NPC 和管理大规模系统世界的人工智能游戏大师”。

“[Motherbrain] 旨在为育碧 Creative House 生态系统内外的全球创作者提供服务，并与选定的技术参与者建立合作伙伴关系。”

育碧首席执行官 Yves Guillemot 补充道，Motherbrain 的目标是“为创作者赋能，并为更丰富、更身临其境和更具吸引力的玩家体验开辟新的可能性”。

《Motherbrain》推出之际，育碧解雇了蒙特利尔和魁北克工作室的 166 名员工。生产和支持角色被取消，“以确保我们的资源与当前的生产优先事项和业务需求保持一致。”

据GamesIndustry.biz了解，裁员人数占工作室总人数的不到4%，其中包括Vantage Studios的成员。

育碧表示：“随着我们产品组合的发展，我们的制作需求也在发生变化，这要求我们调整一些团队的规模，以确保我们的资源与当前的制作优先事项和业务需求保持一致。”

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 育碧在发布上半年财务报告期间正式成立Motherbrain子公司，整合原Teammates生成式AI研发团队。该机构致力于构建具备记忆能力的NPC与负责大规模动态世界逻辑的AI游戏主脑，并将通过生态协同服务内部创意团队及外部技术合作伙伴。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Ubisoft has launched its subsidiary Motherbrain, integrating the generative AI team behind the Teammates project to develop smart NPCs with long-term memory and autonomous systemic world-management engines. The subsidiary intends to provide technical support for internal Creative House workflows while seeking external strategic partnerships.

items.title: Sources: the FBI is investigating an apparent breach of its NCIC database, which is used by law enforcement to share info on warrants and background checks (Evan Perez/CNN)
items.title_en: Sources: the FBI is investigating an apparent breach of its NCIC database, which is used by law enforcement to share info on warrants and background checks (Evan Perez/CNN)

inline_images.caption: Evan Perez
inline_images.alt: Evan Perez

inline_images.caption: A seal reading
inline_images.alt: A seal reading

items.author: CNN
items.article_content:
The FBI is investigating an apparent breach of its nationwide criminal information database that serves as a lifeline between federal, state and local law enforcement, two people briefed on the investigation said. The intrusion of the National Crime Information Center by apparent hackers is the second such breach in recent months.

The NCIC database is used by law enforcement nationwide to share information on warrants and background checks. The discovery of the latest intrusion in recent days comes as the Trump administration has sought to assuage public concern about the nation’s cybersecurity amid a series of high profile outages affecting banks, the National Security Agency and the FAA’s air traffic control system.

The FBI didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment. On Thursday, after bureau officials learned of the latest cybersecurity incident, FBI Director Kash Patel appeared on Fox News to tout the FBI’s cybersecurity work. Patel used the appearance to discuss an operation completed months ago aimed at urging companies to update their systems and prevent hackers from getting to their sensitive data.

Patel referred to Operation Winter Shield as if it was still in the works, and touted the current administration for making updates to key systems to protect the nation’s critical infrastructure. “Other administrations could have made these updates, but they didn’t,” he said. “We are staying ahead of the curve and making up for lost time.” Prior hacks A September attack by a group called ShinyHunters targeted sensitive employee personal data from an FBI jobs website.

A Canadian cybersecurity researcher and author has been arrested and faces charges related to the ShinyHunters breach. After the ShinyHunters breach, some FBI employees felt left in the dark about whether they were affected by the data theft and underwhelmed by the security resources being offered to victims, CNN previously reported.

In an earlier breach in 2023, hackers breached a computer system the FBI’s New York field office used in child sexual exploitation investigations, including a system used to store images related to the Jeffrey Epstein probe, CNN previously reported. CNN’s Sean Lyngaas contributed to this report.

items.summary_en: The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) is investigating a breach of its National Crime Information Center (NCIC) database. This system serves as a central hub for federal, state, and local law enforcement to share warrants and background check information, triggering intense scrutiny over the nation's critical infrastructure defense capabilities.

items.summary_zh: FBI正调查NCIC数据库入侵事件，该系统负责全美执法机构的逮捕令和背景审查信息共享

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 美国联邦调查局（FBI）现正对全国犯罪信息中心（NCIC）数据库的入侵事件展开调查。该数据库是连接联邦、州及地方执法机构的核心枢纽，用于共享逮捕令及背景审查信息，此次入侵已引起政府对国家关键基础设施网络防御能力的深度关注。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) is investigating a breach of its National Crime Information Center (NCIC) database. This system serves as a central hub for federal, state, and local law enforcement to share warrants and background check information, triggering intense scrutiny over the nation's critical infrastructure defense capabilities.

elements_zh.why: 作为执法部门信息共享核心，系统安全性的丧失威胁到全美司法与执法联动效能

elements_en.what: Investigating a serious system intrusion
elements_en.why: As a central hub for law enforcement, its compromise threatens judicial and operational coordination nationwide

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 作为美国执法体系的底层数字骨干，NCIC多次遭到入侵暴露出关键基础设施在横向权限管理与威胁检测上的严重短板。此类针对执法核心数据库的渗透，不仅是单纯的数据泄露，更可能造成司法流程干扰与针对执法人员的信息对抗危机。
ai_analysis.insight_en: As the digital backbone of the U.S. law enforcement system, repeated intrusions into the NCIC reveal critical weaknesses in lateral access management and threat detection. Such penetration of core databases transcends simple data theft, risking disruption to judicial processes and operational security for law enforcement personnel.

items.article_content_zh:
两名了解调查情况的人士表示，联邦调查局正在调查其全国犯罪信息数据库明显遭到破坏的事件，该数据库是联邦、州和地方执法部门之间的生命线。明显的黑客入侵国家犯罪信息中心是近几个月来第二起此类违规事件。

NCIC 数据库被全国执法部门用来共享逮捕令和背景调查的信息。最近几天发现最新的入侵事件之际，特朗普政府试图缓解公众对国家网络安全的担忧，因为一系列引人注目的网络中断影响了银行、国家安全局和美国联邦航空局的空中交通管制系统。

联邦调查局没有立即回应置评请求。周四，在联邦调查局官员获悉最新的网络安全事件后，联邦调查局局长卡什·帕特尔出现在福克斯新闻节目中，宣传联邦调查局的网络安全工作。帕特尔借此机会讨论了几个月前完成的一项行动，旨在敦促公司更新其系统并防止黑客获取其敏感数据。

帕特尔提到“冬季盾牌行动”时就好像它仍在进行中一样，并称赞现任政府对关键系统进行了更新以保护国家的关键基础设施。 “其他政府本可以进行这些更新，但他们没有，”他说。 “我们保持领先地位并弥补失去的时间。”之前的黑客攻击 一个名为 ShinyHunters 的组织 9 月份发起的攻击针对的是 FBI 招聘网站上的敏感员工个人数据。

一名加拿大网络安全研究人员和作家已被捕，并面临与 ShinyHunters 数据泄露相关的指控。据美国有线电视新闻网 (CNN) 此前报道，在 ShinyHunters 事件发生后，一些联邦调查局 (FBI) 员工对自己是否受到数据盗窃的影响一无所知，并对向受害者提供的安全资源感到失望。

据美国有线电视新闻网 (CNN) 此前报道，在 2023 年早些时候的一次泄露中，黑客入侵了联邦调查局纽约办事处用于儿童性剥削调查的计算机系统，其中包括用于存储与杰弗里·爱泼斯坦调查相关的图像的系统。美国有线电视新闻网 (CNN) 的肖恩·林格斯 (Sean Lyngaas) 对本报告做出了贡献。

items.author: George Steer
items.article_content:
US tech stocks plunged into a bear market in their worst week since the Covid-19 outbreak shook the global economy as fears of a slowdown in the AI investment boom triggered a wave of selling on Wall Street.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 tumbled 5.6 per cent on Friday, taking its loss for the week to 10.4 per cent, its worst run in more than six years. The index has dropped 20 per cent from its intraday high on October 6, the threshold typically associated with bear market territory.

The S&P 500 fell 3.7 per cent, taking its loss since an October peak to more than 10 per cent. Investors fled into haven assets, sending yields on 10-year Treasuries down 0.1 percentage points to 4.94 per cent.

Trading was frantic on Friday, with selling accelerating into the close and AI stocks sustaining the steepest losses. The Vix index — known as Wall Street’s “fear gauge” — soared to 40 points, its highest level since April 2025.

The rout is the latest sign of how enthusiasm over AI has rapidly morphed into deep angst over the huge amount of spending and borrowing by Big Tech companies to finance investments in chips and data centres.

Anthropic had surged 17 per cent on its market debut on Thursday after raising a record $120bn in its initial public offering and a concurrent private placement but dropped 9.1 per cent on Friday.

The AI lab’s listing had been billed as a defining moment for the AI industry and global markets, giving investors the chance to gain exposure to one of the world’s leading developers of the technology. But those hopes unravelled on Friday as the group’s shares fell back close to its listing price.

“It looks like Armageddon out there,” the chief investment officer of a US hedge fund told the FT, adding that he had decided against buying more Anthropic stock as Friday’s sell-off accelerated.

Nvidia also tumbled 14 per cent as the scandal that has engulfed the company at the heart of the AI fervour deepened. The Securities and Exchange Commission is probing Nvidia’s accounting, according to a person familiar with the matter. The news was first reported by Reuters.

The chip giant is already facing congressional hearings, and President Donald Trump has said the FBI is investigating the circumstances around ousted chief executive Jensen Huang’s affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy.

The SEC did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Nvidia declined to comment. The stock has fallen almost 50 per cent since early October, erasing $2.8tn of market value.

“Jensen and Nvidia are the embodiment of the AI build-out. To see that things were less than forthright has shaken everyone’s confidence,” said Mike O’Rourke at Jones Trading.

The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index of US chip stocks on Friday dropped 10.7 per cent, taking its decline since a peak in June to 43 per cent. “The AI bubble has been deflating for months,” O’Rourke added.

Shares in Sandisk and Western Digital dropped 16 per cent and 12 per cent, respectively. Broadcom and Marvell fell 12 per cent and Micron shed 14 per cent.

The Democrats’ resounding US midterm elections victory earlier this month has “absolutely” contributed to the latest stock market sell-off, according to Jim Caron, chief investment officer of portfolio solutions at Morgan Stanley Investment Management.

“All of the spending, AI capex-related, which we know generated this growth — will that now be curtailed by policies, various investigations that we expect to start to come up in January and get announced when the new Congress takes their seats? The market is trying to figure this out,” Caron said.

Volatility across stocks spread to other financial assets, with bitcoin sliding below $60,000 on Friday for the first time since July.

Gold offered little shelter. Spot prices lost almost 3 per cent to about $3,522 a troy ounce, the lowest level in more than a year.

Traders in the Treasury futures market, meanwhile, pulled back expectations of rate rises from the Federal Reserve as the equity market continued to slide.

Investors are no longer fully pricing in a quarter-point increase at the Fed’s meeting in December, days after governor Christopher Waller speculated that the central bank could deliver a jumbo 0.5 percentage point increase.

Hedge funds, pension funds and retail investors all appear to be dumping stocks on intensifying fears about higher interest rates and a slowing data centre build-out, according to Nomura strategists.

“The equity market has been focused on the Nvidia scandal [but] now we have a Fed primed to hike [rates] and commodities pricing in recession risk,” said Alex Witten, Nomura’s co-head of Americas equities.

items.title: Cops Are Pushing Extremely Corny ‘Grand Theft Auto 6’ Slop
items.title_en: Cops Are Pushing Extremely Corny ‘Grand Theft Auto 6’ Slop
items.author: Miles Klee
items.article_content:
Listening to the in-game radio stations while you cruise around in Grand Theft Auto VI, you might hear a recruitment ad for the Vice City Police Department, which makes no secret of the kind of maladjusted psychos it's looking for.

“Have you always dreamed of abusing your power without consequence?” one spot begins. “Well, now you can, when you join the Vice City Police Department, VCPD. You’ll have fun learning the ins and outs of applying excessive force.” The commercial goes on to suggest that cadets will be trained in racial profiling and planting evidence.

Given that blistering analysis of American law enforcement, you might imagine that actual cops aren’t big fans of the latest GTA title, which was released after a 13-year wait on Thursday. Yet as millions of gamers have started to explore every stash house and back alley in the sun-drenched wilderness of a fictionalized South Florida, even police departments have attempted to exploit this monocultural mania to elevate their public messaging or recruit new officers.

It’s a curious strategy given that the series rewards theft and drug dealing while enticing you to run over pedestrians, but evidently the mere presence of law enforcement in the games (as the primary antagonists, mind you) was enough to inspire waves of AI slop celebrating the thin blue line.

An Instagram channel of the San Diego Police Department, for example, on Thursday posted an AI-generated image of an SDPD cruiser set against a sunset over the San Diego Bay. Its neon pinks and purples match the saturated aesthetic of GTA, and in case there was any doubt what the department was going for, the nonsensical phrase “Join San Diego PD VI” appears at the top. “Want to drive a police car, we can make that happen!” reads the caption. “Apply Now!”

Another police department in Washington state shared GTA-like imagery on its Instagram page, encouraging viewers to try “the real-life version” of GTA VI by pursuing a career in law enforcement. “No cheat codes,” the caption advertised. “No respawns. Just real people, real challenges, and a career that makes a difference.” A wave of self-serious GTA slop also flooded the feeds of police departments in Canada, from Edmonton to Toronto—though the Calgary Police Service tried something more lighthearted by having one of their traffic officers react to clips of dangerous and illegal driving maneuvers in the game.

Among police departments that were not seeking to add to their ranks through GTA VI fever, many posted content aimed at reminding people that laws exist in real life. “Keep It In The Game VI,” advised a typical post on the Instagram account of the Glendale Police Department in California, complete with a GTA-fied police cruiser and view of the city. “Follow posted speed limits, respect the law, and keep your wanted level at ZERO!” the caption warned. The Denver Police Department, in similarly scolding fashion, informed followers: “Grand theft auto is still illegal.”

The communications teams for these agencies should have perhaps reconsidered trying to farm engagement and clout from the massive success of GTA VI. As many commenters are noting, the game portrays cops as corrupt and quick to violence. Players have discovered that the Vice City squad will brutalize you if you start filming them during a questionable arrest. One clip showed a cop pulling his weapon on a character who had done nothing worse than stand in the street to take a selfie.

A certain dose of this authoritarian cruelty ought to appeal to the right-wing cranks upset that GTA VI is too “woke” when it comes to gender, race, and politics overall. It’s a little different when the most visible villains of the game are choosing to overlook its vicious take on their profession in order to spam epic social media posts.

Fox News, just for comparison, dutifully took the tired law-and-order line on GTA VI, with talking heads aghast at kids’ exposure to virtual gun violence (never mind actual gun deaths in the US) and an atmosphere of moral depravity. Elon Musk famously declared that he couldn’t play GTA games because they compelled you to shoot cops.

Both stances, however insincere, suggest a modicum of regard for law enforcement that the police departments themselves immediately jettisoned in favor of GTA cringe. They of course won’t win any cool points for it, but at least this way they can pretend to connect with the general population.

More baffling still is that the Russian army has generated its own GTA VI recruitment ads to blast out on its Telegram channel, and NATO has trumpeted its defensive security alliance with military-industrial GTA sludge, boasting that “even the best gamers would have a challenge” eluding fighter jets and submarines. Trying to parse Vice President JD Vance’s depiction of a Trumpian “golden age” with GTA graphics is a fool’s errand. In the most dystopian development of all, a US Army battalion in Georgia granted 43 eligible soldiers four days off to play the new GTA in return for reenlisting for another two years of service.

What do any of these institutions or their missions have to do with a video game where you rob convenience stores in flip-flops? Doesn’t matter. When the zeitgeist is this all-consuming, you fire up ChatGPT and find an angle, no matter how confusing. Surely someone, somewhere, will be tricked into thinking you have anything to do with it.

Listening to the in-game radio stations while you cruise around in Grand Theft Auto VI, you might hear a recruitment ad for the Vice City Police Department, which makes no secret of the kind of maladjusted psychos it's looking for.

“Have you always dreamed of abusing your power without consequence?” one spot begins. “Well, now you can, when you join the Vice City Police Department, VCPD. You’ll have fun learning the ins and outs of applying excessive force.” The commercial goes on to suggest that cadets will be trained in racial profiling and planting evidence.

Given that blistering analysis of American law enforcement, you might imagine that actual cops aren’t big fans of the latest GTA title, which was released after a 13-year wait on Thursday. Yet as millions of gamers have started to explore every stash house and back alley in the sun-drenched wilderness of a fictionalized South Florida, even police departments have attempted to exploit this monocultural mania to elevate their public messaging or recruit new officers.

It’s a curious strategy given that the series rewards theft and drug dealing while enticing you to run over pedestrians, but evidently the mere presence of law enforcement in the games (as the primary antagonists, mind you) was enough to inspire waves of AI slop celebrating the thin blue line.

An Instagram channel of the San Diego Police Department, for example, on Thursday posted an AI-generated image of an SDPD cruiser set against a sunset over the San Diego Bay. Its neon pinks and purples match the saturated aesthetic of GTA, and in case there was any doubt what the department was going for, the nonsensical phrase “Join San Diego PD VI” appears at the top. “Want to drive a police car, we can make that happen!” reads the caption. “Apply Now!”

Another police department in Washington state shared GTA-like imagery on its Instagram page, encouraging viewers to try “the real-life version” of GTA VI by pursuing a career in law enforcement. “No cheat codes,” the caption advertised. “No respawns. Just real people, real challenges, and a career that makes a difference.” A wave of self-serious GTA slop also flooded the feeds of police departments in Canada, from Edmonton to Toronto—though the Calgary Police Service tried something more lighthearted by having one of their traffic officers react to clips of dangerous and illegal driving maneuvers in the game.

Among police departments that were not seeking to add to their ranks through GTA VI fever, many posted content aimed at reminding people that laws exist in real life. “Keep It In The Game VI,” advised a typical post on the Instagram account of the Glendale Police Department in California, complete with a GTA-fied police cruiser and view of the city. “Follow posted speed limits, respect the law, and keep your wanted level at ZERO!” the caption warned. The Denver Police Department, in similarly scolding fashion, informed followers: “Grand theft auto is still illegal.”

The communications teams for these agencies should have perhaps reconsidered trying to farm engagement and clout from the massive success of GTA VI. As many commenters are noting, the game portrays cops as corrupt and quick to violence. Players have discovered that the Vice City squad will brutalize you if you start filming them during a questionable arrest. One clip showed a cop pulling his weapon on a character who had done nothing worse than stand in the street to take a selfie.

A certain dose of this authoritarian cruelty ought to appeal to the right-wing cranks upset that GTA VI is too “woke” when it comes to gender, race, and politics overall. It’s a little different when the most visible villains of the game are choosing to overlook its vicious take on their profession in order to spam epic social media posts.

Fox News, just for comparison, dutifully took the tired law-and-order line on GTA VI, with talking heads aghast at kids’ exposure to virtual gun violence (never mind actual gun deaths in the US) and an atmosphere of moral depravity. Elon Musk famously declared that he couldn’t play GTA games because they compelled you to shoot cops.

Both stances, however insincere, suggest a modicum of regard for law enforcement that the police departments themselves immediately jettisoned in favor of GTA cringe. They of course won’t win any cool points for it, but at least this way they can pretend to connect with the general population.

More baffling still is that the Russian army has generated its own GTA VI recruitment ads to blast out on its Telegram channel, and NATO has trumpeted its defensive security alliance with military-industrial GTA sludge, boasting that “even the best gamers would have a challenge” eluding fighter jets and submarines. Trying to parse Vice President JD Vance’s depiction of a Trumpian “golden age” with GTA graphics is a fool’s errand. In the most dystopian development of all, a US Army battalion in Georgia granted 43 eligible soldiers four days off to play the new GTA in return for reenlisting for another two years of service.

What do any of these institutions or their missions have to do with a video game where you rob convenience stores in flip-flops? Doesn’t matter. When the zeitgeist is this all-consuming, you fire up ChatGPT and find an angle, no matter how confusing. Surely someone, somewhere, will be tricked into thinking you have anything to do with it.

items.summary_zh: 美国加州、华盛顿州及加拿大等地警方利用《GTA VI》发行热度，通过AI生成带有游戏风格的征兵广告进行招募

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 近期随着《侠盗猎车手6》（GTA VI）正式发售，圣地亚哥警察局（SDPD）及华盛顿州、加拿大等地的执法部门在Instagram等平台发布大量AI生成的同风格图像，以此诱导受众应聘警务职位。此举试图利用游戏引发的文化共鸣，将执法职业伪装成现实版的“任务挑战”进行社会宣传。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Following the release of Grand Theft Auto VI, police departments including the San Diego Police Department (SDPD) and agencies in Washington and Canada are utilizing AI-generated imagery mimicking the game’s aesthetic for recruitment campaigns. These departments are attempting to leverage the title's cultural dominance to rebrand police careers as real-world equivalents of the game's high-stakes missions.

elements_en.who: San Diego Police Department (SDPD) and regional police agencies in Washington and Canada
elements_en.what: Posting AI-generated, GTA-themed recruitment ads for police positions

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 公共部门对生成式AI的滥用反映了其在传播策略上的低门槛内卷，缺乏对品牌叙事冲突的审慎评估。将执法机关与嘲讽现实执法的游戏IP深度绑定，本质上暴露了政府机构在数字舆论场中试图通过蹭热点来缓解长期招募困境的焦虑。
ai_analysis.insight_en: The appropriation of pop-culture assets by law enforcement via generative AI reflects a tactical desperation to bridge recruitment gaps, ignoring the severe brand dissonance inherent in associating with an anti-establishment IP. This strategy underscores the lack of sophisticated digital communication governance within public institutions when chasing viral trends.

items.article_content_zh:
当你在《侠盗猎车手 6》中四处巡游时，收听游戏中的广播电台，你可能会听到罪恶城警察局的招聘广告，其中毫不掩饰其正在寻找的那种不适应的精神病患者。

“你是否一直梦想着滥用权力而不承担任何后果？”一个点开始。 “好吧，现在你可以了，当你加入副城警察局 VCPD 时。你会很高兴了解过度使用武力的来龙去脉。”该广告接着建议学员将接受种族定性和种植证据方面的培训。

考虑到对美国执法部门的激烈分析，你可能会认为，真正的警察并不是最新款 GTA 游戏的忠实粉丝，这款游戏在等待了 13 年之后于周四发布。然而，随着数以百万计的游戏玩家开始探索虚构的南佛罗里达州阳光普照的荒野中的每一个藏身处和后巷，甚至警察部门也试图利用这种单一文化的狂热来提升他们的公共信息或招募新警官。

这是一个奇怪的策略，因为该系列奖励盗窃和毒品交易，同时引诱你碾压行人，但显然，游戏中执法部门的存在（请注意，作为主要对手）就足以激发人工智能浪潮庆祝细蓝线。

例如，圣地亚哥警察局的 Instagram 频道周四发布了一张由人工智能生成的 SDPD 巡洋舰图像，背景是圣地亚哥湾的日落。它的霓虹粉色和紫色与 GTA 的饱和美感相匹配，如果有人对部门的目的有任何疑问，顶部会出现荒谬的短语“加入圣地亚哥警察局 VI”。 “想开警车，我们可以实现！”阅读标题。 “现在申请！”

华盛顿州的另一个警察局在其 Instagram 页面上分享了类似 GTA 的图像，鼓励观众通过从事执法工作来尝试“现实版”GTA VI。 “没有作弊码，”标题广告道。 “没有重生。只有真实的人、真正的挑战以及能够带来改变的职业。”从埃德蒙顿到多伦多，一波自以为是的 GTA 言论也充斥着加拿大警察部门的信息流——尽管卡尔加里警察局尝试了一些更轻松的做法，让一名交通警察对游戏中危险和非法驾驶操作的片段做出反应。

在那些不想通过 GTA VI 热潮来扩充自己队伍的警察部门中，许多人发布了旨在提醒人们法律存在于现实生活中的内容。加利福尼亚州格伦代尔警察局 Instagram 帐户上的一条典型帖子写道：“将其保留在游戏 VI 中”，其中配有一辆 GTA 风格的警用巡洋舰和城市景观。 “遵守公布的速度限制，尊重法律，并将通缉级别保持为零！”标题警告道。丹佛警察局以类似的斥责方式告诉追随者：“盗窃汽车仍然是非法的。”

这些机构的沟通团队也许应该重新考虑如何从 GTA VI 的巨大成功中获得参与度和影响力。正如许多评论者指出的那样，游戏将警察描绘成腐败且容易施暴的人。玩家们发现，如果你在可疑的逮捕过程中开始拍摄罪恶都市小队，他们会残酷地对待你。一个片段显示，一名警察拔出武器对着一个角色，而这个角色除了站在街上自拍之外，没有做过任何更糟糕的事。

一定程度的这种专制残酷行为应该会吸引右翼怪人，因为他们对 GTA VI 在性别、种族和政治方面过于“觉醒”感到不满。当游戏中最明显的恶棍选择忽视其对他们职业的恶毒态度，以便在社交媒体上发布垃圾邮件时，情况就有点不同了。

作为比较，福克斯新闻在《侠盗猎车手 6》中尽职尽责地采用了陈旧的法律和秩序路线，评论家们对孩子们接触虚拟枪支暴力（更不用说美国实际的枪支死亡）和道德败坏的氛围感到震惊。埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 曾说过，他不能玩 GTA 游戏，因为它们迫使你射杀警察。

这两种立场，无论多么不真诚，都表明了对执法的一点尊重，而警察部门自己却立即放弃了这种尊重，转而支持 GTA 的畏缩。他们当然不会因此赢得任何酷点，但至少这样他们可以假装与普通民众建立联系。

更令人困惑的是，俄罗斯军队已经制作了自己的《GTA VI》招募广告，并在其 Telegram 频道上发布，而北约则大肆宣扬其与军工《GTA》污泥的防御安全联盟，并吹嘘“即使是最好的游戏玩家也会面临躲避战斗机和潜艇的挑战”。试图用《侠盗猎车手》的图形来解析副总统 JD 万斯对特朗普“黄金时代”的描述是徒劳的。最反乌托邦的事态发展是，驻佐治亚州的美国陆军营为 43 名符合条件的士兵提供了四天假期，让他们玩新版 GTA，以换取重新入伍再服役两年。

这些机构或他们的使命与你穿着人字拖抢劫便利店的视频游戏有什么关系？没关系。当时代精神如此强烈时，你会启动 ChatGPT 并找到一个角度，无论多么令人困惑。肯定会有人在某个地方被欺骗，认为你与这件事有关。

items.article_content:
Food delivery startup Wonder is moving closer to becoming a publicly traded company after confidentially filing for an initial public offering (IPO). The company announced the filing on Thursday, marking a major milestone following years of fundraising, acquisitions, and expansion.

Wonder has yet to reveal how many shares it plans to make available or the expected price range.

Founded in 2018 by entrepreneur Marc Lore, Wonder has evolved from a food delivery concept into a broader food technology business. Its model goes beyond traditional delivery apps, with the company operating food hall-style locations where customers can order meals from multiple restaurant brands through a single platform. The company handles everything from meal preparation to delivery, pickup, and dine-in service.

Lore, who previously founded Jet.com and Diapers.com, has made no secret of his plans to take Wonder public. Those ambitions gained further attention in July, when the company announced it had raised more than $650 million in a funding round that valued it at around $9 billion. Investors include Accel, GV, AllianceBernstein, and ARK Invest.

Meanwhile, Wonder has been busy expanding its footprint and strengthening its business through acquisitions. The company has outlined ambitious growth plans, including a major push into Texas, where it aims to open more than 100 locations by the end of 2027.

Additionally, Wonder has acquired meal-kit company Blue Apron, restaurant delivery platform Grubhub, media company Tastemade, and kitchen robotics company Spyce. The latter acquisition gives Wonder access to automation technology that could help streamline food preparation and improve how food is served.

Wonder is also branching out with Wonder Create, its platform focused on letting food entrepreneurs and social media influencers develop new food concepts, restaurant brands, and menu items. The platform leverages AI to design and launch restaurant brands in less than a minute.

Another notable move is its $425 million partnership with DoorDash to expand its campus dining business, which operates at 450 colleges and universities and other locations.

Despite its growth, a move into the public markets will bring new challenges. Wonder is operating in an increasingly competitive food delivery landscape, going up against established names such as DoorDash and Uber Eats.

items.article_content_zh:
食品配送初创公司 Wonder 在秘密申请首次公开募股 (IPO) 后，距离成为一家上市公司又近了一步。该公司周四宣布了这份文件，标志着经过多年的融资、收购和扩张之后的一个重要里程碑。

Wonder尚未透露计划发行多少股或预期的价格范围。

Wonder 由企业家 Marc Lore 于 2018 年创立，现已从食品配送概念发展成为更广泛的食品技术业务。它的模式超越了传统的配送应用程序，该公司经营美食大厅式的场所，顾客可以通过一个平台从多个餐厅品牌订餐。该公司负责从准备餐点到送货、取货和就餐服务的一切事务。

Lore 曾创立 Jet.com 和 Diapers.com，他毫不掩饰自己将 Wonder 上市的计划。这些雄心壮志在 7 月份得到了进一步关注，当时该公司宣布在一轮融资中筹集了超过 6.5 亿美元，估值约为 90 亿美元。投资者包括 Accel、GV、AllianceBernstein 和 ARK Invest。

与此同时，Wonder 一直忙于通过收购扩大其足迹并加强其业务。该公司制定了雄心勃勃的增长计划，其中包括大力进军德克萨斯州，目标是到 2027 年底在该州开设 100 多家门店。

此外，Wonder 还收购了餐包公司 Blue Apron、餐厅配送平台 Grubhub、媒体公司 Tastemade 和厨房机器人公司 Spyce。后者的收购让 Wonder 获得了自动化技术，可以帮助简化食品准备工作并改善食品供应方式。

Wonder 还推出了 Wonder Create，该平台专注于让食品企业家和社交媒体影响者开发新的食品概念、餐厅品牌和菜单项目。该平台利用人工智能在不到一分钟的时间内设计和推出餐厅品牌。

另一个值得注意的举措是与 DoorDash 合作 4.25 亿美元，以扩大其校园餐饮业务，该业务在 450 所学院和大学及其他地点开展业务。

尽管增长，但进入公开市场将带来新的挑战。 Wonder 正在竞争日益激烈的食品配送领域开展业务，与 DoorDash 和 Uber Eats 等知名品牌展开竞争。

items.title: Databricks In Early Talks To Raise Funds At $225 Billion Valuation
items.title_en: Databricks In Early Talks To Raise Funds At $225 Billion Valuation
items.author: Wall Street Journal
items.article_content:
There’s a funny kind of game that the latest of late-stage startups must play when raising money. They often have to sell more shares than they want or risk offending some of their existing VCs.

This scenario recently played out with AI big-data company Databricks and its latest $5 billion raise announced Thursday, co-founder and CEO Ali Ghodsi (pictured above) told TechCrunch.

“We wanted to raise $1 billion, but then The Information printed this article saying that Databricks is doing a big fundraise. They did that in the middle of our conference. We were heads down with our conference, and we were not actually at all focused on fundraising,” Ghodsi recalled, referring to a conference that took place in June.

“As soon as that article went out, there was a long line of investors that started calling. My phone blew up. It was like the worst timing for us because we were busy with our conference,” he said.

It was an enviable problem that turned the news report into a self-fulfilling prophecy.

“The interest level was just insane. Just from this select group of investors that we looked at, there was $15 billion of interest,” he said.

When there’s that much desire to get into a deal, telling some long-term backers no is a recipe for hard feelings. Databricks decided to issue more stock, and in July, sent out a press release announcing it had closed its new round at a $188 billion valuation. (The company didn’t disclose at the time how much it had raised.)

On Thursday, Databricks shared it raised $5 billion from a paragraph worth of VCs that it let in on the deal and that its valuation pushed higher to a nice round $190 billion. The $5 billion round was led by Coatue and several others, including Blackstone, MGX, various accounts associated with various arms of T. Rowe Price, and new investor Sixth Street Growth. (Sixth Street is the firm founded by former Goldman Sachs chief investment officer Alan Waxman.) About two dozen VCs were named as participants.

Why were they all so eager? Databricks seems like a sure bet.

Ghodsi said his company has hit $7 billion of annualized run rate revenue, which is currently growing at 80% and is cash-flow positive. Its core product, a cloud data warehouse, is $1.5 billion of that run rate, and still growing at 100% year-over-year, he said.

Plus, Databricks has the magic AI pixie dust. Its database for agents, Lakebase, launched in June, 2025, and has hit $100 million revenue run rate. Its AI chatbot tool Genie, that can do business analysis on the spot, “is insanely popular,” he said.

So, if the business is doing so well, why raise more capital? The company had already raised $20 billion over the past 20 months.

AI is expensive, Ghodsi said. Databricks has multibillion-dollar cloud commitments with all three of the major hyperscalers. On top of that, “AI research is very expensive,” he said, adding that the company has an AI research team of 100 people, a highly competitive area.

Plus, Databricks is shopping. “We do a lot of M&A.” Ghodsi said, referencing an acquisition the company announced this week of Electric, the company that makes the lightweight Postgres database PGlite, a means for agents to spin up databases (terms undisclosed). In June, it bought AI cybersecurity company Panther; in March, it bought two startups.

There was a time when a $1 billion round was considered a massive and difficult raise. In this age of AI spending, where startups are raising $1 billion for a seed/Series A right out of the gate, that amount is now a pittance.

Still, Databricks’ private fundraising, instead of going public, has become something of a meme among the Valley. When it announced this round last month, people joked online that it has raised so many, it was running out of letters of the alphabet.

Ghodsi told CNBC that he still wants to take the company public one day. With such a giant roster of investors who will want to cash out one day, how can he promise anything else?

But today, he wants to focus on investing in AI, he said. Given the expenses involved in that, perhaps doing so out of the public eye is a wise idea.

Plus, when he can command an instant $15 billion of interest, and on his own terms, what’s the rush?

AI is expensive, Ghodsi said. Databricks has multibillion-dollar cloud commitments with all three of the major hyperscalers. On top of that, “AI research is very expensive,” he said, adding that the company has an AI research team of 100 people, a highly competitive area.

Plus, Databricks is shopping. “We do a lot of M&A.” Ghodsi said, referencing an acquisition the company announced this week of Electric, the company that makes the lightweight Postgres database PGlite, a means for agents to spin up databases (terms undisclosed). In June, it bought AI cybersecurity company Panther; in March, it bought two startups.

There was a time when a $1 billion round was considered a massive and difficult raise. In this age of AI spending, where startups are raising $1 billion for a seed/Series A right out of the gate, that amount is now a pittance.

Still, Databricks’ private fundraising, instead of going public, has become something of a meme among the Valley. When it announced this round last month, people joked online that it has raised so many, it was running out of letters of the alphabet.

Ghodsi told CNBC that he still wants to take the company public one day. With such a giant roster of investors who will want to cash out one day, how can he promise anything else?

But today, he wants to focus on investing in AI, he said. Given the expenses involved in that, perhaps doing so out of the public eye is a wise idea.

Plus, when he can command an instant $15 billion of interest, and on his own terms, what’s the rush?

items.article_content_zh:
最新的后期初创公司在融资时必须玩一种有趣的游戏。他们常常不得不出售比他们想要的更多的股票，否则就有冒犯一些现有风险投资人的风险。

联合创始人兼首席执行官 Ali Ghodsi（上图）告诉 TechCrunch，最近人工智能大数据公司 Databricks 就出现了这种情况，该公司周四宣布最新一轮 50 亿美元融资。

“我们想筹集 10 亿美元，但后来 The Information 发表了这篇文章，说 Databricks 正在进行大规模筹款。他们在我们的会议进行到一半时就这么做了。我们低着头参加会议，实际上根本没有专注于筹款，”Ghodsi 回忆道，他指的是 6 月份举行的一次会议。

“那篇文章一发出，就有一长串投资者开始打电话。我的电话爆炸了。这对我们来说是最糟糕的时机，因为我们正忙于我们的会议，”他说。

这是一个令人羡慕的问题，将新闻报道变成了一个自我实现的预言。

“兴趣水平简直太疯狂了。仅从我们研究的这群精选投资者中，就有 150 亿美元的兴趣，”他说。

当人们非常渴望达成协议时，对一些长期支持者说“不”会让人感到不舒服。 Databricks 决定发行更多股票，并于 7 月发布新闻稿，宣布已以 1880 亿美元的估值完成新一轮融资。 （该公司当时没有透露筹集了多少资金。）

周四，Databricks 分享称，它从参与此次交易的多家风投公司那里筹集了 50 亿美元，其估值也升至 1900 亿美元。这轮 50 亿美元的融资由 Coatue 和其他几家公司领投，其中包括 Blackstone、MGX、与 T. Rowe Price 各个部门相关的多个账户以及新投资者 Sixth Street Growth。 （第六街是由前高盛首席投资官艾伦·韦克斯曼创立的公司。）大约有两打风险投资家被指定为参与者。

Ghodsi 表示，他的公司年化营业收入已达到 70 亿美元，目前正以 80% 的速度增长，现金流为正。他说，其核心产品云数据仓库的运行费用为 15 亿美元，并且仍在以 100% 的同比速度增长。

另外，Databricks 还拥有神奇的 AI 精灵尘埃。其代理数据库 Lakebase 于 2025 年 6 月推出，收入运行率已达到 1 亿美元。他说，其人工智能聊天机器人工具 Genie 可以现场进行业务分析，“非常受欢迎”。

那么，如果业务做得这么好，为什么还要筹集更多资金呢？该公司在过去 20 个月内已筹集了 200 亿美元。

戈德西说，人工智能很昂贵。 Databricks 与三大主要超大规模提供商签订了数十亿美元的云承诺。最重要的是，“人工智能研究非常昂贵”，他补充道，该公司拥有一个 100 人的人工智能研究团队，这是一个竞争非常激烈的领域。

另外，Databricks 正在购物。 “我们进行了很多并购。” Ghodsi 说，他提到了该公司本周宣布的对 Electric 的收购，该公司生产轻量级 Postgres 数据库 PGlite，这是代理商启动数据库的一种手段（具体条款未公开）。 6月，收购人工智能网络安全公司Panther；三月份，它收购了两家初创公司。

items.title: SpaceX’s subsidiary Cursor tells lawmakers it's considering phasing out Chinese AI models
items.title_en: SpaceX’s subsidiary Cursor tells lawmakers it's considering phasing out Chinese AI models
items.author: Kai Nicol-Schwarz
items.article_content:
SpaceX's artificial-intelligence coding platform, Cursor, is considering moving away from using of Chinese AI models due to "geopolitical risk,"CNBC has learned.

Cursor, which SpaceX acquired at an implied $60 billion equity value in August, had built its coding model Composer 2 on top of Chinese lab Moonshot AI's Kimi K2.5.

It's among the U.S. firms that have adopted Chinese models, whose usage has spiked across the globe this year, worrying lawmakers in Washington. The battle for AI supremacy between the U.S. and China has reached new heights in 2026 as Chinese models have improved.

But now Cursor plans to "explore phasing out PRC [People's Republic of China]-developed open-weight models because of geopolitical risk,"according to a report produced by the House Committee on Homeland Security and the House Select Committee on China, shared exclusively with CNBC ahead of its publication on Friday.

The report, which follows a months-long investigation into the adoption of Chinese AI models into the American tech stack, said Cursor "informed the Committees"of those plans. Airbnb and DoorDash also engaged with the investigation about their use of Chinese AI models.

SpaceX announced it entered into a formal agreement to buy Cursor in June; the deal was completed in August. SpaceX is developing the Grok family of models, which Cursor has been involved in training.

Cursor, SpaceX and DoorDash did not respond to a CNBC request for comment. Airbnb declined to comment. The U.S. Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

### Chinese AI adoption

The report found that cost, customization and near-frontier performance of Chinese AI models were driving adoption, with the U.S. lacking a competitive open-weight alternative at "price and performance the market demands."

"Beijing is now seeking to turn those technological gains into global market share and long-term dependence,"the report says. China's embassy in the U.K. did not respond to a request for comment. China's Foreign Ministry did not immediately respond.

It also sets out recommendations to address the issues it has identified.

Those include launching a "national American open-weight initiative"that combines public computing power, shared evaluation infrastructure and "lawful access"to American frontier models for training.

The report also says an order, made public in October, that banned DeepSeek from federal civilian agency systems, should be built on, by prohibiting the use of "PRC-developed AI models"in federal information systems and in performance of federal contracts.

Separately, Washington is also concerned about Chinese companies accessing Nvidia chips remotely, via overseas data centers, and gaining ground by using "distillation,"where new models use older, more established ones to help train them.

The U.S. Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security, or BIS, announced on Monday an interim final rule designed to prevent Chinese companies' remote access to AI chips.

items.title_zh: SpaceX子公司Cursor拟放弃使用中国AI模型
items.summary_zh: SpaceX旗下Cursor平台告知美国国会，受地缘政治风险影响，正考虑淘汰基于Moonshot AI开发的模型

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: SpaceX旗下AI编程平台Cursor向美国众议院国土安全委员会及中国问题特设委员会披露，正考虑淘汰目前使用的中国AI实验室Moonshot AI开发的Kimi K2.5模型，理由为存在潜在地缘政治风险。此前调查显示，多家美企因成本优势及模型性能采用了中国AI模型，立法者已启动针对此类技术供应链依赖的审查，并建议组建美国国家级开源模型倡议以填补替代空白。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: SpaceX's AI coding platform, Cursor, informed the U.S. House Committee on Homeland Security and the Select Committee on China that it is exploring the phase-out of the Kimi K2.5 model from Chinese lab Moonshot AI due to geopolitical risks. Investigations revealed that several U.S. firms adopted Chinese models for cost and performance advantages, prompting lawmakers to propose a national American open-weight AI initiative to reduce reliance on foreign models.

elements_zh.who: SpaceX旗下Cursor平台；美国众议院国土安全委员会；Moonshot AI（月之暗面）
elements_zh.where: 美国国会监管听证与合规审计场合
elements_zh.what: 考虑淘汰Kimi K2.5模型，并应对针对中国AI模型采购的立法审查
elements_zh.why: 日益严峻的地缘政治摩擦及美国对关键AI供应链自主可控的要求

elements_en.who: Cursor (SpaceX subsidiary); U.S. House Committees; Moonshot AI
elements_en.what: Considering phasing out Kimi K2.5 model amidst legislative scrutiny
elements_en.why: Rising geopolitical tensions and U.S. concerns over AI supply chain sovereignty

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 此举揭示了美国科技企业在追求模型推理成本效益与遵守地缘政治合规性之间的剧烈撕裂。虽然中国开源模型在性价比上具有极强竞争力，但随着美国国会立法收紧及国防背景企业的敏感性增加，AI供应链的“去中国化”将成为强制性合规门槛，这将倒逼美国本土模型厂商加快低成本、高性能开源替代方案的研发进度。
ai_analysis.insight_en: This move highlights the tension between cost-efficient model inference and geopolitical compliance for U.S. tech firms. While Chinese open-weight models offer competitive performance, increasing legislative pressure and the scrutiny on defense-linked entities will make 'de-risking' the AI supply chain a mandatory compliance requirement, accelerating the push for U.S.-native cost-effective alternatives.

Investigations revealed that several U.S. firms adopted Chinese models for cost and performance advantages, prompting lawmakers to propose a national American open-weight AI initiative to reduce reliance on foreign models.
key_points_zh: Cursor响应监管要求，拟淘汰中国Moonshot AI的Kimi K2.5模型。
美国政府正对AI供应链中的外国模型进行深度调查与合规限制。
立法建议提出构建美国国家级开源模型方案以强化技术安全。
key_points_en: Cursor aims to phase out Chinese Moonshot AI models following regulatory scrutiny.
U.S. government is investigating the reliance on foreign AI models within the domestic tech stack.
Legislators propose a national initiative for open-weight models to ensure technical sovereignty.
ai_analysis.takeaway_zh: 此举揭示了美国科技企业在追求模型推理成本效益与遵守地缘政治合规性之间的剧烈撕裂。虽然中国开源模型在性价比上具有极强竞争力，但随着美国国会立法收紧及国防背景企业的敏感性增加，AI供应链的“去中国化”将成为强制性合规门槛，这将倒逼美国本土模型厂商加快低成本、高性能开源替代方案的研发进度。
ai_analysis.takeaway_en: This move highlights the tension between cost-efficient model inference and geopolitical compliance for U.S. tech firms. While Chinese open-weight models offer competitive performance, increasing legislative pressure and the scrutiny on defense-linked entities will make 'de-risking' the AI supply chain a mandatory compliance requirement, accelerating the push for U.S.-native cost-effective alternatives.

items.article_content_zh:
由于“地缘政治风险”，SpaceX 的人工智能编码平台 Cursor 正在考虑不再使用中国人工智能模型。

SpaceX 在 8 月份以 600 亿美元的股权价值收购了 Cursor，该公司在中国实验室 Moonshot AI 的 Kimi K2.5 基础上构建了其编码模型 Composer 2。

它是采用中国模式的美国公司之一，今年中国模式的使用在全球范围内激增，这令华盛顿的立法者感到担忧。随着中国模型的改进，中美之间的人工智能霸主之争在 2026 年达到了新的高度。

但根据众议院国土安全委员会和众议院中国问题特别委员会制作的一份报告，Cursor 计划“出于地缘政治风险，探索逐步淘汰中华人民共和国开发的开放权重模型”，该报告在周五发布前独家与 CNBC 分享。

这份报告是在对美国技术堆栈采用中国人工智能模型进行了长达数月的调查之后发布的，Cursor 表示，“已向委员会通报了这些计划”。 Airbnb 和 DoorDash 也参与了有关其使用中国人工智能模型的调查。

Cursor、SpaceX 和 DoorDash 没有回应 CNBC 的置评请求。爱彼迎拒绝置评。美国商务部工业与安全局没有立即回应置评请求。

该报告发现，中国人工智能模型的成本、定制化和接近前沿的性能正在推动采用，而美国缺乏“市场所需的价格和性能”的有竞争力的开放重量替代方案。

报告称：“北京现在正在寻求将这些技术成果转化为全球市场份额和长期依赖。”中国驻英国大使馆没有回应置评请求。中国外交部没有立即回应。

它还提出了解决已发现问题的建议。

其中包括发起一项“美国国家开放权重倡议”，该倡议将公共计算能力、共享评估基础设施和“合法访问”美国前沿模型进行培训相结合。

该报告还表示，10 月份发布的一项禁止 DeepSeek 进入联邦民事机构系统的命令应该以此为基础，禁止在联邦信息系统和履行联邦合同中使用“中国开发的人工智能模型”。

另外，华盛顿还担心中国公司通过海外数据中心远程访问英伟达芯片，并通过使用“蒸馏”技术取得进展，即新模型使用旧的、更成熟的模型来帮助训练它们。

美国商务部工业与安全局（BIS）周一宣布了一项临时最终规则，旨在阻止中国公司远程访问人工智能芯片。

【起因与机理】日益严峻的地缘政治摩擦及美国对关键AI供应链自主可控的要求
【调查与监管诉求】Cursor响应监管要求，拟淘汰中国Moonshot AI的Kimi K2.5模型。
【各方立场与态度】立法建议提出构建美国国家级开源模型方案以强化技术安全。

[Root Cause & Mechanism] Rising geopolitical tensions and U.S. concerns over AI supply chain sovereignty
[Regulatory & Investigation Focus] Cursor aims to phase out Chinese Moonshot AI models following regulatory scrutiny.

items.title: Artificial Analysis says Inkling 2 Mini, with 5.4B active parameters, matches Qwen3.8 27B (xhigh) on its Intelligence Index with ~5x fewer active parameters (Artificial Analysis)
items.title_en: Artificial Analysis says Inkling 2 Mini, with 5.4B active parameters, matches Qwen3.8 27B (xhigh) on its Intelligence Index with ~5x fewer active parameters (Artificial Analysis)
items.author: Artificial Analysis
items.article_content:
Thinking Machines has released Inkling 2 Mini at 20 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, an open weights looped transformer on the Pareto frontier for Intelligence vs. Active Parameters

Inkling 2 Mini is a 26B total, 5.4B active parameter mixture-of-experts model. The 5.4B active parameter count includes three passes through its looped layers; it uses 3.1B unique weights per text token, and it is small enough to run on a MacBook or DGX Spark.

It is released under an Apache 2.0 license, with text and image input and a 1M token context window.

Inkling 2 Mini matches Qwen3.8 27B (xhigh) and Nanbeige4.3-33B on the Intelligence Index with ~5x and ~6x fewer active parameters, respectively.

It is on the Pareto frontier for Intelligence vs. size on both total and active parameters.

Inkling 2 Mini uses ~38% more output tokens than Qwen3.8 27B for the same Intelligence Index score, but ~2.8x less compute.

Twelve of its 24 layers run three times per token, adding compute without adding output tokens. It averages ~152K output tokens per Intelligence Index task vs. ~110K for Qwen3.8 27B and ~158K for Nanbeige4.3-33B. On our compute proxy measure (active parameters × tokens), it sits on the Pareto frontier, using ~2.8x less compute than Qwen3.8 27B and ~5x less than Nanbeige4.3-33B.

Inkling 2 Mini is ~6x cheaper and ~4x faster per task than Qwen3.8 27B.

It costs $0.59 and takes 9.0 minutes per Intelligence Index task vs. $3.53 and 38.2 minutes for Qwen3.8 27B. GPT-6 Luna (max) scores 28 for $0.15 per task. Cost uses Thinking Machines' first-party pricing ($0.15/$0.50/$0.015 per 1M input/output/cache hit tokens).

OpenAI’s release of GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol delivers the #2 model in the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index and most of the Cost per Task Pareto frontier

items.article_content_zh:
Thinking Machines 发布了人工智能分析智能指数排名第 20 的 Inkling 2 Mini，这是一个位于帕累托前沿的开放权重循环变压器，用于智能与主动参数的比较

Inkling 2 Mini 是一个总共 26B、5.4B 活动参数的专家混合模型。 5.4B 活动参数计数包括通过其循环层的三遍；它对每个文本标记使用 3.1B 唯一权重，并且足够小，可以在 MacBook 或 DGX Spark 上运行。

它是在 Apache 2.0 许可证下发布的，具有文本和图像输入以及 1M 令牌上下文窗口。

Inkling 2 Mini 在智力指数上与 Qwen3.8 27B (xhigh) 和 Nanb​​eige4.3-33B 相匹配，活动参数分别少约 5 倍和约 6 倍。

它位于总参数和主动参数的智力与规模的帕累托前沿。

对于相同的智能指数分数，Inkling 2 Mini 使用的输出令牌比 Qwen3.8 27B 多约 38%，但计算量却少约 2.8 倍。

其 24 层中的 12 个层每个令牌运行 3 次，增加计算量而不添加输出令牌。每个智力指数任务的平均输出令牌约为 152K，而 Qwen3.8 27B 约为 110K，Nanbeige4.3-33B 约为 158K。在我们的计算代理度量（主动参数 × 令牌）上，它位于 Pareto 边界，使用的计算量比 Qwen3.8 27B 少约 2.8 倍，比 Nanb​​eige4.3-33B 少约 5 倍。

Inkling 2 Mini 比 Qwen3.8 27B 便宜约 6 倍，每项任务速度快约 4 倍。

每个智力指数任务的成本为 0.59 美元，需要 9.0 分钟，而 Qwen3.8 27B 的成本为 3.53 美元，需要 38.2 分钟。 GPT-6 Luna（最高）得分 28，每项任务 0.15 美元。成本使用 Thinking Machines 的第一方定价（每 100 万输入/输出/缓存命中令牌 0.15 美元/0.50 美元/0.015 美元）。

OpenAI 发布的 GPT-6.2 Astra 和 GPT-6.2 Sol 提供了人工分析智能指数中的第二名模型以及大部分每任务成本帕累托前沿

items.article_content:
AI (Artificial Intelligence) letters and robot hand are placed on computer motherboard in this illustration taken, June 23, 2023. REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration

Nov 20 : Coding startup Cognition AI is in funding talks at a $75 billion valuation, Bloomberg News reported on Friday, citing people familiar with the matter.

The company is considering raising $2 billion or more in the latest round, the report said, adding that the talks were ongoing and the details could change.

The news comes about two months after Cognition raised $2 billion in a Series E funding round at a valuation of $48 billion. The round was led by new investors Andreessen Horowitz and Accel, alongside existing backers Founders Fund, General Catalyst, and Avenir.

Cognition did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.

The company is an AI startup that develops autonomous software-engineering agents, which can plan, write, test and deploy code with limited human intervention.

The company was valued at $26 billion in a funding round in May, when it raised $1 billion.

11 月 20 日：据彭博社周五援引知情人士消息称，编码初创公司 Cognition AI 正在进行融资谈判，估值为 750 亿美元。

报道称，该公司正在考虑在最新一轮融资中筹集 20 亿美元或更多资金，并补充说谈判仍在进行中，细节可能会发生变化。

两个月前，Cognition 在 E 轮融资中筹集了 20 亿美元，估值达到 480 亿美元。此轮融资由新投资者 Andreessen Horowitz 和 Accel 领投，现有投资者包括 Founders Fund、General Catalyst 和 Avenir。

Cognition 没有立即回应路透社的置评请求。

该公司是一家人工智能初创公司，开发自主软件工程代理，可以在有限的人工干预下规划、编写、测试和部署代码。

该公司在 5 月份的一轮融资中筹集了 10 亿美元，估值达到 260 亿美元。

items.title: Many Etsy Sellers Close Up Shop Over Site’s New A.I. Policy
items.title_en: Many Etsy Sellers Close Up Shop Over Site’s New A.I. Policy
items.author: Reggie Ugwu
items.article_content:
Many longtime owners of shops on Etsy, the online marketplace known for its handmade goods, said this week that they had left the site over a policy change that they said leaves them vulnerable to exploitation by artificial intelligence companies.

Language in Etsy’s new terms, set to take effect on Dec. 16, says the company and its “third party partners and vendors” reserve the right to use sellers’ content to “develop, train, test and improve artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies.”

The terms say that Etsy and its partners will use such technologies in part to improve the platform and keep it safe for users. The previous version of the terms did not include a clause about using content for artificial intelligence.

“Etsy decided that selling on their platform now means letting them train AI on our artwork AND resell that data to third parties, with no way to opt out,” Aaron Millard, an illustrator, wrote in an Instagram post announcing that he was deleting the shop that he has run for nearly a decade. “My work took years to learn and create. I won’t let it be stolen.”

Kristen and Geoff Zephyrus, the founders of the home goods and stationary brand Cognitive Surplus, which has sold its products on Etsy for 13 years, also deleted their shop. In an Instagram post, they accused the company of claiming “perpetual, free, boundless permission to not only train AI on our art, but also to resell the data for profit.”

“For Etsy to be helping to train algorithms with our human content is just unimaginably awful,” Kristen Zephyrus said in an interview. “We don’t want anything to do with that.”

In a statement posted to Etsy’s website on Monday, James Ossman, the company’s vice president for customer operations, addressed the site’s sellers directly.

Etsy will not “use your content to train A.I. models designed to copy your original work or replace your creativity,” Ossman wrote. He cited the development of fraud detection tools and advertisements on the site as among the reasons for granting third parties access to sellers’ content.

A representative for Etsy did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Friday.

Many publicly traded internet companies like Etsy have been caught between pressure from shareholders to embrace artificial intelligence and the ire of users who reject the technology.

Big bets by major firms and their investors on the A.I. revolution have helped the U.S. stock market set records in recent years. But Americans in general are much less enthusiastic. A Gallup poll from the summer found that nearly 40 percent of Americans feel that A.I. does more harm than good. Many of the Democratic political candidates who swept into power during the midterm elections this month campaigned explicitly against A.I. companies and data centers.

Etsy, which was founded in 2005 to help independent artisans find customers online, is no stranger to user revolt. In 2022, more than 20,000 Etsy sellers went on strike to protest a 30 percent increase in its base-line sales fee, to 6.5 percent from 5 percent. In October, the company announced tighter restrictions on so-called A.I. slop after many users decried such content.
