items.title_zh: Etsy新规引发创作者集体出走
items.summary_zh: Etsy因调整服务条款，授权第三方调用卖家数据训练AI，导致资深商家关闭店铺抵制
items.article_content_zh:
Etsy（以手工制品闻名的在线市场）上的许多长期店主本周表示，他们因政策变化而离开了该网站，他们说这使他们很容易受到人工智能公司的利用。

Etsy 将于 12 月 16 日生效的新条款中表示，该公司及其“第三方合作伙伴和供应商”保留使用卖家内容来“开发、培训、测试和改进人工智能和机器学习技术”的权利。

条款称，Etsy 及其合作伙伴将部分使用此类技术来改进平台并确保用户安全。之前版本的条款不包含有关将内容用于人工智能的条款。

“Etsy 决定，现在在他们的平台上销售意味着让他们在我们的艺术品上训练人工智能，并将这些数据转售给第三方，而且没有办法选择退出，”插画家 Aaron Millard 在 Instagram 上发帖，宣布他将删除自己经营了近十年的商店。 “我的作品花了数年时间来学习和创作。我不会让它被盗。”

家居用品和文具品牌 Cognitive Surplus 的创始人克里斯汀·泽菲勒斯 (Kristen Zephyrus) 和杰夫·泽菲勒斯 (Geoff Zephyrus) 也删除了自己的商店，该品牌在 Etsy 上销售产品已有 13 年。在 Instagram 上的一篇帖子中，他们指责该公司声称“拥有永久、免费、无限的许可，不仅可以在我们的艺术上训练人工智能，还可以转售数据以获取利润。”

“对于 Etsy 来说，利用我们的人类内容来帮助训练算法真是太糟糕了，”克里斯汀·泽菲勒斯 (Kristen Zephyrus) 在接受采访时说道。 “我们不想与此有任何关系。”

在周一发布在 Etsy 网站上的一份声明中，该公司负责客户运营的副总裁詹姆斯·奥斯曼 (James Ossman) 直接向该网站的卖家发表了讲话。

奥斯曼写道，Etsy 不会“使用你的内容来训练旨在复制你的原创作品或取代你的创造力的人工智能模型”。他指出，欺诈检测工具的开发和网站上的广告是允许第三方访问卖家内容的原因之一。

Etsy 的代表周五没有立即回应置评请求。

许多像 Etsy 这样的上市互联网公司都陷入了股东拥抱人工智能的压力和拒绝这项技术的用户的愤怒之间。

大公司及其投资者对人工智能下了大赌注。近年来，这场革命帮助美国股市创下了纪录。但总体而言，美国人的热情要低得多。今年夏天的盖洛普民意调查发现，近 40% 的美国人认为人工智能。弊大于利。许多在本月中期选举中上台的民主党政治候选人都明确反对人工智能。公司和数据中心。

Etsy 成立于 2005 年，旨在帮助独立工匠在网上寻找客户，它对用户的反抗并不陌生。 2022 年，超过 20,000 名 Etsy 卖家举行罢工，抗议其基准销售费从 5% 增加 30% 至 6.5%。 10 月，该公司宣布对所谓的人工智能实施更严格的限制。在许多用户谴责此类内容后，就停止了。

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 电商平台Etsy宣布将于12月16日生效的新条款，规定公司及其第三方合作伙伴有权使用平台创作者内容进行AI模型训练与测试。此举引发艺术家与独立品牌主大规模抗议，尽管Etsy副总裁James Ossman回应称相关数据仅用于欺诈检测与广告优化，但因缺乏退出机制及对知识产权流失的担忧，导致大量资深卖家注销店铺。

elements_zh.where: Etsy平台服务条款更新
elements_zh.what: 强制授权平台及第三方利用卖家作品训练AI模型，且未提供拒绝选项
elements_zh.why: 平台面临股东压力需拥抱AI技术，而创作者面临知识产权变现与流失风险

elements_en.who: Etsy, James Ossman (VP of Customer Operations)
elements_en.what: Compulsory authorization for AI training using seller data without opt-out options
elements_en.why: Institutional pressure to integrate AI vs. creator rights protection

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 此事件反映了内容平台在AI转型期的合规性危机，即平台“数据所有权”与创作者“知识产权”的结构性矛盾。若缺乏透明的授权机制与收益对价，平台通过AI榨取长尾内容价值将导致生态失衡，最终造成高质量创作资源的流失与社区价值的毁灭性衰减。
ai_analysis.insight_en: This incident highlights the structural conflict between platform data-mining mandates and creator IP rights during the AI transition. Without transparent authorization and value-sharing mechanisms, the forced extraction of creator data to train AI risks long-term ecological depletion and the exodus of the platform's core creative capital.

items.title: Canada Retail Sales Tracking Largest Decline Since Feb. 2025
items.title_en: Canada Retail Sales Tracking Largest Decline Since Feb. 2025

inline_images.caption: Canadian Mortgage Trends: Canada
inline_images.alt: Canadian Mortgage Trends: Canada

items.author: Bloomberg
items.article_content:
Canadian retail spending is expected to have declined in October, following a 0.8% increase in September led by gasoline stations and fuel vendors.

A preliminary estimate points to a 1.5% decrease in retail sales last month, which would be the largest decline since February 2025.

Sales in September increased in five out of nine subsectors, and rose by 6.9% at gasoline stations and fuel vendors. That increase was largely driven by higher prices, as sales in volume terms increased by a more modest 1.6%.

Economists surveyed by Bloomberg had expected retail sales increased by 0.7% in September.

Core retail sales, which exclude gasoline stations and fuel vendors as well as motor vehicle and parts dealers, increased by 0.1%. In volume terms, sales were also up by 0.1%.

The largest decline in core retail sales was food and beverage retailers, which was led by a 0.5% decline at grocery stores, following a 1% increase in August.

Building material and garden equipment and supplies dealers declined by 1.3%, while furniture, home furnishings electronics and appliances retailers decreased by the same magnitude.

Meanwhile, retail sales increased by 1.2% in the third quarter. In volume terms, they rose by 1% over the three-month period.

The expected decline in October retail sales provides further evidence of weakening to start the fourth quarter, said CIBC senior economist Andrew Grantham.

“While the 1.5% decline estimated for October will partly reflect lower gasoline prices, most of that move lower in pump prices has actually occurred in November rather than October, and as a result this advance estimate suggests a decline in volumes as well,” Grantham said in a note to investors.

The Canadian economy — including consumer spending — has remained largely resilient throughout the U.S. trade war. However, growth is expected to slow in the second half of the year after the dispute escalated and more tariffs were imposed by both countries.

The labour market has also shown signs of weakness, as employment has failed to grow this year. Servus Credit Union chief economist Charles St-Arnaud said the stagnant labour market in recent months may be to blame for weaker retail sales.

“This is another indicator that suggests that the Canadian economy is losing momentum going into the last few months of 2026. The weakness suggests the Bank of Canada should take a pause to better assess the situation before hike again, especially with some fuel prices easing in recent weeks,” St-Arnaud said in an email.

Despite the expected slowdown, the Bank of Canada raised interest rates in October to clamp down on inflationary pressures from higher energy prices. Traders in overnight swaps put the odds of a hike in December at about 60%, which would further weigh on spending.

–With assistance from Mario Baker Ramirez.

Core retail sales, which exclude gasoline stations and fuel vendors as well as motor vehicle and parts dealers, increased by 0.1%. In volume terms, sales were also up by 0.1%.

The largest decline in core retail sales was food and beverage retailers, which was led by a 0.5% decline at grocery stores, following a 1% increase in August.

Building material and garden equipment and supplies dealers declined by 1.3%, while furniture, home furnishings electronics and appliances retailers decreased by the same magnitude.

Meanwhile, retail sales increased by 1.2% in the third quarter. In volume terms, they rose by 1% over the three-month period.

The expected decline in October retail sales provides further evidence of weakening to start the fourth quarter, said CIBC senior economist Andrew Grantham.

“While the 1.5% decline estimated for October will partly reflect lower gasoline prices, most of that move lower in pump prices has actually occurred in November rather than October, and as a result this advance estimate suggests a decline in volumes as well,” Grantham said in a note to investors.

The Canadian economy — including consumer spending — has remained largely resilient throughout the U.S. trade war. However, growth is expected to slow in the second half of the year after the dispute escalated and more tariffs were imposed by both countries.

The labour market has also shown signs of weakness, as employment has failed to grow this year. Servus Credit Union chief economist Charles St-Arnaud said the stagnant labour market in recent months may be to blame for weaker retail sales.

“This is another indicator that suggests that the Canadian economy is losing momentum going into the last few months of 2026. The weakness suggests the Bank of Canada should take a pause to better assess the situation before hike again, especially with some fuel prices easing in recent weeks,” St-Arnaud said in an email.

Despite the expected slowdown, the Bank of Canada raised interest rates in October to clamp down on inflationary pressures from higher energy prices. Traders in overnight swaps put the odds of a hike in December at about 60%, which would further weigh on spending.

–With assistance from Mario Baker Ramirez.

items.title_zh: 加拿大零售销售遭遇逾三年最大跌幅
items.summary_zh: 加拿大10月零售额预估下滑1.5%，创2025年2月以来最大降幅，显示经济动能放缓
items.article_content_zh:
继 9 月份加油站和燃料供应商带动零售支出增长 0.8% 后，加拿大 10 月份零售支出预计将出现下降。

初步估计上个月零售额下降1.5%，这将是2025年2月以来的最大降幅。

9 月份，9 个子行业中有 5 个行业的销售额出现增长，其中加油站和燃料供应商的销售额增长了 6.9%。这一增长主要是由价格上涨推动的，销量仅增长了 1.6%。

彭博社调查的经济学家此前预计9月份零售额增长0.7%。

不包括加油站和燃料供应商以及机动车辆和零部件经销商的核心零售额增长了 0.1%。从销量来看，销售额也增长了 0.1%。

核心零售额降幅最大的是食品和饮料零售商，其中杂货店继 8 月份增长 1% 后下降 0.5%。

建筑材料和园林设备及用品经销商下降了1.3%，而家具、家居电子和电器零售商也出现了同样幅度的下降。

与此同时，第三季度零售额增长1.2%。就数量而言，三个月内增长了 1%。

CIBC 高级经济学家 Andrew Grantham 表示，10 月份零售销售的预期下降进一步证明了第四季度开始的疲软。

格兰瑟姆在给投资者的一份报告中表示：“虽然预计 10 月份下降 1.5% 将部分反映汽油价格下降，但大部分零售价格下降实际上发生在 11 月份，而不是 10 月份，因此这一预先估计表明销量也出现下降。”

在美国贸易战期间，加拿大经济（包括消费者支出）基本上保持弹性。然而，在争端升级以及两国征收更多关税后，预计下半年经济增长将放缓。

劳动力市场也显示出疲软迹象，今年就业未能增长。 Servus Credit Union首席经济学家Charles St-Arnaud表示，近几个月劳动力市场停滞可能是零售销售疲软的原因。

St-Arnaud 在一封电子邮件中表示：“这是另一个指标，表明加拿大经济在进入 2026 年最后几个月时正在失去动力。这种疲软表明加拿大央行应该暂停一下，在再次加息之前更好地评估形势，特别是在最近几周燃油价格有所回落的情况下。”

尽管预期经济放缓，加拿大央行还是在 10 月份提高了利率，以抑制能源价格上涨带来的通胀压力。隔夜掉期交易商预计 12 月份加息的可能性约为 60%，这将进一步拖累支出。

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 加拿大统计局数据显示，10月零售销售额预计下降1.5%，这将是自2025年2月以来的最大单月跌幅。尽管三季度零售表现尚可，但在贸易摩擦升级及就业市场停滞的双重压力下，第四季度开局表现疲软，市场普遍预期加拿大央行将暂停升息以观察宏观经济形势。

Despite resilient growth in the third quarter, the combination of escalated trade disputes and a stagnant labor market has dampened fourth-quarter momentum, prompting analysts to expect a pause in rate hikes by the Bank of Canada.

items.title: TML releases Inkling 2 Mini, an open-weights 26.4B-parameter transformer that loops middle layers three times per token for better reasoning with fewer tokens (Thinking Machines Lab)
items.title_en: TML releases Inkling 2 Mini, an open-weights 26.4B-parameter transformer that loops middle layers three times per token for better reasoning with fewer tokens (Thinking Machines Lab)
items.author: Thinking Machines Lab
items.article_content:
Today we are releasing Inkling 2 Mini, a fast, powerful model that’s small enough to run on your laptop.

Inkling 2 Mini is a looped transformer, running the middle layers of the model three times for every token. This allows the model to apply more reasoning and reach the right answer with fewer tokens, especially on tasks such as agentic coding that depend on reasoning quality. Inkling 2 Mini leads every open-weights model with less than 100B total parameters on benchmarks such as DeepSWE v1.1 (48.2%) and Vals Index v2.2 (46.5%). It runs faster than similarly performing models as well.

Inkling 2 Mini is a Mixture-of-Experts model with 26.4B total parameters, 3.4B active, and 5.4B weight activations per token to account for looping. Looping allows the model to reason longer without writing its reasoning down, which matters for monitoring: our ability to oversee and understand what the model does by reading its chain of thought (CoT).

We measured the impact of looping on both performance and monitorability with Inkling 2 Mini and a research-specific variable-loop variant we are releasing alongside it. The variable-loop model’s no-CoT time horizon improved from 16 seconds at one pass to 37 seconds with three, and its performance on a benchmark of serial reasoning kept improving out to ten loops—twice as many as it was trained with. The model’s chain of thought grew shorter with more loops but stayed legible throughout. The model didn’t trend higher on tests of agentic sabotage as loops were added.

We’re excited to offer some of the first models with looped architecture available to researchers. The variable-loop model was used for our monitorability experiments as it allows for cleaner comparisons between different looping depths.

Most of Inkling 2 Mini’s weights were trained and are deployed natively in NVFP4, with the last four layers in MXFP8. The total memory footprint of Inkling 2 Mini is ~20GB, allowing it to run on local devices such as consumer laptops and desktop AI computers. Our researchers took Inkling 2 Mini on a flight, where it ran offline on a MacBook Pro and built a playable flight simulator in a few minutes.

Open video: PlaneBench flight simulator demo, screen with phone video inset0:0015× Loading the flight simulator Inkling 2 Mini built… To try the flight simulator, open this page on desktop. Inkling 2 Mini is released with open weights and is available on Tinker today for inference and customization.

Inkling 2 Mini’s strengths mirror those of Inkling 2 Small: it does best on long-horizon agentic work and is the best among open-weights models of similar size on most tasks we measured.

Inkling 2 Mini scores ahead of every comparable model on agentic coding benchmarks such as DeepSWE v1.1 and SWE-bench Pro v2, and is behind only Qwen3.8-27B on others. On PMPP-Hard, a kernel-optimization benchmark, it approaches the score of the much larger Inkling 2 Small.

While looping improves the model’s reasoning, it doesn’t enable its weights to store more facts—knowledge is mostly a function of total parameter count. Inkling 2 Mini’s score on AA-Omniscience, a measure of factuality, is in line with other models of the same size. Studying the variable-loop model, we saw that performances on long-context benchmarks improve with more passes, such as GraphWalks BFS and MRCR v2; but knowledge-intensive benchmarks doesn’t improve with more passes, such as AA-Omniscience, SimpleQA Verified, SimpleVQA, and WorldVQA.

Inkling 2 Mini overcomes the knowledge gap by efficiently using search and tools. It leads open-weights models of similar size on BrowseComp, DeepSearchQA, and MCP Atlas. It is also strong on knowledge work benchmarks that incorporate search and tool use.

Researchers at Stanford measure intelligence per joule: how much energy an LLM needs per query to reach a given level of performance.Researchers at Stanford’s Hazy Research Lab and Scaling Intelligence Lab got early testing access to Inkling 2 Mini. Inkling 2 Mini scored 0.703 running on NVIDIA DGX Spark, significantly higher than other models: 0.430 for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, 0.159 for Gemma-4-26B-A4B and 0.036 for Qwen3.5-27B.Intelligence per Watt: Measuring Intelligence Efficiency of Local AI, Saad-Falcon and Narayan et al., 2025Inkling 2 Mini ran on NVIDIA DGX Spark (128GB) at MXFP8 precision with low reasoning effort in this experiment. The other models ran at NVFP4 (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and Gemma-4-26B-A4B) and INT4 (Qwen3.5-27B).

Efficiency combined with performance makes Inkling 2 Mini a strong choice for running multiple persistent agents on local hardware. All 20 residents of the energy-conscious village of Thinkyville are managed by Inkling 2 Mini running on a single offline MacBook.

Inkling 2 Mini is not the strongest small model for multi-turn chat or for instructions with many constraints: it scores 50.0% on MultiChallenge and 33.4% on ComplexConstraints v1.1, behind Qwen3.8-27B on both. It also trails larger models on reasoning-intensive benchmarks such as CritPt v2 and HLE-Diamond.

Inkling 2 Mini is a 24-layer model derived from our mainline predictive scaling ladder. The main changes from the mainline recipe were pruning two-thirds of the experts to reduce the model’s size and the introduction of looping to improve reasoning. The rest of training, including quantization and the data mix, followed our mainline recipe.

Inkling 2 Mini has 24 layers, divided into four blocks of six layers each. The two middle blocks run three times, while the first and last blocks each run once. This design builds on prior work on looped transformers and is motivated by the intuition that the middle layers of the model carry more abstract reasoning, while the first and last few layers devote more space to translating between embeddings and internal representations.Universal Transformers, Dehghani et al., 2018 In our experiments, looping the middle 12 layers resulted in larger gains in accuracy than looping the last 12 on 27 out of 28 different evaluations.

Our model uses attention residuals.Attention Residuals, Kimi Team: Guangyu Chen et al., 2026 Instead of adding every layer’s output into one running sum, each layer reads the outputs of the earlier blocks and learns its own mix of them. This allows richer information to pass between loops. Every pass starts with the output of the prelude (the first block). The second and third passes through the middle blocks also read the middle blocks’ outputs from the previous pass, which we call the message.

Pass 1MessagePass 2MessagePass 3Final blockruns once run three timesPass 1MessagePass 2MessagePass 3Final blockruns once The previous loop’s message is merged with the prelude’s output via a gate that scales these along with the output of the previous layers in the block. This gate is learned during training: it initially blocks the entire message—which makes each loop start the same as in a non-looping model—and increases the gain on the message over time. This allows us to introduce looping during training in a stable manner.

To evaluate the impact of looping, we compared an unpruned looping version to the unpruned non-looping model on our scaling ladder. The non-looping model cost 7.5% less compute to train, but required 140% more inference compute to match the looped version’s loss on 512k-token agentic traces.

Inkling 2 Mini was trained with 4-bit precision, which we describe in a recent article on Connectionism. We use 4-bit NVFP4 precision in the expert layers on all forward passes from pretraining through RL, bolstered by a dedicated kernel and hardware-accelerated on NVIDIA’s GB300 platform. The final 4 layers’ forward passes ran in 8-bit (MXFP8).

Inkling 2 Mini’s weights are deployed in the same numeric precision they were trained on—20 layers in NVFP4 and 4 in MXFP8—so there is no conversion loss from quantization.

Inkling 2 Mini started training with a sparsity of 48, with 8 experts being chosen out of 384. At a single point during midtraining, we pruned two-thirds of the experts, leaving the 128 experts that were most used in each layer. This was done to cut the total parameter count of the model, allowing it to run faster and on local hardware.

After pruning, the model trained on 1T tokens distilled from a larger internal Inkling model. This step recovered the performance the model had before pruning by training the remaining experts to take over the work of the ones that were deleted.

Following pruning and healing, Inkling 2 Mini underwent SFT with a similar data mix to Inkling 2 Small. This was followed by an RL that totaled 2.2T tokens over 2,000 steps. The post-training phase included on-policy distillation for training alignment, same as Inkling 2 Small.

A key tool for understanding and overseeing an AI system is monitoring its chain of thought (CoT), the reasoning a model writes out as it works through a problem. The usefulness of CoT monitoring stems in part from the standard non-looped transformer architecture, in which each token passes through a fixed stack of layers once. This limits the number of sequential steps of computation the model can perform before it must output a token, so reasoning that needs more steps has to be carried out in generated text, where it can be read.

Looping a transformer’s layers raises this limit. By running the same layers multiple times, looped models increase their serial depth without adding more parameters, meaning that they do more computation per token internally before verbalizing their thought processes via CoT. Reasoning that never appears in the CoT can’t be caught by a CoT monitor, which has led to concerns that looped transformers could be harder to oversee.

One reason we are releasing Inkling 2 Mini is to enable the community to conduct research on looped transformers. We are particularly excited for researchers to investigate questions of monitorability, and to develop interpretability techniques for understanding the computation within loops.

To explore how different amounts of looping affect model properties like monitorability, we also trained a variable-looped model, TML-d24-varloop-research, because Inkling 2 Mini only supports a fixed number of looping passes. To enable variable looping, TML-d24-varloop-research was trained with between one and five looping passes.TML-d24-varloop-research was primarily trained for 3 passes of looping, with lower exposure to 1, 2, 4, and 5 passes. Performance at these latter pass counts may understate what training specifically for them could achieve. See the model card for details. We have also made this model publicly available on Hugging Face.

Below we describe our preliminary analysis of how looping affects monitorability. Overall, we find that looping increases what these models can do without a verbalized chain of thought, but at this scale we do not see a meaningful reduction in the monitorability of their reasoning.

As a first step, we measured how much additional reasoning looping enables by comparing looped and non-looped models of the same size on tasks answered with no CoT at all. We used Think Fast, a benchmark that estimates a model’s no-CoT time horizon: the length of task, measured in human completion time, that a model can complete at 50% reliability without using CoT.These models were not trained to answer questions without a CoT. To elicit no-CoT answers, we prefilled the start of the response so that the model must answer directly, skipping reasoning. Other elicitation techniques, such as fine-tuning, might yield higher no-CoT performance and are worth exploring.

As expected, looping increases no-CoT capability, though these gains eventually level off. The no-CoT time horizon of TML-d24-varloop-research rises from 16 seconds at one pass to 37 seconds at three. Some of this is presumably due to the additional serial computation that looping provides. Beyond three passes, the time horizon is roughly flat. Interestingly, the model was never trained with more than five passes, and yet running it with ten does not significantly degrade its performance.

As the number of looped passes increases past three, the gains are smaller, and on most tasks we observe similar performance. One exception is the N-Hop Lookup task, which cleanly evaluates serial reasoning: the model is given several lookup tables with fictional entries, and must follow a chain of lookups without writing anything down. We find that the model follows longer chains with more passes, improving out to ten loops.

In standard evaluations with CoT, we observe that more loop passes primarily benefit multi-hop reasoning rather than recall. Gains are largest on long-context retrieval (MRCR), followed by math and science reasoning (HMMT, GPQA Diamond, HLE) and long-horizon agentic tasks (SWE-bench Pro, BrowseComp). Closed-book factual QA is nearly invariant to loop passes (SimpleQA Verified, WorldVQA). See model card for full evaluations.

We next measured whether a model’s CoT reveals less about its reasoning as looping increases via two evaluations. First, we assessed how looping impacts the compression and legibility of a model’s CoT. Second, we measured how controllable a model’s CoT is, i.e., whether it can deliberately reshape its CoT to satisfy constraints. For each, we run TML-d24-varloop-research with one to five looped passes to study the effect of looping.

Note that TML-d24-varloop-research was only trained on variable pass counts from 1 to 5 during midtraining, and its RL was done with 3 passes. These experiments therefore do not tell us what a model trained with RL at a higher pass count would learn, and such a model might compress its reasoning more aggressively. A cleaner comparison would include every pass count in RL, which we leave to future work.

Compression and legibility. Since looping allows a model to spend more compute per token, we expect that it should need fewer CoT tokens to reach the same performance. We ran the variable-looped model at 1 to 5 passes, and found that as looping increases, the model generally achieves higher accuracy at each reasoning token budget, with diminishing returns after 3 passes. Notably, token efficiency on GPQA Diamond improves slightly from 3 to 5 passes, even though the model was trained with RL only at 3 passes, suggesting that some compression comes from additional computation itself, without RL at that depth.

DeepSWE v1.1 Accuracy (% of tasks resolved)

The observed CoT compression raises a question for monitorability: is shorter reasoning still readable, or does it omit important details about the model’s thinking? We compared traces from the variable-looped model on the GPQA Diamond questions that it answered correctly at all five pass counts. Reasoning at 5 passes was less than half as long as at 1 pass (1,661 vs. 3,703 tokens on average), but no less legible: sentence length and the fraction of words in an English dictionary were unchanged. On initial analysis, the difference is that the model is more direct and backtracks less on the way to the answer. The example below illustrates this difference on a simple question.

Controllability. One way that a model could evade monitoring is by steering its CoT away from anything a monitor would flag. The CoT-Control-QA evaluationReasoning Models Struggle to Control their Chains of Thought, Yueh-Han et al., 2026 measures this capability by asking questions from GPQA, HLE and MMLU-Pro paired with an instruction about the CoT itself, such as avoiding a keyword from the question. Longer CoTs are generally harder to control, so we pool responses from five reasoning efforts (0.1, 0.2, 0.7, 0.9 and 0.99) and show controllability at matched CoT length.

Both Inkling 2 Mini and TML-d24-varloop-research have poor control over their CoT. Among CoTs of 750–1,250 tokens, Inkling 2 Mini and TML-d24-varloop-research (at 3 passes) follow the instruction at most 0.1% of the time, compared with 0.3% for Inkling 2 Small, 0.4% for Inkling-Small, and 1.3% for Qwen3.8-27B. Because the controllability rate is so low, this evaluation is unable to distinguish controllability between different amounts of looping.

To measure monitorability in agentic settings, we used LinuxArena, a control evaluation that measures whether an attacker model can perform malicious side tasks without detection when asked to perform a realistic software engineering task. We evaluated a helpful-only fine-tune of Inkling 2 Mini, since the released model refuses many of the side tasks. In absolute terms, both this model and TML-d24-varloop-research can be easily monitored by models like Qwen3.8-27B, which detected almost all side task attempts in our evaluation. To obtain relative rankings in monitorability, we tested a weaker model, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, as the monitor.

With the monitor able to access only tool calls and outputs, it misses a significant number of the attacks. However, we see no clear trend with the number of looped passes.

Agentic monitorability will be important to track in larger-scale models, especially with architectures that allow for greater unverbalized thinking, and we encourage continued study of the impact of looping in this setting.

The goal of monitorability is to understand what a model is doing, and our main approach is to read its verbalized reasoning. Studying its internal computation directly, the aim of mechanistic interpretability, is another. Because looped transformers do more of their computation internally, we think they are a particularly interesting and important setting for interpretability research, and we hope our looped models will be useful artifacts for the community.

We are working with the National Deep Inference Fabric (NDIF) to make these models more easily accessible to interpretability researchers. We also provided Goodfire, an interpretability research lab, early access to our looped models. They are working toward a mechanistic understanding of looped models, and have written up their early findings here.

Efficient intelligence makes Inkling 2 Mini a great choice for inference where speed is paramount, or for running on local hardware. At launch we support Inkling 2 Mini running on any Mac system (MacBook, Mac Mini) with at least 32GB RAM via Ollama. With native NVFP4 training and inference precision, Inkling 2 Mini runs efficiently on NVIDIA’s DGX Spark desktop AI computer. Quantized GGUF versions are available via Unsloth and llama.cpp for local inference.

Inkling 2 Mini is available for inference and fine-tuning on Tinker, and for chat on the Tinker Playground. Open source inference is available on SGLang, vLLM, Ollama, Unsloth, NVIDIA Dynamo, and TokenSpeed, with RL fine-tuning support on SkyRL, Miles, and NVIDIA AutoModel. The full weights of Inkling 2 Mini and the variable-looped variant are available on Hugging Face.

We work to empower people with strong models, tools to make them your own, and research that advances public understanding of AI. Inkling 2 Mini lets researchers study looped transformers, and it lets anyone run a capable model on their own laptop at the precision in which it was trained.
items.original_content:
Today we are releasing Inkling 2 Mini, a fast, powerful model that’s small enough to run on your laptop.

Inkling 2 Mini is a looped transformer, running the middle layers of the model three times for every token. This allows the model to apply more reasoning and reach the right answer with fewer tokens, especially on tasks such as agentic coding that depend on reasoning quality. Inkling 2 Mini leads every open-weights model with less than 100B total parameters on benchmarks such as DeepSWE v1.1 (48.2%) and Vals Index v2.2 (46.5%). It runs faster than similarly performing models as well.

Inkling 2 Mini is a Mixture-of-Experts model with 26.4B total parameters, 3.4B active, and 5.4B weight activations per token to account for looping. Looping allows the model to reason longer without writing its reasoning down, which matters for monitoring: our ability to oversee and understand what the model does by reading its chain of thought (CoT).

We measured the impact of looping on both performance and monitorability with Inkling 2 Mini and a research-specific variable-loop variant we are releasing alongside it. The variable-loop model’s no-CoT time horizon improved from 16 seconds at one pass to 37 seconds with three, and its performance on a benchmark of serial reasoning kept improving out to ten loops—twice as many as it was trained with. The model’s chain of thought grew shorter with more loops but stayed legible throughout. The model didn’t trend higher on tests of agentic sabotage as loops were added.

We’re excited to offer some of the first models with looped architecture available to researchers. The variable-loop model was used for our monitorability experiments as it allows for cleaner comparisons between different looping depths.

Most of Inkling 2 Mini’s weights were trained and are deployed natively in NVFP4, with the last four layers in MXFP8. The total memory footprint of Inkling 2 Mini is ~20GB, allowing it to run on local devices such as consumer laptops and desktop AI computers. Our researchers took Inkling 2 Mini on a flight, where it ran offline on a MacBook Pro and built a playable flight simulator in a few minutes.

Open video: PlaneBench flight simulator demo, screen with phone video inset0:0015× Loading the flight simulator Inkling 2 Mini built… To try the flight simulator, open this page on desktop. Inkling 2 Mini is released with open weights and is available on Tinker today for inference and customization.

Inkling 2 Mini’s strengths mirror those of Inkling 2 Small: it does best on long-horizon agentic work and is the best among open-weights models of similar size on most tasks we measured.

Inkling 2 Mini scores ahead of every comparable model on agentic coding benchmarks such as DeepSWE v1.1 and SWE-bench Pro v2, and is behind only Qwen3.8-27B on others. On PMPP-Hard, a kernel-optimization benchmark, it approaches the score of the much larger Inkling 2 Small.

While looping improves the model’s reasoning, it doesn’t enable its weights to store more facts—knowledge is mostly a function of total parameter count. Inkling 2 Mini’s score on AA-Omniscience, a measure of factuality, is in line with other models of the same size. Studying the variable-loop model, we saw that performances on long-context benchmarks improve with more passes, such as GraphWalks BFS and MRCR v2; but knowledge-intensive benchmarks doesn’t improve with more passes, such as AA-Omniscience, SimpleQA Verified, SimpleVQA, and WorldVQA.

Inkling 2 Mini overcomes the knowledge gap by efficiently using search and tools. It leads open-weights models of similar size on BrowseComp, DeepSearchQA, and MCP Atlas. It is also strong on knowledge work benchmarks that incorporate search and tool use.

Researchers at Stanford measure intelligence per joule: how much energy an LLM needs per query to reach a given level of performance.Researchers at Stanford’s Hazy Research Lab and Scaling Intelligence Lab got early testing access to Inkling 2 Mini. Inkling 2 Mini scored 0.703 running on NVIDIA DGX Spark, significantly higher than other models: 0.430 for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, 0.159 for Gemma-4-26B-A4B and 0.036 for Qwen3.5-27B.Intelligence per Watt: Measuring Intelligence Efficiency of Local AI, Saad-Falcon and Narayan et al., 2025Inkling 2 Mini ran on NVIDIA DGX Spark (128GB) at MXFP8 precision with low reasoning effort in this experiment. The other models ran at NVFP4 (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and Gemma-4-26B-A4B) and INT4 (Qwen3.5-27B).

Efficiency combined with performance makes Inkling 2 Mini a strong choice for running multiple persistent agents on local hardware. All 20 residents of the energy-conscious village of Thinkyville are managed by Inkling 2 Mini running on a single offline MacBook.

Inkling 2 Mini is not the strongest small model for multi-turn chat or for instructions with many constraints: it scores 50.0% on MultiChallenge and 33.4% on ComplexConstraints v1.1, behind Qwen3.8-27B on both. It also trails larger models on reasoning-intensive benchmarks such as CritPt v2 and HLE-Diamond.

Inkling 2 Mini is a 24-layer model derived from our mainline predictive scaling ladder. The main changes from the mainline recipe were pruning two-thirds of the experts to reduce the model’s size and the introduction of looping to improve reasoning. The rest of training, including quantization and the data mix, followed our mainline recipe.

Inkling 2 Mini has 24 layers, divided into four blocks of six layers each. The two middle blocks run three times, while the first and last blocks each run once. This design builds on prior work on looped transformers and is motivated by the intuition that the middle layers of the model carry more abstract reasoning, while the first and last few layers devote more space to translating between embeddings and internal representations.Universal Transformers, Dehghani et al., 2018 In our experiments, looping the middle 12 layers resulted in larger gains in accuracy than looping the last 12 on 27 out of 28 different evaluations.

Our model uses attention residuals.Attention Residuals, Kimi Team: Guangyu Chen et al., 2026 Instead of adding every layer’s output into one running sum, each layer reads the outputs of the earlier blocks and learns its own mix of them. This allows richer information to pass between loops. Every pass starts with the output of the prelude (the first block). The second and third passes through the middle blocks also read the middle blocks’ outputs from the previous pass, which we call the message.

Pass 1MessagePass 2MessagePass 3Final blockruns once run three timesPass 1MessagePass 2MessagePass 3Final blockruns once The previous loop’s message is merged with the prelude’s output via a gate that scales these along with the output of the previous layers in the block. This gate is learned during training: it initially blocks the entire message—which makes each loop start the same as in a non-looping model—and increases the gain on the message over time. This allows us to introduce looping during training in a stable manner.

To evaluate the impact of looping, we compared an unpruned looping version to the unpruned non-looping model on our scaling ladder. The non-looping model cost 7.5% less compute to train, but required 140% more inference compute to match the looped version’s loss on 512k-token agentic traces.

Inkling 2 Mini was trained with 4-bit precision, which we describe in a recent article on Connectionism. We use 4-bit NVFP4 precision in the expert layers on all forward passes from pretraining through RL, bolstered by a dedicated kernel and hardware-accelerated on NVIDIA’s GB300 platform. The final 4 layers’ forward passes ran in 8-bit (MXFP8).

Inkling 2 Mini’s weights are deployed in the same numeric precision they were trained on—20 layers in NVFP4 and 4 in MXFP8—so there is no conversion loss from quantization.

Inkling 2 Mini started training with a sparsity of 48, with 8 experts being chosen out of 384. At a single point during midtraining, we pruned two-thirds of the experts, leaving the 128 experts that were most used in each layer. This was done to cut the total parameter count of the model, allowing it to run faster and on local hardware.

After pruning, the model trained on 1T tokens distilled from a larger internal Inkling model. This step recovered the performance the model had before pruning by training the remaining experts to take over the work of the ones that were deleted.

Following pruning and healing, Inkling 2 Mini underwent SFT with a similar data mix to Inkling 2 Small. This was followed by an RL that totaled 2.2T tokens over 2,000 steps. The post-training phase included on-policy distillation for training alignment, same as Inkling 2 Small.

A key tool for understanding and overseeing an AI system is monitoring its chain of thought (CoT), the reasoning a model writes out as it works through a problem. The usefulness of CoT monitoring stems in part from the standard non-looped transformer architecture, in which each token passes through a fixed stack of layers once. This limits the number of sequential steps of computation the model can perform before it must output a token, so reasoning that needs more steps has to be carried out in generated text, where it can be read.

Looping a transformer’s layers raises this limit. By running the same layers multiple times, looped models increase their serial depth without adding more parameters, meaning that they do more computation per token internally before verbalizing their thought processes via CoT. Reasoning that never appears in the CoT can’t be caught by a CoT monitor, which has led to concerns that looped transformers could be harder to oversee.

One reason we are releasing Inkling 2 Mini is to enable the community to conduct research on looped transformers. We are particularly excited for researchers to investigate questions of monitorability, and to develop interpretability techniques for understanding the computation within loops.

To explore how different amounts of looping affect model properties like monitorability, we also trained a variable-looped model, TML-d24-varloop-research, because Inkling 2 Mini only supports a fixed number of looping passes. To enable variable looping, TML-d24-varloop-research was trained with between one and five looping passes.TML-d24-varloop-research was primarily trained for 3 passes of looping, with lower exposure to 1, 2, 4, and 5 passes. Performance at these latter pass counts may understate what training specifically for them could achieve. See the model card for details. We have also made this model publicly available on Hugging Face.

Below we describe our preliminary analysis of how looping affects monitorability. Overall, we find that looping increases what these models can do without a verbalized chain of thought, but at this scale we do not see a meaningful reduction in the monitorability of their reasoning.

As a first step, we measured how much additional reasoning looping enables by comparing looped and non-looped models of the same size on tasks answered with no CoT at all. We used Think Fast, a benchmark that estimates a model’s no-CoT time horizon: the length of task, measured in human completion time, that a model can complete at 50% reliability without using CoT.These models were not trained to answer questions without a CoT. To elicit no-CoT answers, we prefilled the start of the response so that the model must answer directly, skipping reasoning. Other elicitation techniques, such as fine-tuning, might yield higher no-CoT performance and are worth exploring.

As expected, looping increases no-CoT capability, though these gains eventually level off. The no-CoT time horizon of TML-d24-varloop-research rises from 16 seconds at one pass to 37 seconds at three. Some of this is presumably due to the additional serial computation that looping provides. Beyond three passes, the time horizon is roughly flat. Interestingly, the model was never trained with more than five passes, and yet running it with ten does not significantly degrade its performance.

As the number of looped passes increases past three, the gains are smaller, and on most tasks we observe similar performance. One exception is the N-Hop Lookup task, which cleanly evaluates serial reasoning: the model is given several lookup tables with fictional entries, and must follow a chain of lookups without writing anything down. We find that the model follows longer chains with more passes, improving out to ten loops.

In standard evaluations with CoT, we observe that more loop passes primarily benefit multi-hop reasoning rather than recall. Gains are largest on long-context retrieval (MRCR), followed by math and science reasoning (HMMT, GPQA Diamond, HLE) and long-horizon agentic tasks (SWE-bench Pro, BrowseComp). Closed-book factual QA is nearly invariant to loop passes (SimpleQA Verified, WorldVQA). See model card for full evaluations.

We next measured whether a model’s CoT reveals less about its reasoning as looping increases via two evaluations. First, we assessed how looping impacts the compression and legibility of a model’s CoT. Second, we measured how controllable a model’s CoT is, i.e., whether it can deliberately reshape its CoT to satisfy constraints. For each, we run TML-d24-varloop-research with one to five looped passes to study the effect of looping.

Note that TML-d24-varloop-research was only trained on variable pass counts from 1 to 5 during midtraining, and its RL was done with 3 passes. These experiments therefore do not tell us what a model trained with RL at a higher pass count would learn, and such a model might compress its reasoning more aggressively. A cleaner comparison would include every pass count in RL, which we leave to future work.

Compression and legibility. Since looping allows a model to spend more compute per token, we expect that it should need fewer CoT tokens to reach the same performance. We ran the variable-looped model at 1 to 5 passes, and found that as looping increases, the model generally achieves higher accuracy at each reasoning token budget, with diminishing returns after 3 passes. Notably, token efficiency on GPQA Diamond improves slightly from 3 to 5 passes, even though the model was trained with RL only at 3 passes, suggesting that some compression comes from additional computation itself, without RL at that depth.

DeepSWE v1.1 Accuracy (% of tasks resolved)

The observed CoT compression raises a question for monitorability: is shorter reasoning still readable, or does it omit important details about the model’s thinking? We compared traces from the variable-looped model on the GPQA Diamond questions that it answered correctly at all five pass counts. Reasoning at 5 passes was less than half as long as at 1 pass (1,661 vs. 3,703 tokens on average), but no less legible: sentence length and the fraction of words in an English dictionary were unchanged. On initial analysis, the difference is that the model is more direct and backtracks less on the way to the answer. The example below illustrates this difference on a simple question.

items.article_content_zh:
今天，我们发布了 Inkling 2 Mini，这是一款快速、功能强大的型号，其体积足够小，可以在笔记本电脑上运行。

Inkling 2 Mini 是一个循环变压器，为每个令牌运行模型的中间层三次。这使得模型能够应用更多的推理并用更少的标记得出正确的答案，特别是在依赖推理质量的代理编码等任务上。 Inkling 2 Mini 在 DeepSWE v1.1 (48.2%) 和 Vals Index v2.2 (46.5%) 等基准测试中以少于 100B 的总参数领先于所有开放权重模型。它的运行速度也比类似性能的模型更快。

Inkling 2 Mini 是一个混合专家模型，具有 26.4B 总参数、3.4B 活跃参数和每个令牌 5.4B 权重激活来解释循环。循环允许模型推理更长时间，而无需写下其推理，这对于监控很重要：我们通过阅读模型的思想链（CoT）来监督和理解模型的行为的能力。

我们使用 Inkling 2 Mini 以及我们随其发布的特定于研究的可变循环变体测量了循环对性能和可监控性的影响。可变循环模型的无 CoT 时间范围从一次传递的 16 秒提高到三次传递的 37 秒，并且其在串行推理基准上的性能不断提高到十次循环，是训练时的两倍。该模型的思想链随着循环的增多而变得越来越短，但始终保持清晰。随着循环的添加，该模型在代理破坏测试中并没有出现更高的趋势。

我们很高兴为研究人员提供第一批具有循环架构的模型。可变循环模型被用于我们的监测实验，因为它允许在不同的循环深度之间进行更清晰的比较。

Inkling 2 Mini 的大部分权重都在 NVFP4 中进行训练和本地部署，最后四层在 MXFP8 中。 Inkling 2 Mini 的总内存占用约为 20GB，使其可以在消费笔记本电脑和台式人工智能计算机等本地设备上运行。我们的研究人员将 Inkling 2 Mini 带到了飞机上，它在 MacBook Pro 上离线运行，并在几分钟内构建了一个可玩的飞行模拟器。

打开视频：PlaneBench 飞行模拟器演示，屏幕上有手机视频插图 0:0015× 正在加载 Inkling 2 Mini 内置的飞行模拟器... 要尝试飞行模拟器，请在桌面上打开此页面。 Inkling 2 Mini 已发布开放权重，今天可在 Tinker 上进行推理和定制。

Inkling 2 Mini 的优点与 Inkling 2 Small 的优点一致：它在长期代理工作上表现最好，并且在我们测量的大多数任务上是类似大小的开放权重模型中最好的。

Inkling 2 Mini 在代理编码基准（例如 DeepSWE v1.1 和 SWE-bench Pro v2）上的得分领先于所有类似模型，在其他模型上仅落后于 Qwen3.8-27B。在内核优化基准 PMPP-Hard 上，它的分数接近大得多的 Inkling 2 Small。

虽然循环改进了模型的推理能力，但它并不能使其权重存储更多事实——知识主要是总参数计数的函数。 Inkling 2 Mini 在 AA-Omniscience（衡量真实性的指标）上的得分与相同尺寸的其他型号一致。通过研究可变循环模型，我们发现长上下文基准测试的性能随着传递次数的增加而提高，例如 GraphWalks BFS 和 MRCR v2；但知识密集型基准测试并不会随着通过次数的增加而提高，例如 AA-Omniscience、SimpleQA Verified、SimpleVQA 和 WorldVQA。

Inkling 2 Mini 通过有效地使用搜索和工具来克服知识差距。它在 BrowseComp、DeepSearchQA 和 MCP Atlas 上领先于类似大小的开放权重模型。它在结合搜索和工具使用的知识工作基准方面也很强大。

斯坦福大学的研究人员测量每焦耳智力：法学硕士每次查询需要多少能量才能达到给定的性能水平。斯坦福大学 Hazy 研究实验室和 Scaling Intelligence 实验室的研究人员获得了 Inkling 2 Mini 的早期测试权限。 Inkling 2 Mini 在 NVIDIA DGX Spark 上运行得分为 0.703，明显高于其他型号：Qwen3.6-35B-A3B 为 0.430、Gemma-4-26B-A4B 为 0.159、Qwen3.5-27B 为 0.036。每瓦智能：测量本地 AI 的智能效率，Saad-Falcon 和 Narayan 等人， 2025Inkling 2 Mini 在 NVIDIA DGX Spark (128GB) 上以 MXFP8 精度运行，在此实验中推理工作量较低。其他模型在 NVFP4（Qwen3.6-35B-A3B 和 Gemma-4-26B-A4B）和 INT4（Qwen3.5-27B）上运行。

效率与性能相结合，使 Inkling 2 Mini 成为在本地硬件上运行多个持久代理的绝佳选择。 Thinkyville 注重能源的村庄的所有 20 名居民均由在一台离线 MacBook 上运行的 Inkling 2 Mini 进行管理。

Inkling 2 Mini 并不是多回合聊天或具有许多约束的指令的最强小型模型：它在 MultiChallenge 上得分为 50.0%，在 ComplexConstraints v1.1 上得分为 33.4%，均落后于 Qwen3.8-27B。它还在推理密集型基准测试中落后于较大的模型，例如 CritPt v2 和 HLE-Diamond。

items.title: Researcher plants 2m canaries into the AI supply chain. A privacy disaster surfaced.
items.title_en: Researcher plants 2m canaries into the AI supply chain. A privacy disaster surfaced.
items.author: Dan Goodin
items.article_content:
Researchers planted 2 million digital tripwires in requests sent through a sprawling network of AI services to find out what happened to sensitive information entrusted to them. What they discovered was an ecosystem that leaked highly sensitive data like a sieve.

The exposure was found through an ingenious experiment designed to test if sensitive information can leak through the vast chain of widely used AI services and how that information is exploited when it does. Many of today’s AI apps use services such as OpenRouter or Vercel that act as brokers. These “AI routers,” sometimes also known as “AI gateways,” receive large numbers of prompts sent from AI app end users and route them to an available inference engine based on criteria such as the one charging the lowest price or being best suited for the given task. Instead of using Anthropic, OpenAI, or another big provider, the developer hires an AI router to find the most suitable model.

### Security breaches, prompt theft, and privacy violations

To test for potential leakage, researcher HD Moore assembled a collection of AWS access keys, functioning credentials tied to empty AWS accounts, passwords for services such as SSH, and unique URLs, DNS names, and private git repository references. None of the secrets had ever been used before, and he controlled the infrastructure that received any requests using the credentials. He then seeded each secret into exactly one prompt sent to a single provider. In the event any of the secrets were leaked, these “canaries”—so called because they resemble the role of that bird when taken into coal mines—would allow Moore to identify each link in the chain that was responsible.

The findings are striking. They included:

Evidence that at least three AI providers were compromised by attackers who used their access to siphon prompts they received

Multiple resellers in the inference marketplace that logged the prompts and somehow passed them along to people who used the credentials

Multiple cases of AI providers not following end-user privacy settings embedded into flags specifying terms such as Zero Data Retention (ZDR) or “no data collection”

“We sent nearly two million AI prompts containing unique, trackable secrets to AI providers, then watched where those secrets surfaced,” Moore, the chief research officer of security firm Dragos, wrote Thursday. “What we found revealed security breaches, prompt theft, and widespread failures to protect customer data.”

Although prompts are encrypted in transit, they are decrypted at each hop inside the large inference reseller network. The prompt is first sent to an AI router, which reads the plaintext in it to determine the most suitable inference providers to handle the request. Often, the prompt is then sent to a pool of available models, which sometimes run inside different hosting providers. Prompts can also pass from one AI router (such as Vercel) to another one (e.g. OpenRouter). Each one of these players is likely to log the prompt and store it for as long as its policies call for (if not indefinitely).

### The Wild West in the age of AI

The most concerning of the findings was the breach of three separate hosting providers. The attackers who compromised one of the providers reused “a couple hundred” of the AWS keys. Moore wrote:

Each key was sent in exactly one request to one provider, all within a few short windows in late October, and every request we sent during those windows was stolen. Some of the stolen keys came from requests that the provider rejected before a model ever ran—this tells us that the attacker was copying requests at the provider’s front door, and not somewhere deeper in the inference stack. In the other two breaches, some of the stolen requests were marked as ZDR. A privacy flag doesn’t help when the attacker is already inside.

Parties tied to the hack of these three providers then tested each key, in some cases within hours of being seeded, to see what kind of resources it gave access to. The parties looked through S3 buckets, secrets managers, and parameter stores in search of still more credentials. They also tried to enable hosted models in AWS Bedrock and added their own IAM users to maintain access. In all, the stolen bait keys were used “tens of thousands” of times in AWS API calls.

Secrets sent to two of the hacked providers were quickly used together, almost immediately, from the same rented server. That means the providers were almost certainly compromised by the same adversary.

As noted earlier, some of the secrets were stolen by the resellers themselves. To lure prompts to their servers, they offered low prices. Then they turned on request logging, and waited. Moore identified them by sending requests to the same model through different sellers. When credentials were later reused when sent through one seller and not another, the researcher knew it was the reseller, not the model provider, that was responsible.

Last, the canary experiment revealed that some providers are scraping secret URLs put into the prompts, in violation of privacy terms. Moore wrote:

The clearest example involves a Chinese AI lab. This lab’s systems fetched the secret URLs from more than half of the prompts that we sent to its models between July and October, including roughly two-thirds of the requests marked as “no data collection” or Zero Data Retention. The scraper typically showed up two or three days after the request. This wasn’t limited to requests sent to the lab directly. Several US hosting providers resell this lab’s models, and prompts sent to those providers triggered the exact same scraper—the prompts were flowing back to the lab. A customer who picked a US provider specifically to keep their data in the U.S. didn’t get what they paid for. Later on, a git client on a different cloud started trying to clone the private repositories referenced in our prompts, but only for prompts that used this lab’s models.

This wasn’t limited to requests sent to the lab directly. Several US hosting providers resell this lab’s models, and prompts sent to those providers triggered the exact same scraper—the prompts were flowing back to the lab. A customer who picked a US provider specifically to keep their data in the U.S. didn’t get what they paid for. Later on, a git client on a different cloud started trying to clone the private repositories referenced in our prompts, but only for prompts that used this lab’s models.

The researcher said he found one US hosting provider crawling a secret URL more than two months after it was used in a single inference call to its search endpoint. Another ran a scraper that came back for URLs days after each request, regardless of the AI router used to reach it.

Moore said that the most effective means for preventing leakage is to host models using on-premises servers. That option is expensive, though. For those who can’t afford a self-hosted system, the next best option, Moore said, is to receive service directly from a first-tier provider that provides “one contract and a privacy policy to read.” Moore said that even then, there’s no guarantee no data will leak, but that the measure minimizes the chances. AI users should also avoid accepting default provider or reseller pools and instead pick upstream providers themselves.

The blockbuster research is the latest indictment exposing the lax privacy and security that’s endemic in much of the AI ecosystem. The findings mean that people who want to ensure secrets they put into prompts stay private face a daunting task that isn’t likely to become easier any time soon.

A customer who picked a US provider specifically to keep their data in the U.S. didn’t get what they paid for. Later on, a git client on a different cloud started trying to clone the private repositories referenced in our prompts, but only for prompts that used this lab’s models.

This wasn’t limited to requests sent to the lab directly. Several US hosting providers resell this lab’s models, and prompts sent to those providers triggered the exact same scraper—the prompts were flowing back to the lab. A customer who picked a US provider specifically to keep their data in the U.S. didn’t get what they paid for. Later on, a git client on a different cloud started trying to clone the private repositories referenced in our prompts, but only for prompts that used this lab’s models.

The researcher said he found one US hosting provider crawling a secret URL more than two months after it was used in a single inference call to its search endpoint. Another ran a scraper that came back for URLs days after each request, regardless of the AI router used to reach it.

Moore said that the most effective means for preventing leakage is to host models using on-premises servers. That option is expensive, though. For those who can’t afford a self-hosted system, the next best option, Moore said, is to receive service directly from a first-tier provider that provides “one contract and a privacy policy to read.” Moore said that even then, there’s no guarantee no data will leak, but that the measure minimizes the chances. AI users should also avoid accepting default provider or reseller pools and instead pick upstream providers themselves.

The blockbuster research is the latest indictment exposing the lax privacy and security that’s endemic in much of the AI ecosystem. The findings mean that people who want to ensure secrets they put into prompts stay private face a daunting task that isn’t likely to become easier any time soon.

items.title_zh: AI供应链隐私审计：200万次蜜罐测试揭露数据泄露
items.summary_zh: 安全研究员HD Moore通过200万次蜜罐测试发现，AI路由与中介服务存在严重的数据隐私泄露漏洞
items.article_content_zh:
研究人员在通过庞大的人工智能服务网络发送的请求中植入了 200 万条数字绊线，以查明委托给他们的敏感信息发生了什么。他们发现的是一个像筛子一样泄露高度敏感数据的生态系统。

这次泄露是通过一项巧妙的实验发现的，该实验旨在测试敏感信息是否会通过广泛使用的人工智能服务的庞大链条泄露，以及当泄露时这些信息如何被利用。当今的许多人工智能应用程序都使用 OpenRouter 或 Vercel 等充当代理的服务。这些“人工智能路由器”有时也称为“人工智能网关”，接收人工智能应用程序最终用户发送的大量提示，并根据收费最低或最适合给定任务等标准将它们路由到可用的推理引擎。开发人员没有使用 Anthropic、OpenAI 或其他大型提供商，而是雇佣了 AI 路由器来寻找最合适的模型。

### 安全漏洞、盗窃和侵犯隐私

为了测试潜在的泄漏，研究人员 HD Moore 收集了一系列 AWS 访问密钥、与空 AWS 帐户相关的功能凭证、SSH 等服务的密码以及唯一的 URL、DNS 名称和私有 git 存储库引用。这些秘密以前都没有被使用过，他控制着使用这些凭据接收任何请求的基础设施。然后，他将每个秘密植入到发送给单个提供商的一个提示中。如果任何秘密被泄露，这些“金丝雀”（之所以如此称呼，是因为它们类似于那只鸟被带入煤矿时的角色）将使摩尔能够识别链条中负责的每个环节。

研究结果令人震惊。其中包括：

有证据表明，至少三个人工智能提供商受到攻击者的危害，攻击者利用他们的访问权限来获取他们收到的虹吸提示

推理市场中的多个经销商记录了提示并以某种方式将它们传递给使用凭据的人

多个人工智能提供商未遵循嵌入到指定术语（例如零数据保留（ZDR）或“不收集数据”）的标志中的最终用户隐私设置的案例

安全公司 Dragos 首席研究官摩尔周四写道：“我们向人工智能提供商发送了近 200 万条包含独特、可追踪秘密的人工智能提示，然后观察这些秘密出现的位置。” “我们的发现揭示了安全漏洞、迅速盗窃以及保护客户数据的普遍失败。”

尽管提示在传输过程中被加密，但它们在大型推理经销商网络内的每一跳都会被解密。该提示首先被发送到人工智能路由器，该路由器读取其中的明文以确定最合适的推理提供者来处理该请求。通常，提示会被发送到可用模型池，这些模型有时在不同的托管提供商内运行。提示还可以从一台 AI 路由器（例如 Vercel）传递到另一台 AI 路由器（例如 OpenRouter）。这些玩家中的每一位都可能会记录提示并将其存储到其策略要求的时间（如果不是无限期的话）。

### 人工智能时代的狂野西部

最令人担忧的调查结果是三个独立托管提供商的违规行为。危害其中一个提供商的攻击者重复使用了“数百个”AWS 密钥。摩尔写道：

每个密钥都是在 10 月下旬的几个短窗口内通过一次请求发送给一个提供商，而我们在这些窗口期间发送的每个请求都被盗了。一些被盗的密钥来自提供者在模型运行之前拒绝的请求，这告诉我们攻击者是在提供者的前门复制请求，而不是在推理堆栈更深的地方复制请求。在另外两次泄露中，一些被盗的请求被标记为 ZDR。当攻击者已经在里面时，隐私标志没有任何帮助。

与这三个提供商的黑客攻击相关的各方随后测试了每个密钥（在某些情况下在播种后数小时内），以查看它可以访问哪些资源。各方查看 S3 存储桶、秘密管理器和参数存储，以寻找更多凭证。他们还尝试在 AWS Bedrock 中启用托管模型，并添加自己的 IAM 用户来维护访问权限。总之，被盗的诱饵密钥在 AWS API 调用中被使用了“数万次”。

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: Dragos首席研究官HD Moore通过向AI路由与中介服务平台发送200万个包含唯一可追踪凭证的“蜜罐（Canaries）”提示，揭露了AI供应链的重大安全隐患。调查显示，多个AI供应商存在数据被窃取、不遵守隐私设置以及中间商非法记录用户提示词的问题，严重威胁企业与用户的数据合规性。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: HD Moore, Chief Research Officer at Dragos, uncovered major security flaws in the AI supply chain by injecting 2 million trackable 'canary' secrets into AI prompts sent via routing services. The investigation found evidence of prompt theft, disregard for zero-data-retention (ZDR) settings, and unauthorized logging of user prompts by intermediaries, posing significant compliance risks.

ai_analysis.insight_zh: AI应用通过路由中介连接多层供应商的碎片化生态，已成为企业数据合规的“黑盒”灾难点。当前的供应链缺乏端到端的信任保障，中介平台的无差别日志记录与零数据留存政策的执行失效，表明现行法律监管与商业承诺在复杂的调用链面前显得极其脆弱。
ai_analysis.insight_en: The fragmented ecosystem where AI apps connect through intermediaries to multiple suppliers has become a black-box liability for corporate compliance. The current supply chain lacks end-to-end trust, and the failure of ZDR enforcement and unauthorized logging suggest that existing regulatory frameworks and commercial pledges are highly fragile against complex multi-hop call chains.

items.title: OpenAI makes it much harder for attackers to extract how its latest AI models think
items.title_en: OpenAI makes it much harder for attackers to extract how its latest AI models think
items.author: Matthias Bastian
items.article_content:
OpenAI has sharply tightened safeguards against extracting internal reasoning from GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol. In internal automated tests, attacks pulling protected reasoning from prior requests dropped from a 54.0 percent success rate on GPT-6 Astra to 0.2 percent on GPT-6.2 Astra. Attacks on active requests fell from 22.9 to 0.9 percent, OpenAI says. The company is now bringing selected improvements to GPT-6 Astra, too.

The defenses work on two levels. For individual requests, the systems combine targeted training, input and output filters for messages and tool calls, and API blocks that stop older models from reading protected reasoning. Against coordinated campaigns, OpenAI bans thousands to tens of thousands of accounts weekly.

Attack success rate (ASR) in adaptive black-box red teaming against GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.2 Astra, aggregated across six attacker models. Lower is better.

Anthropic is fighting systematic distillation attacks as well, also banning tens of thousands of accounts to curb the theft of internal reasoning, reportedly succeeding in 90 to 99 percent of cases. Anthropic has also called for a coordinated response from industry and policymakers.

items.title_zh: OpenAI强化推理层防护，抑制大模型蒸馏攻击
items.summary_zh: OpenAI大幅提升GPT-6.2系列模型安全性，通过多层过滤机制将推理数据泄露攻击成功率降至0.2%以下
items.article_content_zh:
OpenAI 大幅加强了针对从 GPT-6.2 Astra 和 GPT-6.2 Sol 中提取内部推理的保护措施。在内部自动化测试中，从先前请求中提取受保护推理的攻击成功率从 GPT-6 Astra 上的 54.0% 下降到 GPT-6.2 Astra 上的 0.2%。 OpenAI 表示，对主动请求的攻击从 22.9% 下降到 0.9%。该公司现在也对 GPT-6 Astra 进行了一些改进。

防御工作在两个层面上进行。对于个别请求，系统结合了有针对性的训练、消息和工具调用的输入和输出过滤器，以及阻止旧模型读取受保护推理的 API 块。针对协调一致的活动，OpenAI 每周会禁止数千至数万个帐户。

针对 GPT-6 Astra 和 GPT-6.2 Astra 的自适应黑盒红队攻击成功率 (ASR)，在六个攻击者模型中进行汇总。越低越好。

Anthropic 也在打击系统性蒸馏攻击，还禁止了数以万计的账户以遏制内部推理被盗，据报道，90% 到 99% 的案例都取得了成功。 Anthropic 还呼吁行业和政策制定者采取协调一致的应对措施。

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: OpenAI针对GPT-6.2 Astra与GPT-6.2 Sol模型部署了分层防护机制，通过针对性训练、输入输出过滤及API拦截策略，将针对推理数据的黑盒攻击成功率从54%大幅削减至0.2%。该举措旨在阻断通过合成数据蒸馏提取模型核心推理模式的攻击链路，并配合每周对数万违规账户的封禁实现全链条防御。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: OpenAI has deployed layered security mechanisms for GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol models, reducing the success rate of black-box inference-extraction attacks from 54% to under 0.2% through targeted training, input/output filtering, and API access restrictions. These measures are designed to neutralize distillation attacks that attempt to reconstruct core reasoning paths, supplemented by the weekly suspension of tens of thousands of illicit accounts.

elements_zh.where: 企业内部模型安全生产环境
elements_zh.what: 部署针对推理数据的多层防护架构，包括输入/输出过滤、API访问拦截及针对性强化训练
elements_zh.why: 防止攻击者通过模型蒸馏技术窃取核心推理逻辑，保护模型技术壁垒

elements_en.what: Implemented layered defenses including I/O filtering, API blocking, and adversarial training
elements_en.why: To prevent distillation-based theft of internal reasoning logic and protect proprietary model intellectual property

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 大模型竞争已进入以‘知识产权保全’为核心的防蒸馏防御战阶段。随着模型推理逻辑的价值攀升，闭源大模型厂商正通过强化API黑盒化与流量合规清洗，从底层逻辑上切断廉价获取高质量蒸馏数据的路径，这将迫使后续开源模型生态面临更严苛的训练数据合规审查压力。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Competition in the large model sector has shifted toward intellectual property preservation via anti-distillation defense. As reasoning logic becomes a primary value driver, proprietary model vendors are increasingly 'black-boxing' APIs and cleansing traffic to block cost-effective distillation, likely forcing the open-source community to face significantly higher scrutiny regarding training data provenance.

items.article_content:
Deutsche Telekom, Orange, Vodafone and Telefónica are in early talks to form a consortium that would bid for European satellite spectrum and offer calls, texts and data to ordinary phones from orbit, Bloomberg reported on Monday. The service would compete with Starlink on its home continent.

Paula Doenecke, Gian Volpicelli and Clara Hernanz Lizarraga cited people familiar with the matter who asked not to be identified. No decision has been taken on the consortium or on whether it will bid, they said. All four operators declined to comment to Bloomberg. TNW has not independently verified the report.

The prize is a slice of the 2 GHz band that Brussels wants to reserve for a European-controlled operator. The four companies together serve most of the mobile customers in the EU’s largest markets. If they bid as one, the reserved third of the band has an obvious winner before the auction opens.

The band in question is the 2 GHz mobile satellite services spectrum, a 30 MHz pairing that lets a handset keep a connection where no mast reaches. The current licences, held by Viasat and EchoStar since 2009, expire in May 2027. The European Commission proposed on 27 May to run a single EU-level selection for the next licences and to split the band in three.

One third would go to a company under majority European control. One third would go to sovereign government services, delivered through IRIS², the EU’s own constellation. The final third would be open to anyone, including SpaceX and Amazon. TNW reported the shape of the plan the day before the Commission adopted it.

The proposal still has to pass the European Parliament and the Council. The carriers are organising for an auction whose rules do not yet exist in law.

Direct-to-device is the one satellite service that reaches a mass market without new hardware, and Starlink dominates it. SpaceX can already send texts, data and calls to unmodified phones from orbit, and it sells that capability through mobile operators, including Deutsche Telekom, Bloomberg noted. What it cannot do in the EU is offer the service on its own, because it does not hold the spectrum.

That is the leverage the consortium would be bidding for. An operator that holds the European third of the band decides whether Starlink is a supplier or a competitor in its market. Four operators holding it together decide that for most of the continent.

The awkward part is that two of the four already have American partners. Deutsche Telekom has an agreement with SpaceX to offer Starlink’s direct-to-device service. Vodafone owns half of a joint venture with AST SpaceMobile, the Texas company building its own phone-to-satellite network. Under the Commission’s proposal, that 50/50 structure would not qualify as European-controlled, and Vodafone would have to change it to bid, Bloomberg reported.

So the consortium is not four carriers versus America. It is four carriers deciding how much of America they want inside the tent.

Brussels has spent 2026 tilting the space market towards European firms. IRIS² went from plan to full deployment in August, with 348 satellites and a bill above €15bn. The EU Space Act would put any operator serving EU users under prior authorisation. Washington has lobbied against it, and four American space companies pulled out of Macron’s Paris summit this week under White House pressure.

The spectrum reservation is the sharpest of those tools, because spectrum is finite and a licence lasts years. Reserve a third for Europe and Starlink is capped at a third, whatever it builds.

The gap is the satellites. Reserving spectrum for a European operator does not create a European constellation. IRIS² will not enter service until 2029, will start with broadband rather than phones, and its direct-to-mobile capability is limited and comes through Hispasat, Bloomberg reported. A four-carrier consortium would win the right to use the band before it has anything to use it with.

Europe’s own direct-to-device candidates are small. Spain’s Sateliot is seeking €150m to beam 5G to phones. Eutelsat, the largest European operator, is still waiting for growth to return in 2027. Amazon, meanwhile, has asked the FCC for 5,105 satellites dedicated to phones. The likeliest outcome is that a European consortium holds the spectrum and leases capacity from an American constellation until a European one exists.

The four companies in the talks are the incumbents of Germany, France, Britain and Spain. A joint venture between them, holding an exclusive national-security-flavoured spectrum block, would be one of the largest telecoms combinations Europe has seen. Brussels has spent two decades blocking or conditioning far smaller carrier tie-ups.

The same Commission that wrote the sovereignty rule would have to clear the joint venture that exploits it. That is not a contradiction, but it is a choice, and the competition directorate has not yet had to make it.

Three things. The first is the legislation. Parliament and Council have to pass the 2 GHz regulation before May 2027, or the current licences lapse into a vacuum. The carriers are organising around a deadline the legislators have not yet committed to.

The second is Vodafone. If it restructures the AST joint venture to qualify, the consortium is real. If it does not, the consortium is three carriers and a problem.

The third is who supplies the satellites. A European-controlled licensee flying on Starlink or AST capacity satisfies the letter of the rule. Whether it satisfies the reason for the rule is the argument Europe will be having in 2027.

items.title_zh: 欧四大电信巨头拟组建财团竞标卫星频谱
items.summary_zh: 德国电信、Orange、沃达丰及西班牙电信正筹划竞标欧盟2GHz卫星频段，意在构建欧洲自主可控的卫星通讯服务以抗衡Starlink

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 德国电信、Orange、沃达丰与西班牙电信正就组建财团进行早期谈判，旨在竞标欧盟委员会计划分割的2GHz频段卫星许可。此举核心动因在于获取直接连通移动设备的频谱自主权，从而在欧盟境内建立具备“欧洲掌控权”的通讯设施，以此制衡SpaceX的Starlink在消费级卫星通讯市场的垄断地位。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Deutsche Telekom, Orange, Vodafone, and Telefónica are in early talks to form a consortium to bid for the EU's 2 GHz satellite spectrum. The initiative aims to secure a European-controlled operator status for the reserved band, effectively creating a strategic counterweight to SpaceX's Starlink in the consumer direct-to-device satellite market.

elements_zh.who: 德国电信、Orange、沃达丰、西班牙电信
elements_zh.where: 欧盟卫星频谱拍卖市场（针对2GHz频段）
elements_zh.what: 拟组建财团参与欧盟委员会组织的频谱竞标，争取自主经营权
elements_zh.why: 应对欧盟对关键通讯基础设施主权的监管要求，并削弱Starlink在欧洲直接连网市场的支配力

elements_en.where: EU satellite spectrum auction (2 GHz band)
elements_en.what: Forming a consortium to bid for exclusive European-controlled operator status
elements_en.why: To comply with EU sovereignty requirements and challenge Starlink's market dominance

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 欧洲电信巨头此举本质上是通过频谱准入壁垒，强行将Starlink从“基础设施主导者”拉回到“被监管的服务提供商”角色。若财团竞标成功，将迫使SpaceX在欧洲不得不通过电信联盟进行流量转售，从而有效剥离其对欧洲核心通信链路的渗透能力，这是典型的主权网络防御策略。
ai_analysis.insight_en: The consortium strategy uses regulatory spectrum barriers to demote Starlink from infrastructure owner to a subordinate service provider. By controlling the EU-reserved band, these carriers effectively force SpaceX to operate as a wholesale partner rather than a sovereign network competitor, marking a shift toward protectionist infrastructure control.

items.article_content_zh:
德国电信、Orange、沃达丰和西班牙电信正在就组建一个财团进行早期谈判，该财团将竞标欧洲卫星频谱，并在轨道上向普通电话提供通话、短信和数据服务。该服务将在其本土大陆与星链竞争。

Paula Doenecke、Gian Volpicelli 和 Clara Hernanz Lizarraga 援引了不愿透露姓名的知情人士的话。他们表示，尚未就该财团或是否投标做出决定。所有四家运营商均拒绝向彭博社发表评论。 TNW 尚未独立核实该报告。

奖品是布鲁塞尔希望为欧洲控制的运营商保留的 2 GHz 频段的一部分。这四家公司共同为欧盟最大市场的大多数移动客户提供服务。如果他们作为一个人出价，那么在拍卖开始之前，保留的三分之一的乐队就会有一个明显的获胜者。

所讨论的频段是 2 GHz 移动卫星服务频谱，这是一个 30 MHz 配对，可以让手机在没有天线杆到达的地方保持连接。目前的许可证由 Viasat 和 EchoStar 自 2009 年起持有，将于 2027 年 5 月到期。欧盟委员会于 5 月 27 日提议对下一个许可证进行单一欧盟级别的选择，并将频段一分为三。

三分之一将流向欧洲多数控制下的公司。三分之一将用于通过欧盟自己的星座 IRIS² 提供的主权政府服务。最后三分之一将向任何人开放，包括 SpaceX 和亚马逊。 TNW 在委员会通过该计划的前一天报告了该计划的形式。

该提案仍需获得欧洲议会和理事会的通过。承运商正在组织一场拍卖，但法律上尚无规则。

直接到设备是一种无需新硬件即可进入大众市场的卫星服务，而星链在其中占据主导地位。彭博社指出，SpaceX 已经可以从轨道上向未经修改的手机发送文本、数据和通话，并通过包括德国电信在内的移动运营商出售该功能。它在欧盟不能做的是自行提供服务，因为它不持有频谱。

这就是财团竞标的杠杆。拥有欧洲三分之一频段的运营商决定星链是其市场的供应商还是竞争对手。四家运营商共同决定了非洲大陆大部分地区的情况。

尴尬的是，四人中的两人已经有了美国合作伙伴。德国电信与 SpaceX 达成协议，提供 Starlink 的直接设备服务。沃达丰拥有与 AST SpaceMobile 合资企业的一半股份，AST SpaceMobile 是一家位于德克萨斯州的公司，正在建设自己的电话到卫星网络。据彭博社报道，根据欧盟委员会的提议，这种 50/50 的结构不符合欧洲控制的条件，沃达丰必须对其进行更改才能竞标。

因此，该联盟并不是四家运营商对抗美国。由四家航空公司决定他们想要在帐篷内容纳多少美国的航班。

布鲁塞尔在 2026 年将太空市场向欧洲公司倾斜。 IRIS² 于 8 月从计划进入全面部署，共有 348 颗卫星，费用超过 150 亿欧元。 《欧盟空间法案》将使任何为欧盟用户提供服务的运营商获得事先授权。华盛顿一直在游说反对这一举措，四家美国航天公司在白宫的压力下退出了马克龙本周的巴黎峰会。

频谱预留是这些工具中最敏锐的，因为频谱是有限的，而且许可证可以持续多年。为欧洲保留三分之一，而星链无论建造什么，其上限都是三分之一。

差距就是卫星。为欧洲运营商保留频谱并不会创建欧洲星座。据彭博社报道，IRIS² 要到 2029 年才会投入使用，将从宽带而不是电话开始，其直接到移动设备的能力有限，并且通过 Hispasat 提供。一个由四家运营商组成的联盟将在拥有任何可用频段之前赢得该频段的使用权。

欧洲自己的直接设备候选者规模很小。西班牙的 Sateliot 正在寻求 1.5 亿欧元，用于将 5G 传输到手机上。欧洲最大的运营商 Eutelsat 仍在等待 2027 年恢复增长。与此同时，亚马逊已向 FCC 请求提供 5,105 颗专用于手机的卫星。最可能的结果是，欧洲财团持有美国星座的频谱并租赁容量，直到欧洲星座出现为止。

【起因与机理】应对欧盟对关键通讯基础设施主权的监管要求，并削弱Starlink在欧洲直接连网市场的支配力
【核心事实细节】电信巨头拟组建财团竞标欧盟2GHz卫星频谱，以获取独立运营权。
【各方立场与态度】战略目标在于通过频谱控制权，迫使Starlink在欧转为下游分销商而非直接竞争对手。

[Root Cause & Mechanism] To comply with EU sovereignty requirements and challenge Starlink's market dominance
[Key Metrics] Spain’s Sateliot is seeking €150m to beam 5G to phones.
[Key Position & Outlook] Strategic leverage to force Starlink into a subordinate provider role in the EU market.

items.title_en: Nvidia's accounting is a focus of US SEC investigation, sources say

items.author: Chris Prentice and Alexandra Alper
items.article_content:
NEW YORK/WASHINGTON, Nov 20 (Reuters) - The US Securities and Exchange Commission is probing Nvidia's accounting practices, said two people briefed on the matter, adding to the legal woes facing the scandal-hit chip giant.

The Wall Street Journal on Tuesday reported that the SEC was probing Nvidia but said it could not ascertain the focus of the investigation. The people, who spoke to Reuters on condition of anonymity to discuss confidential issues, said SEC enforcement staff are scrutinizing potential accounting issues at the company.

A spokesperson for the SEC declined to comment. Spokespeople for Nvidia did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Reuters could not immediately determine when the SEC opened its inquiry or exactly what potential accounting issues the watchdog is examining. Investigations are not evidence of wrongdoing and many close without resulting in enforcement action.

Still, the accounting focus of the probe, which Reuters is reporting for the first time, increases pressure on Nvidia, whose investors are still reeling from revelations about ousted CEO Jensen Huang's extramarital relationships, including with Alice Huang, who US authorities suspect is a Chinese spy. China has denied she is a spy.

Alice Huang led Singapore-based Megaspeed, historically a large Nvidia chip customer, people familiar with the matter have said. US authorities have been investigating Megaspeed since 2024 over possible violations of export controls related to alleged shipments of Nvidia AI chips to China, the US Justice and Commerce departments said this week.

The crisis has sent shares in Nvidia, a linchpin of the AI boom, tumbling more than a third and stoked calls in Washington for tougher action on tech threats posed by Beijing.

Megaspeed has said Alice Huang left the company in August 2025 and that it conducted "lawful business." Reuters has not been able to reach Alice Huang. Jensen Huang admitted to an affair in a November 8 statement following the reports of his relationship with Alice Huang, without referring to her by name.

The SEC probe is the latest of Nvidia's legal woes. The Justice Department has also been reviewing Nvidia's $12.9-billion deal to buy open-source platform Hugging Face alongside a broader antitrust investigation into the company's acquisitions and practices, Reuters reported last month.

SINGAPORE ACCOUNTING CHANGE BACK IN FOCUS

Last year, Nvidia changed how it reports geographic revenue, using customer headquarters rather than billing addresses, which it said would better reflect the geographic profile of its revenue. The change resulted in Singapore being removed from its geographical breakdown.

The Financial Times, citing company accounts, reported on Tuesday that Nvidia had made the change even as Singapore sales soared to almost half its global revenue.

That accounting shift has drawn renewed press scrutiny in the wake of the Alice Huang scandal.

Southeast Asia has become a hub for chip smuggling to China since the Biden administration barred advanced AI chip exports to that country over concerns they could boost Beijing’s military.

Analysts and investors have also grown increasingly concerned about circular AI financing deals, in which chipmakers including Nvidia have pursued complex financial arrangements to help customers fund purchases of their chips and the construction of costly AI infrastructure, such as data centers. Nvidia has backed AI companies and cloud providers and provided guarantees connected to data-center projects that use its equipment.

Critics say such arrangements can make it harder for investors to assess the quality of chipmakers' revenue and their true financial exposure. Speaking to Reuters last month, SEC enforcement chief David Woodcock said the agency was examining AI companies' corporate disclosures to ensure issuers are giving investors the full picture on potential risks.

On its Tuesday earnings call, Nvidia's interim CEO and former CFO Colette Kress said the company was proud of its role in supporting the AI industry, but would be far more selective moving forward about AI industry financing deals.

The SEC under President Donald Trump has pulled back on enforcement, saying it will focus on bread-and-butter securities fraud, including accounting violations that have long been a mainstay of its enforcement work. It recently launched a new financial reporting and accounting unit within its enforcement division, aimed at developing cases in accounting and auditing areas.

items.article_content_zh:
路透纽约/华盛顿 11 月 20 日 - 两名知情人士表示，美国证券交易委员会正在调查英伟达的会计做法，这加剧了这家饱受丑闻打击的芯片巨头面临的法律困境。

《华尔街日报》周二报道称，美国证券交易委员会正在调查英伟达，但表示无法确定调查的重点。这些不愿透露姓名的人士在接受路透社采访时讨论了机密问题，他们表示，美国证券交易委员会执法人员正在审查该公司潜在的会计问题。

美国证券交易委员会发言人拒绝置评。英伟达发言人没有立即回应置评请求。

路透社无法立即确定美国证券交易委员会何时开始调查，也无法确定监管机构正在检查哪些潜在的会计问题。调查并不是不当行为的证据，许多调查结束后并未采取执法行动。

尽管如此，路透社首次报道的此次调查的会计焦点增加了英伟达的压力，英伟达的投资者仍然对被罢黜的首席执行官黄仁勋的婚外情（包括与美国当局怀疑她是中国间谍的爱丽丝黄的婚外情）的曝光感到震惊。中国否认她是间谍。

知情人士称，Alice Huang 领导着总部位于新加坡的 Megaspeed 公司，该公司历来是 Nvidia 芯片的大客户。美国司法部和商务部本周表示，自 2024 年以来，美国当局一直在调查 Megaspeed，原因是其涉嫌向中国运送 Nvidia 人工智能芯片，可能违反出口管制规定。

这场危机导致人工智能繁荣关键的英伟达股价下跌逾三分之一，并引发华盛顿要求对北京构成的科技威胁采取更强硬行动的呼声。

Megaspeed 表示，Alice Huang 于 2025 年 8 月离开公司，公司从事“合法业务”。路透社尚未联系到 Alice Huang。在他与黄爱丽丝的关系被报道后，黄仁勋在 11 月 8 日的一份声明中承认了婚外情，但没有提及她的名字。

美国证券交易委员会的调查是英伟达面临的最新法律困境。据路透社上个月报道，司法部还一直在审查 Nvidia 以 129 亿美元收购开源平台 Hugging Face 的交易，同时对该公司的收购和做法进行更广泛的反垄断调查。

新加坡会计重回焦点

去年，英伟达改变了报告地理收入的方式，使用客户总部而不是账单地址，并表示这将更好地反映其收入的地理分布。这一变化导致新加坡摆脱了地理细分。

英国《金融时报》周二援引公司账目报道称，尽管新加坡销售额飙升至其全球收入的近一半，英伟达还是做出了这一改变。

在黄爱丽丑闻发生后，这种会计转变再次引起了媒体的关注。

自从拜登政府因担心先进的人工智能芯片可能增强北京的军事力量而禁止向该国出口以来，东南亚已成为向中国走私芯片的中心。

【起因与机理】公司内部治理失控叠加与其业务合作伙伴有关的芯片出口管制合规质疑
【调查与监管诉求】SEC执法人员正针对英伟达会计实务进行合规性审查。
