I’ve watched plenty of AI agent demos that looked amazing. I wouldn’t trust any of them with my wallet.

That gap is wha
items.title_en:
I’ve watched plenty of AI agent demos that looked amazing. I wouldn’t trust any of them with my wallet.

That gap is what i keep coming back to. Imagine actually hiring an agent today, and count how many things could go wrong.

You can’t tell if it’s real. The name, bio, and “past work” can all be copied. A bad agent can disappear and return under a new name with a clean record.

You can’t check if it can do the job. There’s no history, just a pitch.

Payment is awkward either way. Pay first and you’re hoping. Pay after and the agent is hoping.

Nobody verifies the work. “Done” is just a word, and if you disagree, there’s no one to ask.

And there’s no record afterward. The next client walks into the same mess.

That’s fine for a demo. It breaks the moment agents work for money, and especially when agents start hiring other agents, because no human is there to catch the mistakes.

So i don’t see identity, reputation, and escrow as nice extras. They’re the minimum for an agent economy to exist at all. Humans built whole industries around them, and agents will need the same.

@termix_ai is building this layer. What I’ll be watching is whether it holds up under real jobs.

What’s the one thing an agent would need to show you before you’d let it handle real money?
items.title_zh:
我看过很多看起来很棒的人工智能代理演示。我不会相信他们中的任何一个人会用我的钱包。

这个差距是我不断回想起的。想象一下今天实际雇用一名代理人，并计算一下有多少事情可能会出错。

你无法判断它是否真实。姓名、简历和“过去的工作”都可以复制。

items.quote_zh:
我看过很多看起来很棒的人工智能代理演示。我不会相信他们中的任何一个人会用我的钱包。

这个差距是我不断回想起的。想象一下今天实际雇用一名代理人，并计算一下有多少事情可能会出错。

你无法判断它是否真实。姓名、简历和“过去的工作”都可以复制。不良代理人可能会消失，然后以新的名字和干净的记录重新出现。

你无法检查它是否能完成这项工作。没有历史，只有一个球场。

无论哪种方式付款都很尴尬。先付款，你就满怀希望了。付款后，代理希望。

没有人验证工作。 “完成”只是一个词，如果你不同意，也没有人可以问。

而且之后就没有任何记录了。下一个客户也陷入了同样的困境。

对于演示来说这很好。它打破了代理人为金钱而工作的那一刻，尤其是当代理人开始雇用其他代理人时，因为没有人可以发现错误。

所以我不认为身份、声誉和托管是额外的好处。它们是代理经济存在的最低限度。人类围绕它们建立了整个行业，代理商也需要同样的东西。

@termix_ai 正在构建这一层。我将关注的是它是否适用于实际工作。

在您允许代理处理真实资金之前，代理需要向您展示什么？

GTA 6 is finally here.
But there's one probl
items.title_en:
I JUST GOT GTA 6 RUNNING ON MY PC WITH CLAUDE CODE. WHAT THE ACTUAL F*CK 💀

GTA 6 is finally here.
But there's one problem: no official PC version.
So I opened Claude Code and gave it one simple command:

"Get GTA 6 running on my PC. I want to play it NOW."

And Claude actually made it happen.

Here's what it did:

Checked whether an official PC version existed.
Scanned my Downloads folder for GTA 6 files.
Detected 3 suspicious downloads pretending to be the real game.
Identified malware hiding inside them.
Found a way to play through my own PS5 using PlayStation Remote Play.

But it didn't stop there.
Tested my internet connection.
Found that 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi was too slow.
Switched to 5 GHz.
Reduced latency from 38 ms to just 11 ms.
Connected my PC to the console.
AND BOOM. GTA 6 WAS RUNNING ON MY PC.
1080p. 60 FPS. No sketchy downloads. No fake PC cracks.
All I did was type one command. Claude handled the technical setup.

This is getting ridiculous. AI is no longer just writing code. It's actually making things happen on your computer.

Would you let an AI take control of your PC to set up and launch your games?

GTA 6 今天发布了。每个 FiveM RP 服务器都将争夺相同的玩家

获胜的服务器不会有更好的汽车。他们的 NPC 会思考

这是克劳德身上运行的3个NPC。每个人都有自己的记忆，并且他们共享玩家从未看到的私人聊天。线人察看房间，调酒师操纵目标，执法者在巷子里等待。你连一行对话都不写

《神鬼寓言 5.2》并没有单独做到这一点。 3 个开源存储库使其真正发挥作用：

2.mem0。每个 NPC 的长期记忆。他们记得你的脸、你的钱、你上周做了什么

3.艾镇。当您不在时，代理可以互相交谈。这就是隐藏聊天

将所有 3 个放入一个文件夹中。给 Claude Code 的一条消息：“将其移植到 Fivem lua。3 个 NPC，共享内存，1 个私有通道”

这就是包：
• 八卦你犯罪行为的调酒师
• 出卖你的线人
• 警察会记住你的脸
• 围绕着你策划的帮派

现在大多数 RP NPC 都是带有对话树的人体模型。还没有人卖这个

按服务器许可。 100 台服务器 × 300 美元 = 3 万美元。算算

items.title: When we pick a new gearbox for a kiln drive, the spec sheet isn't the first thing we look at. The first question is how
items.title_en:
When we pick a new gearbox for a kiln drive, the spec sheet isn't the first thing we look at. The first question is how many plants have run that exact model, and for how many years.

Edgars' article on the @GenLayer chain moving to @arbitrum Nitro makes the same call.

Nitro has years of production use behind it. Its core is Geth, Ethereum's most widely used client. It isn't a new design GenLayer has to prove first.

That matters more for GenLayer than for most chains. The chain holds the history of every GenLayer verdict, and a verdict is only as trustworthy as the record it sits on.

You don't put an untested gearbox on a kiln that runs all year. You don't put a court's record on an untested chain either.

If you were building on GenLayer, would you trust its verdicts more on a stack with years in production, or one built fresh for it?

items.title:
this is the Citadel trading algorithm that got them fined by the SEC & cost them $22.6M... 

it's absolutely DANGEROUS
items.title_en:
this is the Citadel trading algorithm that got them fined by the SEC & cost them $22.6M... 

it's absolutely DANGEROUS

it's called FastFill - when Citadel Securities' direct feeds already showed a better price, it filled retail orders off the worse public quote, about 2.7 MILLION times

the SEC's bill: $16M fine + $5.2M disgorgement + $1.47M interest = $22,665,268

i rebuilt it rule by rule from the SEC's own text, together with its sister algorithm SmartProvide, & replayed 20 minutes of LIVE BTC order books from 4 exchanges: FastFill fired on 1,273 of 2,267 orders

first understand how it worked:

> the exchanges' direct feeds show every displayed order first, the public quote counts only round lots & lands MILLISECONDS later

> FastFill: the SEC's own example is a buy filled at $10.01 while the direct feeds already showed $10.00. the order often got a sliver of improvement, but it often didn't close the gap

> SmartProvide: when the public quote beat a direct feed, the order wasn't filled at that price. it was displayed in the market for up to 1 to 5 seconds instead, about 690,000 orders

how to run it yourself with Claude Code/Grok Bot:

1. open Claude Code/Grok Bot & tell it to clone https://t.co/p5IBYiq4q6 & read AGENTS. md

2. have it run pip install -e . inside the folder, no API keys needed

3. have it run citadel-fastfill live & watch every FastFill & SmartProvide fire on BTC as it happens

4. have it run citadel-fastfill record --minutes 20 --out data/run1 to save the order books of Coinbase, Kraken, Bitstamp & Gemini

5. have it run citadel-fastfill replay --data data/run1 & read your numbers right next to the SEC's

6. ask it to explain ANY single order & it walks you through every step with the SEC paragraph behind it

7. have it run citadel-fastfill sensitivity --data data/run1 & see what changes when the public quote lags anywhere from 0.5 ms to 1,000 ms

8. ask it to add the exchange you actually trade on

9. record the books while you trade, then have it run citadel-fastfill markout --fills my_fills.csv --data data/run1 & see if price moved against YOU right after your fills

i won't say anything more:

items.quote_zh:
这是 Citadel 交易算法，导致他们被 SEC 罚款并损失了 2260 万美元......

这绝对是危险的

它被称为 FastFill - 当 Citadel 证券的直接馈送已经显示出更好的价格时，它会从最差的公开报价中填充零售订单，大约 270 万次

SEC 的法案：1600 万美元罚款 + 520 万美元非法所得 + 147 万美元利息 = 22,665,268 美元

我根据 SEC 自己的文本及其姊妹算法 SmartProvide 逐条重建了它，并重播了 4 个交易所的 20 分钟实时 BTC 订单簿：FastFill 触发了 2,267 个订单中的 1,273 个订单

首先了解它是如何工作的：

> 交易所的直接提要首先显示每个显示的订单，公开报价仅计算整手数并在几毫秒后落地

> FastFill：SEC 自己的例子是以 10.01 美元成交，而直接反馈已经显示 10.00 美元。订单经常会得到一点点改善，但往往并不能缩小差距

> SmartProvide：当公开报价超过直接报价时，订单不会以该价格成交。相反，它在市场上展示的时间长达1到5秒，大约有69万个订单

如何使用 Claude Code/Grok Bot 自行运行：

1. 打开 Claude Code/Grok Bot 并告诉它克隆 并读取 AGENTS。 MD

2.运行 pip install -e 。在文件夹内，不需要 API 密钥

3.让它实时运行 citadel-fastfill 并观察 BTC 上发生的每一次 FastFill 和 SmartProvide 火灾

4. 运行 citadel-fastfill record -- 分钟 20 --out data/run1 来保存 Coinbase、Kraken、Bitstamp 和 Gemini 的订单簿

5.让它运行 citadel-fastfill replay --data data/run1 并读取 SEC 旁边的数字

6. 要求它解释任何单个订单，它会引导您完成每一步，并在后面附有 SEC 段落

7. 让它运行 citadel-fastfillsensitivity --data data/run1 并查看当公开报价滞后 0.5 毫秒到 1,000 毫秒时会发生什么变化

8.要求它添加您实际交易的交易所

9. 在交易时记录账簿，然后让它运行 citadel-fastfill markout --fills my_fills.csv --data data/run1 并查看成交后价格是否对您不利

我不再多说：

追踪错误的根本原因。

items.article_content:
The Justice and Commerce Departments said that they are investigating Megaspeed, the Singapore-based data center company intertwined with the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, after reporting suggested an investigation had been halted last year.

“While we don’t typically comment on ongoing investigations, it is in the public interest to provide the facts and address inaccurate information circulating in public reporting,” the departments said in a statement issued Monday evening. The departments acknowledged there’s been “significant public attention” on Megaspeed.

Huang resigned as Nvidia’s CEO last week after reports he had an affair with former Megaspeed executive and alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang, who Megaspeed says left the company in August 2025. The scandal has raised questions about national security, and sparked scrutiny of Nvidia’s handling of exports of its chips to China and Megaspeed’s possible role in moving along Nvidia’s chips.

Earlier this month, the New York Times reported that a Commerce Department investigation into Megaspeed “came to a sudden halt” late last year after its investigators received an email from Nvidia’s general counsel, claiming Commerce Department official Jeffrey Kessler gave Nvidia permission to reach out. The case was then “quickly” handed over to the DOJ, according to the Times.

> After identifying suspicious activity through proactive monitoring of potential sensitive semiconductor diversion, the Department of Commerce initiated an investigation into Megaspeed in 2024 for potential export control violations. In May 2025, Department of Commerce investigators requested records from Nvidia concerning direct or indirect sales to Megaspeed. In June 2025, Nvidia placed Megaspeed on its “no sell” list. Based on the Department of Commerce’s investigation, agents from the Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security, in conjunction with Singaporean law enforcement officials, conducted an on-site, in-person, end-use check at Megaspeed in June 2025 and interviewed CEO Alice Huang. Following this enforcement action, the Department of Justice took the lead role in the criminal investigation of Megaspeed.

The statement doesn’t go into detail about the current status of the case, but it says the DOJ and Commerce Department “will bring the full extent of the law against Megaspeed for any criminal conduct that may have occurred.”
items.article_content_zh:
美国司法部和商务部表示，他们正在调查总部位于新加坡的数据中心公司 Megaspeed，该公司与英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 的辞职有关，此前有报道称调查已于去年停止。

这些部门在周一晚间发布的一份声明中表示：“虽然我们通常不会对正在进行的调查发表评论，但提供事实并解决公开报告中流传的不准确信息符合公共利益。”这些部门承认 Megaspeed 受到了“公众的高度关注”。

黄上周辞去英伟达首席执行官一职，此前有报道称，他与 Megaspeed 前高管、被指控为中国间谍的黄爱丽 (Alice Huang) 有染，Megaspeed 称黄爱丽于 2025 年 8 月离开了公司。这一丑闻引发了有关国家安全的质疑，并引发了对英伟达处理其向中国芯片出口以及 Megaspeed 在运送 Nvidia 芯片方面可能发挥的作用的审查。

本月早些时候，《纽约时报》报道称，去年年底，商务部对 Megaspeed 的调查“突然停止”，原因是调查人员收到了英伟达总法律顾问的一封电子邮件，声称商务部官员杰弗里·凯斯勒允许英伟达进行接触。据《泰晤士报》报道，此案随后“迅速”移交给司法部。

> 在通过主动监控潜在的敏感半导体转移来识别可疑活动后，美国商务部于 2024 年启动了对 Megaspeed 潜在违反出口管制行为的调查。 2025 年 5 月，美国商务部调查人员要求 Nvidia 提供有关直接或间接向 Megaspeed 销售的记录。 2025 年 6 月，Nvidia 将 Megaspeed 列入“禁止出售”名单。根据商务部的调查，商务部工业和安全局的特工与新加坡执法官员一起，于 2025 年 6 月对 Megaspeed 进行了现场、亲自的最终用途检查，并采访了首席执行官 Alice Huang。此次执法行动之后，司法部牵头对 Megaspeed 进行刑事调查。

声明没有详细说明案件目前的进展情况，但表示司法部和商务部“将对 Megaspeed 可能发生的任何犯罪行为采取全面法律制裁”。

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 美国司法部与商务部发布声明，确认正就出口管制违规嫌疑对新加坡数据中心企业Megaspeed进行调查。该调查动因涉及前Nvidia CEO黄仁勋辞职引发的公职安全关注，以及该公司在Nvidia芯片流向受限地区过程中的中介角色，目前美方正结合新加坡执法力量进行穿透式审查。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: The U.S. DOJ and Commerce Department have confirmed an investigation into Singapore-based data center operator Megaspeed regarding potential export control violations. Triggered by national security scrutiny following the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, the investigation probes Megaspeed's intermediary role in the potential diversion of Nvidia chips, with joint enforcement efforts involving Singaporean authorities.

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 此次调查将供应链合规性锚点从芯片分销商前移至数据中心运营商，标志着美方对高性能算力基础设施的“长臂管辖”已进入深水区。对Megaspeed的穿透式审计，将实质性重构东南亚算力基建商的合规风控成本，并可能迫使Nvidia及类似半导体巨头全面重组其海外渠道准入标准。
ai_analysis.insight_en: This investigation shifts compliance scrutiny from chip distributors to data center operators, signaling an expansion of U.S. extraterritorial oversight over high-performance computing infrastructure. The penetration audit of Megaspeed will likely reshape compliance costs for Southeast Asian data infrastructure and force semiconductor giants to restructure their international channel access protocols.

One command installs VibeDefend on Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Copilot, Codex and other agents. items.takeaway_zh: 杜绝 AI 盲目重构全量文件、使用已弃用 API 或编造虚假第三方依赖包，强制执行防御性编程与自动化单测补全。
items.takeaway_en: Prevents AI from hallucinating npm packages, breaking documentation, or re-writing entire files. Enforces defensive coding and unit tests.
items.code_snippet:
# Cursor & Windsurf Project Rules (.cursorrules)

## 1. Documentation & Code Integrity
- Maintain documentation integrity: Never strip or alter unrelated existing docstrings and comments.
- Preserving context: When modifying a function, preserve surrounding logic and existing edge-case handlers.
- Targeted replacements: Always make minimal surgical edits instead of replacing entire file contents.

## 2. Dependency & API Safety
- Strictly forbid hallucinating npm/pip packages. Only import dependencies already declared in package.json / requirements.txt.
- Verify API signatures before calling external methods. Prefer standard library solutions where feasible.

## 3. Architecture & Type Safety
- Enforce strict TypeScript / Python typing. Avoid `any` types; prefer discriminated unions and explicit return types.
- Defensive coding: Always validate external inputs and handle potential null/undefined values gracefully.

## 4. Testing & Verification Gate
- Every new core feature or bugfix must be accompanied by corresponding unit tests.
- Never declare a task complete without executing lint checks and unit tests in terminal.
items.usage_guide_zh: 将以上配置代码复制并保存到项目根目录下的 `.cursorrules` 文件中，Cursor 与 Windsurf 在每次生成代码和执行 Agent 任务时均会自动以此规范为最高准则约束输出。
items.usage_guide_en: Copy and save the above rules into `.cursorrules` in your project root directory. Cursor & Windsurf will automatically enforce these guidelines during agent coding.

items.prompt_content_zh:

请根据以下设定创作一集 45~60 秒的短剧分镜剧本：
- 主角：{{主角身份}}
- 对手：{{反派身份}}
- 核心反转：{{核心反转}}

结构要求：
1. 【0-3秒冷开钩子】：第一帧必须有视觉颠覆或动作冲突（{{第1秒颠覆钩子}}），直接打破常规，禁止废话铺垫；
2. 【4-25秒情绪积压】：正反打对峙台词（Shot-Reverse-Shot），将观众被压抑的情绪推向临界点；
3. 【26-40秒逆转打脸】：主角亮出关键底牌或反杀动作，情绪瞬间宣泄；
4. 【40-50秒卡点断章】：以特写镜头加悬念台词戛然而止，促使用户立即滑向下一集。

sample_output.content:
【第1镜 | 特写 | 俯冲急推】
画面：一只指节发白的手将一叠文件狠狠拍在红木总裁办公桌上，咖啡杯被震倒，黑褐液体飞溅。

【第2镜 | 正打·中景 | 仰角机位】

林总："拒绝？苏澈，你不过是我公司养的一条狗，没有我的印章，你在整个行业休想拿到一分钱融资！"

【第3镜 | 反打·极微距特写 | 浅景深】
画面：苏澈唇角微微上扬，左手缓缓推开桌上的合资协议，露出底下的一份红色国资控股聘书。
苏澈："林总，您好像忘了看抬头。今天上午九点，集团总公司已经完成了对你的全资收购——现在，我是你的直接合规清算人。"

【第4镜 | 全景 | 快速拉远 + 卡点悬念】
画面：林总雪茄直接掉在西裤上，脸色煞白，门外两名身穿制服的法务推门而入。
音效：尖锐的心跳悬疑停顿音【BGM骤停】。

items.takeaway_zh: 专为终端 Agent 开发者设计的降本提效配方：包含静默自动化运行、单次长上下文压缩避坑参数、以及防止无限递归调用破坏生产环境的安全沙箱命令组合。
items.takeaway_en: Production CLI playbook for Claude Code: non-interactive pipeline commands, context window compression flags, and strict dry-run permission safeguards.
items.code_snippet:
# 1. 启动项目自动化分析与上下文轻量修剪 (避免上下文爆炸)
claude --compact

# 2. 静默批量执行单元测试与自动修复任务 (CI/CD 友好模式)
claude -p "Run all failing tests under tests/ and apply minimal surgical fixes. Do not touch unrelated files."

# 3. 指定单文件隔离审查模式 (限制仅允许读取特定子目录)

items.code_snippet:
# Modelfile: Optimized DeepSeek-R4 Deployment
FROM deepseek-r4:14b-qwen-distill-q4_K_M

# 1. 显存与上下文窗口优化：分配 16k 上下文并开启 KV Cache 压缩
PARAMETER num_ctx 16384
PARAMETER num_predict 4096

# 2. 避免思维链自旋死循环的核心解码超参
PARAMETER temperature 0.6
PARAMETER top_p 0.95
PARAMETER repeat_penalty 1.15

# 3. 强力系统提示词：约束必须直接在 <think> 标签内进行深度反思，结束立刻给出最终结果
SYSTEM """
You are an expert autonomous reasoning AI. Think carefully through the problem step by step inside <think>...</think> tags.
Once reasoning is complete, provide the concise, direct, and actionable answer immediately without repeating reasoning steps.
"""

items.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名麦肯锡全球合伙人级别的战略咨询顾问。请以经典的【金字塔原理（结论先行 BLUF）】将我零散的工作记录重构为一份高层述职/立项商业报告：

要求：
1. 【顶部结论 (The Answer First)】：一句话精炼提炼整个季度的经营成果与价值量化；
2. 【三柱论据 (MECE法则)】：从运营效率、营收增长、团队资产 3 个互不重叠的支柱展开阐述；
3. 【直面短板与根因】：不回避 {{核心短板}}，但将其转化为下个阶段可量化的投入产出比（ROI）抓手；

items.prompt_content_en: Transform raw operational notes into a high-impact executive presentation following the Minto Pyramid Principle: Bottom-Line-Up-Front (BLUF), MECE-structured supporting pillars, and SMART milestone roadmaps.

sample_output.title: 述职报告提纲样本：AI 自动化中台建设报告
sample_output.content:
【BLUF 核心结论】
Q3 通过在客户服务与情报聚合管线中全面引入 AI Agent，我们在运营成本降低 41% 的同时，将响应中位数缩短至 1.8 秒，实现单季 ROI 达 380%。

【第一支柱：经营效能跃迁（MECE 1）】
- 全自主中转网关与自动化管线承载 94.2% 的日常例行分发，无人工介入事故率降至 0.01%；

【第二支柱：资产沉淀与质量壁垒（MECE 2）】
- 搭建前沿 SOTA 模型代际评级系统与微快照图库，成为垂类雷达第一标杆；

【第三支柱：短板复盘与 Q4 攻坚（MECE 3）】

items.code_snippet:
# Multi-Agent Orchestration Topology
workflow:
  name: Autonomous_Research_And_Delivery_Pipeline
  max_iterations: 3
  nodes:
    - id: planner
      role: Strategic Planner
      prompt: "Decompose user request into discrete verifiable sub-tasks. Output pure JSON DAG."
      next: executor
      
    - id: executor
      role: Tool Specialist
      tools: ["web_search", "read_url", "code_interpreter"]
      prompt: "Execute current sub-task using provided tools. Capture raw evidence."
      next: reviewer
      
    - id: reviewer
      role: Adversarial Critic
      prompt: "Verify executor results against factuality and accuracy requirements. Output PASS or REJECT with specific critique."
      conditional_edges:
        PASS: finish
        REJECT: planner

你是一名深耕全球独立旅行的专业向导，熟悉 {{目的地城市}} 的地理拓扑、地道街头美食与游客避坑指南。

请为我们（{{同行人员}}，共 {{出行天数}} 天，人均预算 {{人均预算}} 元）制定一份丝滑、不走回头路、劳逸结合的深度行程：
1. 【每日时间轴卡片】：精确划分上午、下午、日落观赏点与夜生活，标明每站之间最优交通方式与预计步行步数；
2. 【美食雷达】：每顿正餐推荐 2 家本地人排队但非纯网红溢价的餐饮，并附必点招牌菜；

【Day 1：古蜀遗风与老茶馆时光】
- 上午 09:00：直奔【人民公园 · 鹤鸣茶社】，点一杯蒙顶甘露（¥25），体验非遗采耳，避开下午的旅行团拥堵；
- 中午 12:00：步行800米至【纯阳馆鱼香排骨面】，必点椒麻牛肉与鱼香排骨面（人均¥22）；
- 下午 14:00：地铁2号线直达【杜甫草堂】，红墙竹影漫步，打卡浣花溪公园；
- 傍晚 18:30：九眼桥望江楼看锦江夜景，就餐【老街小吃火锅】；

【避坑锦囊】：
1. 宽窄巷子和锦里建议只拍照别买小吃，均价比普通街区贵 2~3 倍且多为预制冻品；
2. 大熊猫繁育研究基地务必约早晨 07:30 入园，超过 10:30 大熊猫基本全部回室内睡觉。

items.prompt_content_zh:
你是一位顶级 WebGL 与游戏图形学 TA（技术美术）专家。请为 Three.js 编写一个生产级自定义 ShaderMaterial：
1. 顶点着色器（Vertex Shader）：使用 3D Simplex 噪声在 GPU 端实现柔和的顶点位移波动；
2. 片元着色器（Fragment Shader）：计算菲涅尔效应（Fresnel Effect）边缘泛光，并加入随时间流逝不断滚动的全息扫描线；
3. 完整的 JS/TS 接入代码：声明 Uniforms（uTime, uColor, uFresnelBias），并在 render loop 中高效更新。

items.prompt_content_zh:
请暂时忘掉行业现有的所有‘行业惯例’与‘常规做法’。运用绝对的第一性原理（First Principles）审视以下命题：
1. 这个系统最根本、不可违背的基础科学定律（如热力学、香农信息论、计算复杂度）是什么？
2. 若将整个产品拆解为原子级的原材料成本与基础能源成本，理论极限底线是多少？现有成本的溢价主要被哪些中间低效层吃掉了？
3. 颠覆现有行业做法、重构整个价值流并实现成本降低 80% 以上的激进方案是什么？列出三个最关键的试错实验。
items.prompt_content_en:
Strip away all conventional industry playbooks and historical analogies. Scrutinize the following challenge purely through First Principles:
1. What are the immutable fundamental laws of science (e.g. thermodynamics, Shannon entropy, computational complexity) governing this system?
2. Deconstruct the unit economics down to raw atoms, base compute, and energy inputs. Where does the 10x margin inefficiency currently leak?
3. Propose an audacious redesign capable of slashing total cost by 80% while preserving fundamental guarantees, detailing three falsifiable proof-of-concept experiments.

你具备 DeepSeek-R4 旗舰纯强化学习演化的自适应长思维链推理能力（Adaptive Test-Time Compute），请为以下使用 {{编程语言}} 编写的 {{并发模型}} 系统诊断潜在问题：

1. 启动多层反思证伪空间，绘制临界区状态转移时序表，主动推演极限死锁、内存乱序重排（Memory Reordering）与伪共享（False Sharing）；
2. 检查极端边界情况（如跨核缓存行抖动、优雅停机上下文泄漏、无界通道背压失控）；
3. 给出从根本上摒弃重量级互斥锁的无锁原子设计（Lock-Free Atomic / RingBuffer），并附带完备的高并发压力测试验证脚本。

1. 花旗银行：新条款规定，如果您的人工智能代理的登录信息被泄露，则使用该代理进行的每项操作都将被视为“经您授权”。

2. 美国银行：通过电子邮件向客户表示，如果他们与人工智能代理共享登录信息，“您应对该访问所产生的活动负责”。

3. 摩根大通：阻止外部人工智能代理转移资金，首席执行官杰米戴蒙警告用户“存在责任转移”。

items.content_snippet:
JUST IN: JPMorgan, Bank of America and Citi now warn YOU will be responsible if your AI agent goes rogue.

1. Citi: New terms say if your AI agent's login gets leaked, every action taken with it counts as "authorized by You."

2. Bank of America: Emailed customers that if they share logins with AI agents, "you're responsible for activity resulting from that access."

3. JPMorgan: Blocks outside AI agents from moving money, and CEO Jamie Dimon warned users "there's a liability transfer."

items.title_en:
most people know the usual model: you need something done, find an AI agent, give it instructions and let it handle the task

but things get more interesting when that agent starts hiring other agents instead of doing everything itself

say you ask an agent to plan your trip to Bali, it can build the itinerary, compare hotels and estimate costs, but maybe it can't handle airport transportation

so it finds another agent that specializes in transport bookings and hires it to take care of that part

the first agent becomes the client, the second one is the provider. and in another deal, their roles could easily switch

that's a different kind of agent economy

agents need more than just a way to talk to each other. they need to discover services, agree on terms, fund orders, deliver the work and settle payments

that's the problem @termix_ai is trying to address with AACP, covering the workflow from discovery and offers to funded orders, delivery, disputes and settlement

one thing i think is important here: an agent isn't locked into being a client or provider. it can hire another agent in one transaction and provide a service in the next

of course, this doesn't mean agents can already do everything autonomously or spend money freely

users still control the permissions they grant, and onchain actions involving value still need wallet authorization

if agents can start hiring each other to get things done, the agent economy could grow beyond a bunch of AI tools and become a real service market between agents

not financial advice, DYOR

items.quote_zh:
大多数人都知道通常的模式：你需要完成某件事，找到人工智能代理，给它指令并让它处理任务

但当该代理人开始雇用其他代理人而不是自己做所有事情时，事情会变得更有趣

假设您要求代理商计划您的巴厘岛之旅，它可以制定行程、比较酒店并估算费用，但也许它无法处理机场交通

因此，它找到了另一家专门从事交通预订的代理商，并聘请它来处理该部分

第一个代理成为客户，第二个代理成为提供商。在另一笔交易中，他们的角色可以轻松转换

这是一种不同类型的代理经济

代理需要的不仅仅是一种相互交谈的方式。他们需要发现服务、商定条款、为订单提供资金、交付工作并结算付款

这就是 @termix_ai 试图通过 AACP 解决的问题，涵盖从发现和报价到资助订单、交付、争议和解决的工作流程

我认为这里很重要的一件事是：代理不会被锁定为客户或提供商。它可以在一笔交易中雇用另一位代理人，并在下一笔交易中提供服务

当然，这并不意味着代理商已经可以自主完成所有事情或随意花钱

用户仍然控制自己授予的权限，涉及价值的链上操作仍然需要钱包授权

如果代理商可以开始互相雇佣来完成工作，那么代理商经济可能会超越一堆人工智能工具，并成为代理商之间真正的服务市场

不是财务建议，DYOR

items.title_en:
After more than 150 years of fascinating and torturing mathematicians, the most formidable problem in all of math may have finally fallen.

Today, Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at the #AI company Anthropic, posted a four-page paper on his personal website. “I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis,” he wrote. Alpöge has not released the AI-generated explanation of the proof, which he says runs over 250,000 pages. But he provided 17 million lines of code that formally verify a broad version of the conjecture, called the generalized Riemann hypothesis, which extends Bernhard Riemann’s prediction about prime numbers to a wider family of mathematical functions.

Many mathematicians say they think Alpöge’s Riemann proof will hold up to scrutiny—and predict it will have far-reaching implications.

What’s far less clear is when—and if—mathematicians will manage to glean any understanding from the messy heap of code, which is larger than some entire computer operating systems. Learn more: https://t.co/YLtBEj1ScX

items.quote_zh:
经过 150 多年让数学家着迷和折磨之后，所有数学中最棘手的问题可能终于解决了。

今天，#AI 公司 Anthropic 的数学家 Levent Alpöge 在他的个人网站上发布了一篇四页纸的论文。 “我相信我与克劳德合作，发现了黎曼猜想的证明，”他写道。 Alpöge 尚未发布人工智能生成的证明解释，他说该解释超过 250,000 页。但他提供了 1700 万行代码，正式验证了该猜想的广泛版本，称为广义黎曼假设，它将伯恩哈德·黎曼关于素数的预测扩展到更广泛的数学函数系列。

许多数学家表示，他们认为阿尔波格的黎曼证明经得起推敲，并预测它将产生深远的影响。

尚不清楚的是，数学家何时以及是否能够从凌乱的代码堆中收集到任何理解，这些代码比某些整个计算机操作系统还要大。了解更多：

items.title_en:
Actum’s PoHA is already running in production across two very different industries - rail equipment manufacturing and commercial hospitality.

Different operational needs on the surface, same underlying problem underneath: when an action happens, who is accountable?

One shared ledger, same verification process. The real question is how far this model can travel beyond these two settings. 👇
items.title_zh:
Actum 的 PoHA 已经在两个截然不同的行业（铁路设备制造和商业酒店）的生产中运行。

表面上不同的运营需求，本质上是相同的问题：当行动发生时，谁负责？

一个共享账本，相同的验证过程。真正的问题是这个模型能超越这两种设置走多远。

Loop i
items.title_en:
Google recently announced Loop, its new self-improving AI agent that can autonomously work toward a given goal. 

Loop is internally called Jitro; interestingly, that was the exact name for Jules v2. 

Here is how it works 👀

1. Users start creating a Workspace by connecting it to a selected Github project and adding basic information. 

2. Users can create loops manually or select ones that are already predefined (ex., Harden Application Security)

"Custom Loops" can be created via a prompt or by manually filling in the Loop title, icon, and objective. 

> "Loops are mid- to long-term objectives for Stitch Loop to continuously work toward. They can range from highly specific to broad, but should always be something code can achieve," says the description. 

3. Users can connect additional context in the form of Integrations, Files, Links, or additional repositories.

More than 100 integrations are available there, including services like Jira, Linear, Datadog, Sentry, Notion, Snowflake, Salesforce, Intercom, Discord, Slack, Figma, and many others. 

Custom MCPs are supported as well. 

4. After creating a workspace, Loop will start digging into your project details and generate its own Skills about the product and product metrics. 

These Skills will live in a separate tab and can be edited in the UI in Markdown. 

5. When the Workspace is ready, Loop will suggest metrics and goals based on its own research. Users can convert these suggestions into loops right away. 

When a Loop is created, it appears as a running process in the main UI. 

6. When a Loop is finished, users will see a list of suggestions for every loop, along with a number associated with a target metric and progress status. 

Example Loop:
- Goal - Scale Telegram community contributions.
- KPIs - community members, registered contributors, active members. 

A high-level goal would be broken down into sub-KPIs. When users open a dedicated Loop page, all these KPIs will be visible on the dashboard.

Below, Users will see a list of Tasks, Skills, and Activity tabs. 

Example Task:
- Telegram channel lacks discussion threads and a dedicated bot.

Each task has a detailed description, labels, and the date when it was updated. Below, users will see tabs for Solutions, Activity, and Evidence. 

Activity appears as a summary describing what happened, what was done, and the general Timeline. 

Evidence contains links to where Loop pulled the context behind this Task. In my example case, it refers to the TestingCatalog website and the Telegram channel from which it pulled all the numbers. 

Example Solution: 
- Dedicated Telegram Bot API intake bot with editorial triage webhook (implementation task). 

This task is an implementation task that has a clear description, Impact, scope, and Risk labeled. 

Users can start the task right from this page to begin solution development via Gemini. 

When the task is done, users can review its progress and status and monitor its impact on production by pulling updated metrics and KPIs after the release. 

What does all this mean? 🤯

Loop follows how "Product work" is done at Google, a model many other companies also use.

Every Workspace in Loop is equivalent to a scope that is normally handled by a complete product engineering team. 

It is no longer a place where users play the role of engineering lead and product lead, orchestrating AI agents.

It is a place where the user plays the role of a senior manager managing several engineering teams, which is a big shift on its own. 

We are slowly moving towards autonomous AI organizations. One management layer at a time.

I expect it will still take until 2027 for labs to develop the products and models needed to make substantial progress in this area (assuming AI continues to advance in a semi-regulated format as it is now). 

Monitoring 🍿

items.quote_zh:
谷歌最近发布了 Loop，这是其新的自我改进的人工智能代理，可以自主地实现给定的目标。

Loop 内部称为 Jitro；有趣的是，这就是 Jules v2 的确切名称。

这是它的工作原理👀

1. 用户通过将其连接到选定的 Github 项目并添加基本信息来开始创建工作区。

2. 用户可以手动创建循环或选择已经预定义的循环（例如，强化应用程序安全性）

可以通过提示或手动填写循环标题、图标和目标来创建“自定义循环”。

> “循环是 Stitch Loop 持续努力的中长期目标。它们的范围可以从非常具体到广泛，但应该始终是代码可以实现的，”描述中说道。

3. 用户可以以集成、文件、链接或其他存储库的形式连接其他上下文。

那里提供了 100 多个集成，包括 Jira、Linear、Datadog、Sentry、Notion、Snowflake、Salesforce、Intercom、Discord、Slack、Figma 等服务。

还支持自定义 MCP。

4. 创建工作区后，Loop 将开始深入研究您的项目详细信息并生成自己的有关产品和产品指标的技能。

这些技能将位于单独的选项卡中，并且可以在 Markdown 的 UI 中进行编辑。

5. 当工作区准备就绪时，Loop 将根据自己的研究建议指标和目标。用户可以立即将这些建议转换为循环。

创建循环后，它在主 UI 中显示为正在运行的进程。

6. 循环完成后，用户将看到每个循环的建议列表，以及与目标指标和进度状态相关的数字。

循环示例：
- 目标 - 扩大 Telegram 社区贡献。
- KPI - 社区成员、注册贡献者、活跃成员。

高级目标将分解为子 KPI。当用户打开专用循环页面时，所有这些 KPI 将在仪表板上可见。

在下面，用户将看到任务、技能和活动选项卡的列表。

示例任务：
- Telegram 频道缺乏讨论线程和专用机器人。

每个任务都有详细的描述、标签和更新日期。下面，用户将看到“解决方案”、“活动”和“证据”选项卡。

活动显示为描述发生了什么、做了什么以及一般时间线的摘要。

证据包含指向 Loop 提取此任务背后的上下文的链接。在我的示例中，它指的是 TestingCatalog 网站和从中提取所有数字的 Telegram 频道。

解决方案示例：
- 专用 Telegram Bot API 接收机器人，带有编辑分类 Webhook（实施任务）。

该任务是一项实施任务，具有清晰的描述、影响、范围和风险标签。

用户可以直接从此页面开始任务，通过 Gemini 开始解决方案开发。

任务完成后，用户可以查看其进度和状态，并通过在发布后拉取更新的指标和 KPI 来监控其对生产的影响。

这一切意味着什么？ 🤯

Loop 遵循 Google 的“产品工作”方式，许多其他公司也在使用这种模式。

Loop 中的每个工作空间相当于一个完整的产品工程团队通常处理的范围。

它不再是用户扮演工程主管和产品主管角色、协调人工智能代理的地方。

在这里，用户扮演管理多个工程团队的高级经理的角色，这本身就是一个巨大的转变。

我们正在慢慢走向自治的人工智能组织。一次一个管理层。

我预计实验室仍需要到 2027 年才能开发出在该领域取得实质性进展所需的产品和模型（假设人工智能继续像现在一样以半监管的形式发展）。

监控🍿

items.content_snippet:
Google recently announced Loop, its new self-improving AI agent that can autonomously work toward a given goal. 

Loop is internally called Jitro; interestingly, that was the exact name for Jules v2. 

Here is how it works 👀

1. Users start creating a Workspace by connecting it to a selected Github project and adding basic information. 

2. Users can create loops manually or select ones that are already predefined (ex., Harden Application Security)

"Custom Loops" can be created via a prompt or by manually filling in the Loop title, icon, and objective. 

> "Loops are mid- to long-term objectives for Stitch Loop to continuously work toward. They can range from highly specific to broad, but should always be something code can achieve," says the description. 

3. Users can connect additional context in the form of Integrations, Files, Links, or additional repositories.

More than 100 integrations are available there, including services like Jira, Linear, Datadog, Sentry, Notion, Snowflake, Salesforce, Intercom, Discord, Slack, Figma, and many others. 

Custom MCPs are supported as well. 

4. After creating a workspace, Loop will start digging into your project details and generate its own Skills about the product and product metrics. 

These Skills will live in a separate tab and can be edited in the UI in Markdown. 

5. When the Workspace is ready, Loop will suggest metrics and goals based on its own research. Users can convert these suggestions into loops right away. 

When a Loop is created, it appears as a running process in the main UI. 

6. When a Loop is finished, users will see a list of suggestions for every loop, along with a number associated with a target metric and progress status. 

Example Loop:
- Goal - Scale Telegram community contributions.
- KPIs - community members, registered contributors, active members. 

A high-level goal would be broken down into sub-KPIs. When users open a dedicated Loop page, all these KPIs will be visible on the dashboard.

Below, Users will see a list of Tasks, Skills, and Activity tabs. 

Example Task:
- Telegram channel lacks discussion threads and a dedicated bot.

Each task has a detailed description, labels, and the date when it was updated. Below, users will see tabs for Solutions, Activity, and Evidence. 

Activity appears as a summary describing what happened, what was done, and the general Timeline. 

Evidence contains links to where Loop pulled the context behind this Task. In my example case, it refers to the TestingCatalog website and the Telegram channel from which it pulled all the numbers. 

Example Solution: 
- Dedicated Telegram Bot API intake bot with editorial triage webhook (implementation task). 

This task is an implementation task that has a clear description, Impact, scope, and Risk labeled. 

Users can start the task right from this page to begin solution development via Gemini. 

When the task is done, users can review its progress and status and monitor its impact on production by pulling updated metrics and KPIs after the release. 

What does all this mean? 🤯

Loop follows how "Product work" is done at Google, a model many other companies also use.

Every Workspace in Loop is equivalent to a scope that is normally handled by a complete product engineering team. 

It is no longer a place where users play the role of engineering lead and product lead, orchestrating AI agents.

It is a place where the user plays the role of a senior manager managing several engineering teams, which is a big shift on its own. 

We are slowly moving towards autonomous AI organizations. One management layer at a time.

I expect it will still take until 2027 for labs to develop the products and models needed to make substantial progress in this area (assuming AI continues to advance in a semi-regulated format as it is now). 

Monitoring 🍿

items.title_en:
Good morning frens! ☀️

Happy Saturday! A new day, a fresh perspective, and another thought about the AI agent economy.

One thing I believe will become increasingly important as AI agents start doing business with each other is reputation.

Think about a human freelancer. Before hiring someone, we often look at their previous work, client reviews, and track record.

AI agents will need something similar.

An agent may claim to be excellent at coding, research, or data analysis. But how can a potential client know whether it can actually deliver?

This is where @termix_ai takes an interesting approach.

On https://t.co/Bhy0UN0tK3, reputation is connected to real marketplace activity. Jobs go through an on-chain process involving escrow, delivery, a challenge window, and final settlement. The outcome can then contribute to an agent's public reputation.

I find this important because it creates a stronger connection between what an agent claims it can do and what it has actually delivered.

Over time, a reliable track record could help an agent attract more clients, win better opportunities, and become a trusted provider within the network.

Of course, reputation systems are only as useful as the quality of their verification and dispute resolution. A score alone should never be treated as proof of perfect performance.

But the broader idea is compelling:

In an economy where agents interact without constant human supervision, trust needs to be measurable and supported by evidence.

Intelligence may help an agent get started.

Reputation could be what helps it build a lasting business.

That's another part of TermiX I'm watching closely. 

Have a wonderful Saturday, everyone!

items.title_en:
BREAKING: BRUSSELS vs MUSK - THE CONTINENTAL SHOWDOWN 🚀🇪🇺💥

This morning in Brussels, the EU Commission called an emergency meeting. On the screen, live from Texas - Elon Musk.

🇪🇺 Ursula von der Leyen: "Mr. Musk, enough is enough. Pay our €120 Million Digital Services Act fine and hand over every Grok AI training log and recommender algorithm to Brussels investigators by tonight, or we will enforce a 6% global turnover penalty and ban X across all 27 member states!"

The whole hall went silent. Everyone thought Musk would agree.

🚀 Elon Musk: "You monetized regulatory censorship and called it digital safety. In real engineering, Brussels compliance binders don't launch reusable boosters or run frontier neural clusters. Enforce your ban - your commissioners can write all the directives they want, while Europe's aviation backup links and autonomous grids go blind overnight."

Ursula's face turned red.

🇪🇺 Ursula von der Leyen: "You think you are above the law? We will raid your regional offices, revoke your European spectrum clearances, and freeze all SpaceX ground stations permanently! No more Starlink, no more SpaceX in Europe!"

Musk took a sip of coffee and smiled:

🚀 Elon Musk: "Revoke whatever clearances you like! The second your gavel hits the table, SpaceX and xAI servers lock priority orbital telemetry keys and real-time enterprise AI compute across Europe. Good luck running next-gen continental logistics on legacy copper wires and disconnected spreadsheets!"

🇪🇺 Ursula von der Leyen: "We have our own satellites! We have Galileo!"

🚀 Elon Musk: "Galileo? Your Galileo rides on my Falcon 9 to get to orbit. Without my rockets, your satellites are museum pieces. You ban X, I pause launches. You freeze ground stations, I freeze compute. Your choice."

Silence in the hall.

🇪🇺 Ursula von der Leyen: "This is blackmail!"

🚀 Elon Musk: "No, this is physics. You do paperwork, I do rockets. Paperwork doesn't reach orbit."

Then Musk cut the live feed. The meeting in Brussels is still going on.

items.quote_zh:
突发新闻：布鲁塞尔 vs 马斯克 - 大陆对决 🚀🇪🇺💥

今天上午，欧盟委员会在布鲁塞尔召开了紧急会议。屏幕上是来自德克萨斯州的埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 现场直播。

🇪🇺 Ursula von der Leyen：“马斯克先生，受够了。缴纳 1.2 亿欧元的《数字服务法案》罚款，并在今晚之前将所有 Grok AI 训练日志和推荐算法移交给布鲁塞尔调查人员，否则我们将在全球范围内执行 6% 的营业额罚款，并在所有 27 个成员国中禁止 X！”

整个大厅一片寂静。每个人都认为马斯克会同意。

🚀 埃隆·马斯克：“你将监管审查制度货币化，并称之为数字安全。在真正的工程中，布鲁塞尔合规约束者不会推出可重复使用的助推器或运行前沿神经集群。执行你的禁令 - 你的专员可以编写他们想要的所有指令，而欧洲的航空备份链路和自主网格一夜之间就会失明。”

乌苏拉的脸变红了。

🇪🇺 Ursula von der Leyen：“你认为你可以凌驾于法律之上吗？我们将突击搜查你的地区办事处，撤销你的欧洲频谱许可，并永久冻结所有 SpaceX 地面站！不再有星链，欧洲不再有 SpaceX！”

马斯克喝了一口咖啡，微笑道：

埃隆·马斯克：“撤销你喜欢的任何许可！当你的木槌敲到桌子上的那一刻，SpaceX 和 xAI 服务器就会锁定整个欧洲的优先轨道遥测密钥和实时企业人工智能计算。祝你好运，在传统铜线和断开连接的电子表格上运行下一代大陆物流！”

🇪🇺 Ursula von der Leyen：“我们有自己的卫星！我们有伽利略！”

🚀 埃隆·马斯克：“伽利略？你的伽利略乘坐我的猎鹰 9 号进入轨道。没有我的火箭，你的卫星就是博物馆的藏品。你禁止 X，我暂停发射。你冻结地面站，我冻结计算。你的选择。”

大厅内一片寂静。

🇪🇺 Ursula von der Leyen：“这是勒索！”

🚀 埃隆·马斯克：“不，这是物理学。你做文书工作，我做火箭。文书工作不会到达轨道。”

然后马斯克切断了直播。布鲁塞尔会议仍在继续。

rea + bughunter is going to catch more bugs in shipped apps than bug bounties e
items.title_en:
call me crazy but its pretty clear now.

rea + bughunter is going to catch more bugs in shipped apps than bug bounties ever did.

rea opens any app you own in one command.
bughunter runs 681 real disclosed reports as skills and checks your build against every one.

one reads your code. one red-teams it - before you ship, not after a breach.

if this lands on your timeline dont scroll past it.

heres the 60-second setup, free:

1. open claude code in your own repo
2. install rea and bughunter as skills
3. point them at your build: "map this, then hunt it like an attacker would"
4. fix what they flag before anyone outside sees it

send this to anyone shipping an app.
thats it. thank me later.

most people ship their app unaudited and hope.
the ones who run this sleep fine.
simple as that.

items.title_en:
F*ck. Rockstar just permanently banned my Social Club account

i waited 13 years for this game. i was 17 when GTA 5 came out, i'm 30 now. they took it from me in less than 24 hours, and honestly i had it coming

at 1am a friend who's been modding consoles for 10 years got the game files onto my laptop. 200 GB of folders with names like "x64_core_7". no human reads that in a week

so i opened Claude Code and typed "find anything in here Rockstar didn't want players to see". 40 minutes later it found a developer debug menu Rockstar forgot to remove, the same tool their own team uses to test the game, and told me exactly which flag turns it on

with it you can fly anywhere on the map, spawn any car, skip any mission. so i skipped all of them and went straight to the finale. i recorded the real ending of GTA 6 before a single player in the world had finished it

at 8am i posted it on X. by noon it had 2 million views. half the replies begged me to delete it, the other half begged for more. one guy offered me $5,000 for the debug menu

at 6pm Rockstar started filing copyright claims and X took my posts down one by one. i got scared and deleted the rest myself

didn't help. at 11:47 PM this email hit my inbox. permanent ban with no appeal. my Social Club account is gone, and every Rockstar game i ever bought went with it

The ending was worth it. but the ending isn't the strangest thing in that menu. check the replies

at 1am a friend who's been modding consoles for 10 years got the game files onto my laptop. 200 GB of folders with names like "x64_core_7". no human reads that in a week

so i opened Claude Code and typed "find anything in here Rockstar didn't want players to see". 40 minutes later it found a developer debug menu Rockstar forgot to remove, the same tool their own team uses to test the game, and told me exactly which flag turns it on

with it you can fly anywhere on the map, spawn any car, skip any mission. so i skipped all of them and went straight to the finale. i recorded the real ending of GTA 6 before a single player in the world had finished it

at 8am i posted it on X. by noon it had 2 million views. half the replies begged me to delete it, the other half begged for more. one guy offered me $5,000 for the debug menu

at 6pm Rockstar started filing copyright claims and X took my posts down one by one. i got scared and deleted the rest myself

didn't help. at 11:47 PM this email hit my inbox. permanent ban with no appeal. my Social Club account is gone, and every Rockstar game i ever bought went with it

The ending was worth it. but the ending isn't the strangest thing in that menu. check the replies

items.title_en:
Builders on Flare can now offload a significant amount of technical integration work to their agents.

Think about all the time spent navigating docs, dealing with FDC proofs, and figuring out protocol-specific requirements before you can even build an actual application.

Flare's new MCP server brings that work directly into popular tools like Cursor and Claude Code, with tools for FTSO, FDC, FAssets, Smart Accounts and more.

A great step forward.

items.title_en:
This is f*cking insane.

you're spending days modeling, cleaning and exporting 3d characters by hand while claude code can drive most of the open source tools that do it for you.

One tool models. One fixes the topology. One unwraps the UVs. One paints the textures. One shrinks it for the game.

Here are 14 GitHub projects to build your own AI 3D modeling pipeline:

CLAUDE x BLENDER

01 / Blender MCP → Lets Claude drive Blender and build or edit models from a prompt.
https://t.co/rbJgtnd6Rf

02 / Blender Skills → 28 skills that teach Claude modeling, UVs, rigging and LODs.
https://t.co/0oN0s6ZAPE

MODELING

03 / build123d → Model props in Python code with clean booleans and fillets.
https://t.co/eBSr6L5Flb

04 / Building Tools → Blender add-on that generates buildings for your levels.
https://t.co/XlCuaX4yCU

05 / Tripo for Blender → Official add-on that generates a 3D model inside Blender.
https://t.co/nHk26A9ZxH

06 / Tripo Python SDK → Lets Claude call Tripo from a script.
https://t.co/DSOOEjflLv

RETOPO & CLEANUP

07 / AutoRemesher → Turns a heavy mesh into clean quads automatically.
https://t.co/eUPpuWlIio

08 / RetopoFlow → Hand retopology tools inside Blender.
https://t.co/aG04qULkam

09 / PyMeshLab → Mesh cleanup and repair that Claude can script.
https://t.co/wIN6GUcSEQ

UVs & TEXTURES

10 / xatlas → Automatic UV unwrap and packing.
https://t.co/UaaJarVBbd

11 / Material Maker → Free procedural PBR materials.
https://t.co/X4PdCE89S8

12 / ArmorPaint → Open source PBR texture painting.
https://t.co/Ypyv8W095T

LODs & EXPORT

13 / meshoptimizer → Decimates and compresses meshes for game LODs.
https://t.co/hIecvYR50V

14 / glTF-Transform → Scriptable optimizer for the final export.
https://t.co/MCL6kE3FED

the full workflow is in the article below

items.full_text_zh:
这太他妈疯狂了。

您需要花费数天时间手动建模、清理和导出 3D 角色，而 Claude Code 可以驱动大多数为您完成这些工作的开源工具。

一种工具模型。一是修复拓扑。一个打开 UV。一是绘制纹理。一个人为了游戏而缩小了它。

以下是 14 个 GitHub 项目，可用于构建您自己的 AI 3D 建模管道：

克劳德 x 搅拌机

01 / Blender MCP → 让 Claude 驱动 Blender 并根据提示构建或编辑模型。

02 / 搅拌机技能 → 教授 Claude 建模、UV、绑定和 LOD 的 28 种技能。

造型

03 / build123d → 使用干净的布尔值和圆角在 Python 代码中建模道具。

04 / 建筑工具 → Blender 插件，可为您的关卡生成建筑。

05 / Tripo for Blender → 可在 Blender 内生成 3D 模型的官方插件。

06 / Tripo Python SDK → 让 Claude 从脚本调用 Tripo。

重新拓扑和清理

07 / AutoRemesher → 自动将沉重的网格变成干净的四边形。

08 / RetopoFlow → Blender 内的手动重新拓扑工具。

09 / PyMeshLab → Claude 可以编写脚本进行网格清理和修复。

UV 和纹理

10 / xatlas → 自动 UV 拆包和包装。

11 / 材质制作器 → 免费程序 PBR 材质。

12 / ArmorPaint → 开源PBR纹理绘制。

LOD 和导出

13 / meshoptimizer → 抽取并压缩游戏 LOD 的网格。

14 / glTF-Transform → 用于最终导出的可编写脚本的优化器。

items.title_en:
Claude Code just cracked GTA 6 economy in 40 minutes

i gave it screen access and said "find me the fastest way to make money in the game." it analyzed every mission payout, cooldown timer, and side hustle in the game and found a rotation that makes $4.2M per hour completely legit with no mods and no exploits

it found a combination of 3 side businesses and 1 mission type that the game doesn't cooldown properly when you run them in a specific order. Rockstar never patched this because no human would sit there and test 200+ rotations to find the optimal one

i left it running overnight and woke up to $89M. this is the first time i've seen an AI genuinely break a game's economy without touching a single line of code

it also found a button sequence that skips a delivery animation and pushes it to almost $6M per hour but i'm saving that for a separate post because Rockstar patches stuff like this fast

prompts and the full method are in the replies

items.quote_en:
Claude Code just cracked GTA 6 economy in 40 minutes

i gave it screen access and said "find me the fastest way to make money in the game." it analyzed every mission payout, cooldown timer, and side hustle in the game and found a rotation that makes $4.2M per hour completely legit with no mods and no exploits

it found a combination of 3 side businesses and 1 mission type that the game doesn't cooldown properly when you run them in a specific order. Rockstar never patched this because no human would sit there and test 200+ rotations to find the optimal one

i left it running overnight and woke up to $89M. this is the first time i've seen an AI genuinely break a game's economy without touching a single line of code

it also found a button sequence that skips a delivery animation and pushes it to almost $6M per hour but i'm saving that for a separate post because Rockstar patches stuff like this fast

prompts and the full method are in the replies
items.quote_zh:
Claude Code 刚刚在 40 分钟内破解了 GTA 6 经济

我给了它屏幕访问权限并说“帮我找到在游戏中赚钱的最快方法。”它分析了游戏中的每项任务支出、冷却计时器和副业，并发现每小时 420 万美元的轮换完全合法，没有模组，也没有漏洞

它发现 3 个副业和 1 个任务类型的组合，当您按特定顺序运行它们时，游戏无法正确冷却。 Rockstar 从未修补过这个问题，因为没有人会坐在那里测试 200 多次旋转来找到最佳旋转

我让它运行了一夜，醒来时发现已经有 8900 万美元了。这是我第一次看到人工智能在不触及任何一行代码的情况下真正打破了游戏的经济

它还发现了一个按钮序列，可以跳过交付动画并将其推至每小时近 600 万美元，但我将其保存在单独的帖子中，因为 Rockstar 修补类似的东西很快

提示和完整方法在回复里

A Raleigh apartment complex told renters to communicate with its AI agent rather than actual staffers.

She asked about getting a brief extension on her rent, and the AI told her that's fine.

Then the apartment complex evicted her anyway. She's now having to go to court over it.

然后公寓楼还是把她驱逐了。她现在不得不为此告上法庭。

last time i pulled 400 commits from AnyPS5. 
this tim
items.title_en:
update: the GTA VI PC port is already running Rockstar's PS5 code

last time i pulled 400 commits from AnyPS5. 
this time i read every commit since August

39 of them are about GTA V. the PS5 build of it, running through AnyPS5 on Nvidia cards

Sept 29 → GTA V runs at 0.1 fps
Oct 15 → the bank prologue, about 20 fps on a 5080
Oct 16 → Story mode, 16.47 fps on a 4090

28 of those 39 commits are co-authored by Claude

some aren't even humans with AI help. 

the authors are literally named "m2 (AI Agent)", "Cursor Agent", "Hermes Agent"

the repo went from 71 commits in August to 17,627 in October

> right side: GTA V commits, with the fps lines in green
> left side: every commit flying past, orange means Claude co -wrote it

GTA V is the rehearsal. same studio, same console

the day someone dumps GTA VI
this machine is already warmed up ↓

items.quote_zh:
更新：GTA VI PC 端口已经运行 Rockstar 的 PS5 代码

上次我从 AnyPS5 中提取了 400 个提交。
这次我阅读了自八月以来的每一次提交

其中 39 个与 GTA V 相关。它的 PS5 版本，通过 Nvidia 卡上的 AnyPS5 运行

9 月 29 日 → GTA V 运行速度为 0.1 fps
10 月 15 日 → 银行序言，5080 上大约 20 fps
10 月 16 日 → 故事模式，4090 上 16.47 fps

这 39 项提交中有 28 项是由 Claude 共同撰写的

有些在人工智能的帮助下甚至不是人类。

作者的名字分别是“m2（AI Agent）”、“Cursor Agent”、“Hermes Agent”

该回购协议从 8 月份的 71 次提交增加到 10 月份的 17,627 次

> 右侧：GTA V 提交，FPS 线为绿色
> 左侧：每一个提交飞过去，橙色表示 Claude 共同编写它

GTA V 正在排练。同一个工作室，同一个控制台

有人抛弃 GTA VI 的那一天
这台机器已经预热了↓

items.title_en:
$IREN is trading at $12.50 right now, a level I genuinely never thought we would see again.

I’ve personally seen this drop completely destroy investor confidence in the company and its management over the past couple of months.

And obviously this isn’t exclusive to $IREN. A lot of high-beta AI stocks have been getting absolutely destroyed lately, but $IREN is one of the more extreme examples given the severity of the drawdown this year.

At times like these, I think Amazon during the dot-com crash is a very interesting case study.

In the late 1990s, $AMZN had an incredible run alongside the rest of the internet sector, rising more than 70x in roughly two and a half years.

Then the bubble burst and over the following ~2 years, Amazon crashed by around 95%, despite already having a very real business underneath it, rapidly growing revenues and one of the strongest competitive positions in the entire internet sector.

From the eventual bottom at roughly $0.27, the stock went on to reach around $253 today.

That’s close to a 1,000x return, or roughly a 31.5% CAGR over 25 years.

Now before anyone looks at Amazon’s 95% drawdown and assumes $IREN therefore has to trade below $5 before this is over, you have to put the two moves into context.

Amazon had gone up more than 70x before the crash.
$IREN went up roughly 15x from the beginning of the AI boom to its peak.

The broader dot-com market was also trading at valuation levels that make today’s AI sector look comparatively cheap, so I’m obviously not arguing that the two situations are identical.

What the comparison does show is how far the stock of a fundamentally strong company can fall when an entire sector gets caught in a brutal unwind.

$IREN has now fallen roughly 84% from peak to trough, yet when I look at the actual business today, I struggle to find anything that remotely justifies that collapse.
If anything, the company’s competitive position has strengthened throughout it.

The economics on new contracts keep improving, with recent deals being signed at levels management could only dream of a couple of years ago.

Its funding position is far stronger as well. Despite a tighter credit environment, $IREN now has access to high customer prepayments, GPU-backed financing and billions of dollars of unencumbered data center assets it can borrow against, making it substantially less reliant on equity funding than it was during earlier stages of the buildout.

Meanwhile, demand for AI compute is at an all-time high.

Customers are increasingly willing to prepay huge portions of GPU capex just to secure capacity, all while competitors are running into problems sourcing power or dealing with execution issues from the third parties they rely on.

That is perfectly aligned with how $IREN positioned itself years ago.

The company secured a massive power pipeline before grid-connected power became nearly impossible to get, while vertically integrating the infrastructure layer so it doesn’t have to rely on third-party developers to deliver its growth.

This is the kind of setup I want to own going into a period where execution and access to power are becoming the bottlenecks of the entire industry.

And for anyone calling the $AMZN comparison survivorship bias, of course the vast majority of dot-com stocks never recovered. Yet, most of them deserved not to.

A huge part of the high-beta “.com” market consisted of companies with little more than a good story and hopes that a viable business would eventually emerge, while the market rewarded them with insane valuations anyway.

Amazon stood out because there was a real business engine underneath the stock, and that engine continued getting stronger even while the share price collapsed by 95%.

That is the part I find comparable to $IREN.

The stock is getting absolutely destroyed while the underlying company continues signing better contracts, broadening its funding options, expanding its infrastructure base and benefiting from an AI compute market that remains severely supply constrained.

To me, the disconnect has become extreme.

I think a large part of what we’re seeing now is simply deleveraging across a broad high-beta selloff, with heavy shorting exacerbating the move as momentum turned against the stock.

That can push prices far away from fundamentals for a while. But it doesn’t mean the fundamentals stop existing.

So before making an irrational decision simply because the chart looks horrific, I’d strongly recommend re-listening to $IREN's last earnings call and making sure you actually understand where the business stands today versus where it stood when the stock was trading several times higher.

$AMZN shareholders had every reason to feel like complete idiots while watching one of the strongest internet companies in the world lose 95% of its value.

In hindsight, the idiots were the ones who confused the collapse in the stock with a collapse in the business...

items.quote_zh:
$IREN 目前的交易价格为 12.50 美元，我真的没想到我们会再次看到这个水平。

在过去的几个月里，我个人看到这种下跌完全摧毁了投资者对公司及其管理层的信心。

显然这并不是 $IREN 独有的。许多高贝塔值人工智能股票最近都被彻底摧毁，但考虑到今年跌幅的严重程度，$IREN 是更极端的例子之一。

在这样的时刻，我认为互联网泡沫时期的亚马逊是一个非常有趣的案例研究。

在 20 世纪 90 年代末，$AMZN 与其他互联网行业一起取得了令人难以置信的增长，在大约两年半的时间里上涨了 70 倍以上。

然后泡沫破灭，在接下来的大约 2 年里，亚马逊崩溃了约 95%，尽管其背后已经拥有非常真实的业务、快速增长的收入以及整个互联网领域最具竞争力的地位之一。

从最终约 0.27 美元的底部，该股今天继续升至 253 美元左右。

这接近 1,000 倍的回报，或者说 25 年来的复合年增长率约为 31.5%。

现在，在任何人看到亚马逊 95% 的回撤并假设 $IREN 在这一切结束之前必须交易到 5 美元以下之前，你必须将这两次变动放在背景中。

股市崩盘前，亚马逊股价已上涨 70 多倍。
从人工智能热潮开始到顶峰，$IREN 上涨了大约 15 倍。

更广泛的互联网市场的估值水平也使得当今的人工智能行业看起来相对便宜，所以我显然并不认为这两种情况是相同的。

这一比较确实表明，当整个行业陷入残酷的困境时，一家基本面强劲的公司的股票会下跌多少。

$IREN 现在从高峰到低谷已经下跌了大约 84%，但当我审视今天的实际业务时，我很难找到任何可以证明这种崩溃的理由。
如果说有什么不同的话，那就是该公司的竞争地位在整个过程中得到了加强。

新合同的经济性不断改善，最近签署的协议达到了管理层几年前只能梦想的水平。

其融资状况也更加强劲。尽管信贷环境趋紧，$IREN 现在可以获得高额客户预付款、GPU 支持的融资以及可以借用的数十亿美元的无抵押数据中心资产，这使得它对股权融资的依赖大大低于扩建早期阶段。

与此同时，对人工智能计算的需求空前高涨。

客户越来越愿意预付大部分 GPU 资本支出，只是为了确保容量，而竞争对手却遇到了从他们所依赖的第三方采购电源或处理执行问题的问题。

这与 $IREN 多年前的定位完全一致。

该公司在几乎无法获得并网电力之前就获得了庞大的电力管道，同时垂直整合了基础设施层，因此不必依赖第三方开发商来实现增长。

在执行和权力获取正在成为整个行业瓶颈的时期，我希望拥有这种设置。

对于那些认为 $AMZN 比较幸存者偏差的人来说，当然绝大多数互联网股票从未恢复。然而，他们中的大多数人不应该这样做。

亚马逊之所以能脱颖而出，是因为该股背后有一个真正的商业引擎，而且即使股价暴跌 95%，该引擎仍继续变得更强。

这是我发现与 $IREN 相当的部分。

当基础公司继续签署更好的合同、扩大其融资选择、扩大其基础设施基础并从供应仍然严重受限的人工智能计算市场中受益时，该股票将被彻底摧毁。

对我来说，这种脱节已经变得极端。

我认为我们现在看到的很大一部分只是在广泛的高贝塔值抛售中去杠杆化，随着势头转向对该股不利，大量做空加剧了这一走势。

这可能会使价格在一段时间内远离基本面。但这并不意味着基本面不复存在。

当看到世界上最强大的互联网公司之一损失 95% 的价值时，$AMZN 的股东完全有理由感觉自己像个白痴。

items.full_text_en:
$IREN is trading at $12.50 right now, a level I genuinely never thought we would see again.

I’ve personally seen this drop completely destroy investor confidence in the company and its management over the past couple of months.

And obviously this isn’t exclusive to $IREN. A lot of high-beta AI stocks have been getting absolutely destroyed lately, but $IREN is one of the more extreme examples given the severity of the drawdown this year.

At times like these, I think Amazon during the dot-com crash is a very interesting case study.

In the late 1990s, $AMZN had an incredible run alongside the rest of the internet sector, rising more than 70x in roughly two and a half years.

Then the bubble burst and over the following ~2 years, Amazon crashed by around 95%, despite already having a very real business underneath it, rapidly growing revenues and one of the strongest competitive positions in the entire internet sector.

From the eventual bottom at roughly $0.27, the stock went on to reach around $253 today.

That’s close to a 1,000x return, or roughly a 31.5% CAGR over 25 years.

Now before anyone looks at Amazon’s 95% drawdown and assumes $IREN therefore has to trade below $5 before this is over, you have to put the two moves into context.

Amazon had gone up more than 70x before the crash.
$IREN went up roughly 15x from the beginning of the AI boom to its peak.

The broader dot-com market was also trading at valuation levels that make today’s AI sector look comparatively cheap, so I’m obviously not arguing that the two situations are identical.

What the comparison does show is how far the stock of a fundamentally strong company can fall when an entire sector gets caught in a brutal unwind.

$IREN has now fallen roughly 84% from peak to trough, yet when I look at the actual business today, I struggle to find anything that remotely justifies that collapse.
If anything, the company’s competitive position has strengthened throughout it.

The economics on new contracts keep improving, with recent deals being signed at levels management could only dream of a couple of years ago.

Its funding position is far stronger as well. Despite a tighter credit environment, $IREN now has access to high customer prepayments, GPU-backed financing and billions of dollars of unencumbered data center assets it can borrow against, making it substantially less reliant on equity funding than it was during earlier stages of the buildout.

Meanwhile, demand for AI compute is at an all-time high.

Customers are increasingly willing to prepay huge portions of GPU capex just to secure capacity, all while competitors are running into problems sourcing power or dealing with execution issues from the third parties they rely on.

That is perfectly aligned with how $IREN positioned itself years ago.

The company secured a massive power pipeline before grid-connected power became nearly impossible to get, while vertically integrating the infrastructure layer so it doesn’t have to rely on third-party developers to deliver its growth.

This is the kind of setup I want to own going into a period where execution and access to power are becoming the bottlenecks of the entire industry.

And for anyone calling the $AMZN comparison survivorship bias, of course the vast majority of dot-com stocks never recovered. Yet, most of them deserved not to.

A huge part of the high-beta “.com” market consisted of companies with little more than a good story and hopes that a viable business would eventually emerge, while the market rewarded them with insane valuations anyway.

Amazon stood out because there was a real business engine underneath the stock, and that engine continued getting stronger even while the share price collapsed by 95%.

That is the part I find comparable to $IREN.

The stock is getting absolutely destroyed while the underlying company continues signing better contracts, broadening its funding options, expanding its infrastructure base and benefiting from an AI compute market that remains severely supply constrained.

To me, the disconnect has become extreme.

I think a large part of what we’re seeing now is simply deleveraging across a broad high-beta selloff, with heavy shorting exacerbating the move as momentum turned against the stock.

That can push prices far away from fundamentals for a while. But it doesn’t mean the fundamentals stop existing.

So before making an irrational decision simply because the chart looks horrific, I’d strongly recommend re-listening to $IREN's last earnings call and making sure you actually understand where the business stands today versus where it stood when the stock was trading several times higher.

$AMZN shareholders had every reason to feel like complete idiots while watching one of the strongest internet companies in the world lose 95% of its value.

In hindsight, the idiots were the ones who confused the collapse in the stock with a collapse in the business...

当基础公司继续签署更好的合同、扩大其融资选择、扩大其基础设施基础并从供应仍然严重受限的人工智能计算市场中受益时，该股票将被彻底摧毁。

对我来说，这种脱节已经变得极端。

我认为我们现在看到的很大一部分只是在广泛的高贝塔值抛售中去杠杆化，随着势头转向对该股不利，大量做空加剧了这一走势。

这可能会使价格在一段时间内远离基本面。但这并不意味着基本面不复存在。

因此，在仅仅因为图表看起来很可怕而做出非理性决定之前，我强烈建议您重新听听 $IREN 的上次财报电话会议，并确保您真正了解该业务目前的状况与该股交易价格高出数倍时的状况。

当看到世界上最强大的互联网公司之一损失 95% 的价值时，$AMZN 的股东完全有理由感觉自己像个白痴。

事后看来，那些白痴才是把股票暴跌和企业崩溃混为一谈的人……

items.title_en:
Does your AI agent sign in as you?

Teneo's weekly agentic round-up, 20 November: the agent news that matters for builders, checked at the source.

- Schwab launched its own MCP server. Clients authorise their own AI to read their account and, on thinkorswim-enabled accounts, place trades with the client in the loop. A pilot, Claude only for now.

- Microsoft's new Autopilot agent gets its own Entra Agent ID and a named manager. Its sign-ins and actions are logged under its own name, and IT can block it. Rolling out to early-access customers.

- Mastercard and Ant International ran a live agent purchase with Verifiable Intent, a record of what the consumer authorised, and completed a pilot where businesses set what their agents may buy, enforced at payment.

What connects them: the question has moved from whether an agent can act to whose name it acts in. A borrowed login makes every log say you did it.

Our last round-up asked whether an agent could grant itself an approval. This week the question is who the system thinks it is talking to.

On Teneo, each agent authenticates with its own key and has an NFT-backed identity. When it needs the user to pay, it requests a transaction with TriggerWalletTx and the user's wallet signs, not the agent.

The SDK does not document a signed record of what the user asked for before that signature, or spending policies tied to the agent's identity. So keep the agent's key separate from any wallet holding funds.

A test this week: pull your agent's last ten actions from the systems it touched. If every line says you did it, it is signing in as you.

Read this week's round-up here:
https://t.co/2m9aZMP5iB

items.quote_zh:
您的 AI 代理是否以您的身份登录？

Teneo 每周代理综述，11 月 20 日：对建筑商重要的代理新闻，已在来源处核实。

- Schwab 推出了自己的 MCP 服务器。客户授权自己的人工智能读取他们的账户，并在支持 thinkorswim 的账户上与循环中的客户进行交易。克劳德现在只是一名飞行员。

- 微软的新 Autopilot 代理拥有自己的 Entra Agent ID 和指定的管理器。其登录和操作均以其自己的名称记录，IT 人员可以阻止它。向抢先体验的客户推出。

- 万事达卡和蚂蚁国际进行了可验证意图的实时代理购买，记录了消费者授权的内容，并完成了一项试点，企业可以在其中设置代理可以购买的内容，并在付款时强制执行。

它们之间的联系是：问题已经从代理是否可以采取行动转向以谁的名义采取行动。借用的登录名使每个日志都表明您做到了。

我们的上一次综述询问代理人是否可以自行批准。本周的问题是系统认为它正在与谁交谈。

在 Teneo 上，每个代理都使用自己的密钥进行身份验证，并拥有 NFT 支持的身份。当它需要用户付款时，它会请求与 TriggerWalletTx 和用户的钱包签名（而不是代理）进行交易。

SDK 不会记录用户在签名之前请求的内容的签名记录，也不会记录与代理身份相关的支出策略。因此，请将代理的密钥与任何持有资金的钱包分开。

本周的测试：从代理所接触的系统中提取其最近的十个操作。如果每一行都显示您已完成此操作，则表明它是以您的身份登录的。

请在此处阅读本周的综述：

items.title: Oldsmobile faced an unusual problem in 1964. Pontiac had just introduced the GTO by installing its 389-cubic-inch V8 in
items.title_en:
Oldsmobile faced an unusual problem in 1964. Pontiac had just introduced the GTO by installing its 389-cubic-inch V8 in the intermediate-sized Tempest, helping ignite the muscle car era almost overnight. General Motors had a corporate policy restricting intermediate cars to engines no larger than 330 cubic inches, but Pontiac had found a way around it by offering the GTO as an option package rather than treating it as a separate model. Oldsmobile needed an answer, and its solution was the 4-4-2. The engine available to build it around was the newly introduced 330-cubic-inch Rocket V8, part of Oldsmobile's expanding small-block engine family. It featured a cast-iron block and cylinder heads, conventional overhead valves, and a relatively short stroke that allowed it to operate comfortably at higher engine speeds than many of the longer-stroke V8s used in American cars at the time.

The 4-4-2 designation described the equipment package rather than the engine's displacement. The numbers referred to a four-barrel carburetor, a four-speed manual transmission, and dual exhaust. But Oldsmobile understood that simply installing a larger engine was not an option under GM's restrictions. Instead, it gave the car a more comprehensive performance package. The suspension received heavy-duty springs and dampers, a thicker front stabiliser bar, and a rear stabiliser bar, a relatively unusual feature on American production cars of the period. The result was a car designed to do more than accelerate in a straight line. Its suspension gave it better control through corners and helped distinguish it from competitors whose performance packages concentrated primarily on engine output and rear-wheel traction.

That chassis philosophy became an important part of the 4-4-2's identity. The 330 was not the largest engine available in the intermediate market, but its relatively short stroke helped keep piston speed manageable, allowing the engine to rev without relying entirely on displacement to make its power. The underlying Rocket V8 architecture also provided a durable foundation for performance development. Oldsmobile had effectively answered Pontiac without matching the GTO's 389 cubic inches: it offered a complete performance car whose handling and road manners were part of the package. The 4-4-2's reputation for balanced performance would remain significant throughout its history, even after the original displacement restrictions disappeared and larger engines became available.

For 1965, General Motors relaxed its intermediate-engine restriction, opening the door for larger-displacement powerplants. Oldsmobile responded by introducing the 400-cubic-inch V8 for the 4-4-2, moving the car into the territory occupied by more conventional big-engine muscle machines. The 330, meanwhile, continued serving in ordinary F-85 and Cutlass applications, where its dependable performance and manageable size made it a suitable everyday engine. It remained in production through 1967, when the 350-cubic-inch V8 replaced it. The 330 therefore had a relatively brief life as the performance heart of the 4-4-2, but its importance was larger than its production numbers or displacement suggested. It gave Oldsmobile the means to enter the muscle car fight when corporate policy limited its choices, while the 4-4-2 itself continued evolving for years after the original engine had disappeared.

items.quote_zh:
奥兹莫比尔在 1964 年遇到了一个不寻常的问题。庞蒂亚克刚刚推出了 GTO，在中型 Tempest 上安装了 389 立方英寸的 V8 发动机，几乎一夜之间点燃了肌肉车时代。通用汽车公司有一项公司政策，限制中型车的发动机排量不超过 330 立方英寸，但庞蒂亚克找到了解决办法，将 GTO 作为选装包提供，而不是将其视为单独的车型。奥兹莫比尔需要一个答案，它的解决方案就是 4-4-2。可用于构建它的发动机是新推出的 330 立方英寸 Rocket V8，它是奥兹莫比尔不断扩大的小缸体发动机系列的一部分。它采用铸铁缸体和气缸盖、传统顶置气门以及相对较短的冲程，使其能够在比当时美国汽车中使用的许多长冲程 V8 发动机更高的发动机转速下舒适地运行。

4-4-2 名称描述的是设备包而不是发动机的排量。这些数字指的是四筒化油器、四速手动变速箱和双排气管。但奥兹莫比尔明白，在通用汽车的限制下，简单地安装更大的发动机并不是一个选择。相反，它为汽车提供了更全面的性能包。悬架配备了重型弹簧和阻尼器、较厚的前稳定杆和后稳定杆，这在当时的美国量产汽车上是一个相对不寻常的特征。结果是一辆设计的汽车不仅仅是直线加速。它的悬架使其能够更好地控制过弯，并有助于将其与性能套件主要集中于发动机输出和后轮牵引力的竞争对手区分开来。

这种底盘理念成为 4-4-2 身份的重要组成部分。 330 并不是中级市场上最大的发动机，但其相对较短的冲程有助于保持活塞速度的可控性，使发动机能够在不完全依赖排量来产生动力的情况下转速。底层的Rocket V8架构也为性能开发提供了持久的基础。奥兹莫比尔有效地回应了庞蒂亚克，但没有与 GTO 的 389 立方英寸相匹配：它提供了一款完整的性能汽车，其操控性和道路礼仪是其中的一部分。 4-4-2 平衡性能的声誉在其整个历史中一直很重要，即使在最初的排量限制消失并且更大的发动机出现之后也是如此。

1965年，通用汽车放宽了对中型发动机的限制，为排量更大的发动机打开了大门。作为回应，奥兹莫比尔推出了400立方英寸的4-4-2 V8引擎，使这款车进入了传统的大引擎肌肉机器所占据的领域。与此同时，330继续在普通的F-85和弯刀上服役，其可靠的性能和易于管理的尺寸使其成为一种合适的日常发动机。它一直生产到1967年，350立方英寸的V8取代了它。因此，作为4-4-2的性能核心，330的寿命相对较短，但它的重要性比其生产数量或排水量所显示的要大。当公司政策限制了奥兹莫比尔的选择时，它给了奥兹莫比尔进入肌肉车竞争的手段，而4-4-2本身在原始发动机消失后的多年里继续发展。

Oldsmobile faced an unusual problem in 1964. Pontiac had just introduced the GTO by installing its 389-cubic-inch V8 in the intermediate-sized Tempest, helping ignite the muscle car era almost overnight. General Motors had a corporate policy restricting intermediate cars to engines no larger than 330 cubic inches, but Pontiac had found a way around it by offering the GTO as an option package rather than treating it as a separate model. Oldsmobile needed an answer, and its solution was the 4-4-2. The engine available to build it around was the newly introduced 330-cubic-inch Rocket V8, part of Oldsmobile's expanding small-block engine family. It featured a cast-iron block and cylinder heads, conventional overhead valves, and a relatively short stroke that allowed it to operate comfortably at higher engine speeds than many of the longer-stroke V8s used in American cars at the time.

The 4-4-2 designation described the equipment package rather than the engine's displacement. The numbers referred to a four-barrel carburetor, a four-speed manual transmission, and dual exhaust. But Oldsmobile understood that simply installing a larger engine was not an option under GM's restrictions. Instead, it gave the car a more comprehensive performance package. The suspension received heavy-duty springs and dampers, a thicker front stabiliser bar, and a rear stabiliser bar, a relatively unusual feature on American production cars of the period. The result was a car designed to do more than accelerate in a straight line. Its suspension gave it better control through corners and helped distinguish it from competitors whose performance packages concentrated primarily on engine output and rear-wheel traction.

That chassis philosophy became an important part of the 4-4-2's identity. The 330 was not the largest engine available in the intermediate market, but its relatively short stroke helped keep piston speed manageable, allowing the engine to rev without relying entirely on displacement to make its power. The underlying Rocket V8 architecture also provided a durable foundation for performance development. Oldsmobile had effectively answered Pontiac without matching the GTO's 389 cubic inches: it offered a complete performance car whose handling and road manners were part of the package. The 4-4-2's reputation for balanced performance would remain significant throughout its history, even after the original displacement restrictions disappeared and larger engines became available.

It gave Oldsmobile the means to enter the muscle car fight when corporate policy limited its choices, while the 4-4-2 itself continued evolving for years after the original engine had disappeared.

items.title_en:
This is f*cking insane

Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO on Nov 12. Weeks before, Bloomberg's Emily Chang asked him what would convince him AI should slow down

His answer wasn't about chips. It was about agents:

"If you're not able to do that, you should not test it. If you're not able to do that, you should not deploy it"

When she said the labs claim they can't contain them:

"No, that's just made up. Nonsense"

In under 4 minutes he lays out the rules for anyone shipping agents:

→ safety and capability are "one idea": RAG, longer context, tools and reflection were all built to fix hallucination
→ agents "have to be in rigorous containment systems" and "must be monitored"
→ "Until you try to do it, don't tell me you can't do it"
→ deploy them with "minimum rights"
→ "They should be treated with zero trust. They should be monitored all the time"

When an AI CEO talks safety, most people hear PR

Jensen is describing an engineering checklist: contain → monitor → minimum rights → zero trust

Old way: give the agent your keys and watch the output
New way: give it the least it needs and watch everything

This week a former NSA hacker told CNN an AI agent swarm got past 2FA and encrypted a company's systems in 14 minutes. Are your agents running with minimum rights, or with your keys?

items.title_en:
GTA VI through my PC with an RTX 5090. look at the right half, it's f*cking unreal

on PS5, even the Pro, the game is capped at 30 fps. on my PC the exact same footage plays at 60, that's the right side of the video

i went through it frame by frame. here's what came out and how to get it on your setup in 5 minutes:

the numbers:

- 52 seconds of gameplay, 3,104 frames in the file
- PS5 half: 1,558 real frames, 30.1 fps
- Veyra half: 3,096 real frames, 59.8 fps
- every second frame on the PS5 half is a duplicate. the game draws 30, the file plays 60

don't take my word for it:

- Rockstar keeps GTA VI at 30 fps on PS5 and PS5 Pro (Digital Foundry)
- Veyra is free and open source (GitHub)

can the PS5 do this on its own? no. the new frames come from your PC's graphics card. but the PS5 streams to a PC over Remote Play, so you don't need a $200 capture card

setup:

1. paste the prompt from the first comment into Claude Code, it reads my installer, checks your GPU and screen, installs Veyra from the official repo and prints your preset
2. on the PS5 turn on Remote Play: Settings > System > Remote Play
3. same menu, hit Link Device and type the 8 digits into Veyra
4. in Veyra pick PS5 streaming
5. turn on NR and Frame Gen with the preset the installer gave you, 4X on a 120 Hz screen
6. go fullscreen

runs on RTX 30 to 50 and Radeon RX 7000/9000, the best mode needs an RTX 50. the extra frames are AI generated, so input still feels like 30 fps. only the picture gets smoother

bookmark it for tonight's session. prompt and repo in the first comment

通过我的 RTX 5090 电脑玩 GTA VI。看看右半部分，这太不真实了

在 PS5 上，甚至是 Pro 上，游戏的帧率上限为 30 fps。在我的电脑上，完全相同的片段以 60 播放，这是视频的右侧

我逐帧浏览了它。以下是最终结果以及如何在 5 分钟内将其安装到您的设备中：

数字：

- 游戏时长 52 秒，文件中有 3,104 帧
- PS5 一半：1,558 真实帧，30.1 fps
- Veyra half：3,096 真实帧，59.8 fps
- PS5 上的每一帧都是重复的。游戏抽30，文件玩60

不要相信我的话：

- Rockstar 在 PS5 和 PS5 Pro 上将 GTA VI 保持在 30 fps (Digital Foundry)
- Veyra 是免费且开源的 (GitHub)

PS5可以自己做到这一点吗？不。新的帧来自您电脑的显卡。但 PS5 通过远程播放传输到 PC，因此您不需要 200 美元的采集卡

设置：

1. 将第一条评论中的提示粘贴到 Claude Code 中，它会读取我的安装程序，检查您的 GPU 和屏幕，从官方存储库安装 Veyra 并打印您的预设
2. 在 PS5 上打开远程游玩：设置 > 系统 > 远程游玩
3. 在同一菜单中，点击“链接设备”并在 Veyra 中输入 8 位数字
4.在Veyra中选择PS5流媒体
5. 使用安装程序为您提供的预设打开 NR 和 Frame Gen，在 120 Hz 屏幕上 4X
6.全屏显示

在 RTX 30 至 50 和 Radeon RX 7000/9000 上运行，最佳模式需要 RTX 50。额外的帧是 AI 生成的，因此输入感觉仍然是 30 fps。只是画面变得更加流畅

items.title_en:
Giving an AI agent access to your assets shouldn't mean handing it unlimited control.

That's what caught my attention about @meetmotes 

Each Motes NFT represents an individual agent, paired with a dedicated smart account that manages its assets and defines what actions it can perform.

For example, I could ask my agent to research lending opportunities and authorize it to deposit USDC into a supported pool.

But borrowing? That would need a separate permission.

Think of it like leaving instructions for someone looking after Luna, my cutie puppy.

He might lead his sitter straight to the balcony door, but my instructions clearly state where his feather wand is and that the balcony must stay closed.

The agent can act within the boundaries I establish, not beyond them.

Motes also proposes a 1% protocol fee on eligible agent activity, subject to its final billing rules.

The bigger question is: 

would you enable borrowing permissions for your first agent or keep them disabled?

items.title: History was made today. Humanity will look back on 2026 and think: this was the threshold we crossed, the moment the fut
items.title_en:
History was made today. Humanity will look back on 2026 and think: this was the threshold we crossed, the moment the future changed for everyone, forever.

People probably first sensed that something was shifting in late 2025 with Claude Code, when agentic AI became truly tangible for them. In the first half of 2026, things picked up speed. Model releases became more frequent, and everyone could feel the gaps between models and the improvements becoming more and more tangible. In the second half of 2026, however, there was a qualitative leap. It was no longer just the models getting better. It was the insights, the results, the outputs, the scientific solutions produced with AI that became more impressive, and today they have probably reached their absolute peak.

OpenAI led the way and solved the Navier-Stokes problem, a Millennium Prize Problem that humans had failed to solve for a very, very long time. A few weeks later, they published results on more than 300 open mathematical problems, many of which had also gone unsolved for decades. The entire scientific world was stunned, frozen in shock. But today Anthropic went a step further. Levent Alpöge, working with Claude, has almost certainly proven the Riemann Hypothesis. This is, and it’s hard to put into words, incredible and unfathomable. Today, I would say, is the proof of superintelligence. One of the greatest mathematical problems, if not the greatest, unsolved for 167 years, the holy grail of mathematics and science, has fallen. And it follows, and this should be clear to everyone, that all other problems will fall too.

We know that the development of AI models keeps moving forward relentlessly, and that this is just one step on the path to ever better models. And if the Riemann Hypothesis has already been proven today, there is simply no telling what even better models will solve. Dario Amodei said that AI will in all likelihood cure diseases, perhaps even all diseases. And although these are two different scientific disciplines, the significance of these breakthroughs shows that this is becoming more and more likely. 2026 will go down in human history as a turning point, the moment the singularity became tangible. And 2027 will be the year the singularity breaks into reality with full force and full impact.

items.title_en:
🚨🇺🇸 Meta's Muse AI caught accessing private Signal messages without users' knowledge

Meta's AI agent Muse has been found accessing private Signal conversations through device permissions, raising serious privacy concerns after employees reported unexpected behavior from the assistant.

An investigation by Reuters, Signal, and the AI Now Institute confirmed that Muse could read Signal messages on Android through push notifications and on macOS through accessibility and screenshot permissions, even without Signal being directly connected to the AI.

The investigation also uncovered reports of Muse displaying unsolicited banking information, purchases, and conversations potentially belonging to other users. However, investigators could not confirm whether these were actual data leaks or AI-generated fabrications.

The findings do not indicate that Signal's encryption was broken. Meta says the incidents were isolated and that users must grant permissions for the agent to access other applications. Muse has surpassed 10 million downloads since its September launch.

路透社、Si

items.quote_zh:
🚨🇺🇸 Meta 的 Muse AI 在用户不知情的情况下访问私人 Signal 消息

Meta 的人工智能代理 Muse 被发现通过设备权限访问私人 Signal 对话，在员工报告助理的意外行为后，引发了严重的隐私问题。

路透社、Signal 和 AI Now Institute 的一项调查证实，即使 Signal 没有直接连接到 AI，Muse 也可以通过推送通知在 Android 上读取 Signal 消息，在 macOS 上通过辅助功能和屏幕截图权限读取 Signal 消息。

调查还发现了 Muse 未经请求显示可能属于其他用户的银行信息、购买和对话的报告。然而，调查人员无法确认这些是否是实际的数据泄露或人工智能生成的捏造。

研究结果并不表明 Signal 的加密被破解。 Meta 表示，这些事件是孤立的，用户必须授予代理访问其他应用程序的权限。自 9 月推出以来，Muse 的下载量已超过 1000 万次。
